Use :func:`get_magnetic_symmetry` for magnetic symmetry search.  Parameters ---------- cell : tuple Crystal structure given in tuple. It has to follow the following form, (basis vectors, atomic points, types in integer numbers, ...)  - basis vectors : array_like shape=(3, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  .. code-block:: python  [[a_x, a_y, a_z], [b_x, b_y, b_z], [c_x, c_y, c_z]]  - atomic points : array_like shape=(num_atom, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  Atomic position vectors with respect to basis vectors, i.e., given in fractional coordinates. - types : array_like shape=(num_atom, ), dtype='intc'  Integer numbers to distinguish species. - optional data : case-I: Scalar shape=(num_atom, ), dtype='double'  Each atomic site has a scalar value. With is_magnetic=True, values are included in the symmetry search in a way of collinear magnetic moments. case-II: Vectors shape=(num_atom, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  Each atomic site has a vector. With is_magnetic=True, vectors are included in the symmetry search in a way of non-collinear magnetic moments. symprec : float Symmetry search tolerance in the unit of length. angle_tolerance : float Symmetry search tolerance in the unit of angle deg. Normally it is not recommended to use this argument. See a bit more detail at :ref:`variables_angle_tolerance`. If the value is negative, an internally optimized routine is used to judge symmetry. mag_symprec : float Tolerance for magnetic symmetry search in the unit of magnetic moments. If not specified, use the same value as symprec. is_magnetic : bool When optional data (4th element of cell tuple) is given in case-II, the symmetry search is performed considering magnetic symmetry, which may be corresponding to that for non-collinear calculation. Default is True, but this does nothing unless optional data is supplied.  Returns ------- symmetry: dict Rotation parts and translation parts of symmetry operations are represented with respect to basis vectors. When the search failed, :code:`None` is returned.  - 'rotations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3, 3), order='C', dtype='intc'  Rotation (matrix) parts of symmetry operations - 'translations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3), dtype='double'  Translation (vector) parts of symmetry operations - 'time_reversals': ndarray (exists when the optional data is given) shape=(num_operations, ), dtype='bool\_'  Time reversal part of magnetic symmetry operations. True indicates time reversal operation, and False indicates an ordinary operation. - 'equivalent_atoms' : ndarray shape=(num_atoms, ), dtype='intc'  A mapping table of atoms to symmetrically independent atoms. This is used to find symmetrically equivalent atoms. The numbers contained are the indices of atoms starting from 0, i.e., the first atom is numbered as 0, and then 1, 2, 3, ... :code:`np.unique(equivalent_atoms)` gives representative symmetrically independent atoms. A list of atoms that are symmetrically equivalent to some independent atom (here for example 1 is in :code:`equivalent_atom`) is found by :code:`np.where(equivalent_atom=1)[0]`.  Notes ----- The orders of the rotation matrices and the translation vectors correspond with each other, e.g. , the second symmetry operation is organized by the set of the second rotation matrix and second translation vector in the respective arrays. Therefore a set of symmetry operations may obtained by  .. code-block:: python  [(r, t) for r, t in zip(dataset['rotations'], dataset['translations'])]  The operations are given with respect to the fractional coordinates (not for Cartesian coordinates). The rotation matrix and translation vector are used as follows:  .. code-block::  new_vector[3x1] = rotation[3x3] * vector[3x1] + translation[3x1]  The three values in the vector are given for the a, b, and c axes, respectively.

场景要求：触发: 实验或数据库结构带反铁磁/非共线磁序，准备从标准化晶胞建立自旋DFT输入或从收敛态重启
对象：晶格和原子坐标、元素/位点映射、逐位点磁矩、普通空间群结果、DFT磁性设置
目标：区分核结构空间群与磁性空间群，保证交付晶胞和磁矩序列保留目标磁序，或暂停交付复核
输入：原始结构、逐原子共线/非共线磁矩、磁胞、spglib磁性数据集及VASP MAGMOM/重启设置
步骤/决策：先保留原始晶格、位点顺序、磁矩方向及其坐标约定；分别计算普通和带磁矩的对称性。对标准化/换轴后的位点、磁矩和时间反演映射逐项核对，非共线磁矩需按新旧坐标约定处理方向；若磁胞缩减使反向磁矩位点合并或磁序无法映射，则保留原磁胞并转人工复核。交付DFT输入时记录MAGMOM、ISYM及重启文件状态，不把初始磁矩当收敛磁序证据。
验收：元素、位点和磁矩一一回链原输入；普通/磁性空间群、时间反演、设置变换及非共线磁矩坐标约定有记录；目标磁序无法映射时阻断；VASP重启保留预期对称性设置且实际磁态需由求解结果另验。

environment.description:
触发: 实验结构/反射数据使用非标准设置或不同轴选择，计算团队将结构标准化后要对照hkl/反射强度
对象：原始晶胞和空间群设置、hkl反射表、标准化晶胞、变换矩阵和原点平移
目标：交付与标准化结构同一设置的反射索引或明确无法安全变换的记录，防止错配峰位/晶面
输入：CIF或结构文件、反射hkl/强度、spglib setting transform、Gemmi reindex operator、原/目标晶胞和空间群
步骤/决策：保存原结构设置、晶胞、空间群、反射hkl/强度及版本；读取spglib设置变换与原点偏移，核对新旧实空间基矢的方向和轴顺序，再据倒易基矢关系构造Gemmi重索引算符，不直接将spglib矩阵传给Gemmi。先用代表反射验证hkl映射、空间群、晶胞和d间距一致；若比较复数结构因子，还须单独核对原点平移引起的相位约定。缺原轴定义、变换不可逆或对照不一致时暂停交接并请求实验端补全。
验收：每个新hkl可回链原hkl、算符方向、轴约定及同一版本的晶胞/空间群；代表反射d间距和等价关系按项目规格保持；涉及结构因子相位时原点偏移单独验证；缺元数据或校验失败不得把实验反射与计算结构强行对应。

When the search failed, :code:`None` is returned. - 'rotations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3, 3), order='C', dtype='intc' Rotation (matrix) parts of symmetry operations - 'translations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3), dtype='double' Translation (vector) parts of symmetry operations - 'time_reversals': ndarray (exists when the optional data is given) shape=(num_operations, ), dtype='bool\_' Time reversal part of magnetic symmetry operations. True indicates time reversal operation, and False indicates an ordinary operation. - 'equivalent_atoms' : ndarray shape=(num_atoms, ), dtype='intc' A mapping table of atoms to symmetrically independent atoms. This is used to find symmetrically equivalent atoms. The numbers contained are the indices of atoms starting from 0, i.e., the first atom is numbered as 0, and then 1, 2, 3, ... :code:`np.unique(equivalent_atoms)` gives representative symmetrically independent atoms. A list of atoms that are symmetrically equivalent to some independent atom (here for example 1 is in :code:`equivalent_atom`) is found by :code:`np.where(equivalent_atom=1)[0]`.

init_ref_tools.ori_description: Find symmetry operations from a crystal structure and site tensors.  .. warning:: :func:`get_symmetry` with ``is_magnetic=True`` is deprecated at version 2.0.  Use :func:`get_magnetic_symmetry` for magnetic symmetry search.  Parameters ---------- cell : tuple Crystal structure given in tuple. It has to follow the following form, (basis vectors, atomic points, types in integer numbers, ...)  - basis vectors : array_like shape=(3, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  .. code-block:: python  [[a_x, a_y, a_z], [b_x, b_y, b_z], [c_x, c_y, c_z]]  - atomic points : array_like shape=(num_atom, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  Atomic position vectors with respect to basis vectors, i.e., given in fractional coordinates. - types : array_like shape=(num_atom, ), dtype='intc'  Integer numbers to distinguish species. - optional data : case-I: Scalar shape=(num_atom, ), dtype='double'  Each atomic site has a scalar value. With is_magnetic=True, values are included in the symmetry search in a way of collinear magnetic moments. case-II: Vectors shape=(num_atom, 3), order='C', dtype='double'  Each atomic site has a vector. With is_magnetic=True, vectors are included in the symmetry search in a way of non-collinear magnetic moments. symprec : float Symmetry search tolerance in the unit of length. angle_tolerance : float Symmetry search tolerance in the unit of angle deg. Normally it is not recommended to use this argument. See a bit more detail at :ref:`variables_angle_tolerance`. If the value is negative, an internally optimized routine is used to judge symmetry. mag_symprec : float Tolerance for magnetic symmetry search in the unit of magnetic moments. If not specified, use the same value as symprec. is_magnetic : bool When optional data (4th element of cell tuple) is given in case-II, the symmetry search is performed considering magnetic symmetry, which may be corresponding to that for non-collinear calculation. Default is True, but this does nothing unless optional data is supplied.  Returns ------- symmetry: dict Rotation parts and translation parts of symmetry operations are represented with respect to basis vectors. When the search failed, :code:`None` is returned.  - 'rotations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3, 3), order='C', dtype='intc'  Rotation (matrix) parts of symmetry operations - 'translations' : ndarray shape=(num_operations, 3), dtype='double'  Translation (vector) parts of symmetry operations - 'time_reversals': ndarray (exists when the optional data is given) shape=(num_operations, ), dtype='bool\_'  Time reversal part of magnetic symmetry operations. True indicates time reversal operation, and False indicates an ordinary operation. - 'equivalent_atoms' : ndarray shape=(num_atoms, ), dtype='intc'  A mapping table of atoms to symmetrically independent atoms. This is used to find symmetrically equivalent atoms. The numbers contained are the indices of atoms starting from 0, i.e., the first atom is numbered as 0, and then 1, 2, 3, ... :code:`np.unique(equivalent_atoms)` gives representative symmetrically independent atoms. A list of atoms that are symmetrically equivalent to some independent atom (here for example 1 is in :code:`equivalent_atom`) is found by :code:`np.where(equivalent_atom=1)[0]`.  Notes ----- The orders of the rotation matrices and the translation vectors correspond with each other, e.g. , the second symmetry operation is organized by the set of the second rotation matrix and second translation vector in the respective arrays. Therefore a set of symmetry operations may obtained by  .. code-block:: python  [(r, t) for r, t in zip(dataset['rotations'], dataset['translations'])]  The operations are given with respect to the fractional coordinates (not for Cartesian coordinates). The rotation matrix and translation vector are used as follows:  .. code-block::  new_vector[3x1] = rotation[3x3] * vector[3x1] + translation[3x1]  The three values in the vector are given for the a, b, and c axes, respectively.

对象：原始晶胞和空间群设置、hkl反射表、标准化晶胞、变换矩阵和原点平移

IStructure is made to be (somewhat) immutable so that they can function as keys in a dict. To make modifications, use the standard Structure object instead. init_ref_tools.description: Search symmetry dataset from an input cell.

cell.description: See :func:`get_symmetry`.

hall_number.description: If a serial number of Hall symbol (>0) is given, the database corresponding to the Hall symbol is made.  The mapping from Hall symbols to a space-group-type is the many-to-one mapping. init_ref_tools.name: get_path
init_ref_tools.description: Return the kpoint path information for band structure given a crystal structure, using the paths from the chosen recipe/reference.  If you use this module, please cite the paper of the corresponding recipe (see parameter below).

structure.description: The crystal structure for which we want to obtain the suggested path. It should be a tuple in the format accepted by spglib: ``(cell, positions, numbers)``, where (if N is the number of atoms): - ``cell`` is a :math:`3 \times 3` list of floats (``cell[0]`` is the first lattice vector, ...) - ``positions`` is a :math:`N \times 3` list of floats with the atomic coordinates in scaled coordinates (i.e., w.r.t. the cell vectors) - ``numbers`` is a length-:math:`N` list with integers identifying uniquely the atoms in the cell (e.g., the Z number of the atom, but any other positive non-zero integer will work - e.g. if you want to distinguish two Carbon atoms, you can set one number to 6 and the other to 1006)

with_time_reversal.description: if False, and the group has no inversion symmetry, additional lines are returned as described in the HPKOT paper.

recipe.description: choose the reference publication that defines the special points and paths. Currently, the following value is implemented: - ``hpkot``: HPKOT paper: Y. Hinuma, G. Pizzi, Y. Kumagai, F. Oba, I. Tanaka, Band structure diagram paths based on crystallography, Comp. Mat. Sci. 128, 140 (2017). DOI: 10.1016/j.commatsci.2016.10.015

threshold.description: the threshold to use to verify if we are in and edge case (e.g., a tetragonal cell, but ``a==c``). For instance, in the tI lattice, if ``abs(a-c) < threshold``, a :py:exc:`~seekpath.hpkot.EdgeCaseWarning` is issued. Note that depending on the bravais lattice, the meaning of the threshold is different (angle, length, ...)

symprec.description: the symmetry precision used internally by SPGLIB

angle_tolerance.description: the angle_tolerance used internally by SPGLIB

return.type: a dictionary with the following keys
return.description: - ``point_coords``: a dictionary with label -> float coordinates - ``path``: a list of length-2 tuples, with the labels of the starting and ending point of each label section - ``has_inversion_symmetry``: True or False, depending on whether the input crystal structure has inversion symmetry or not. - ``augmented_path``: if True, it means that the path was augmented with the :math:`-k` points (this happens if both has_inversion_symmetry is False, and the user set with_time_reversal=False in the input) - ``bravais_lattice``: the Bravais lattice string (like ``cP``, ``tI``, ...) - ``bravais_lattice_extended``: the specific case used to define labels and coordinates (like ``cP1``, ``tI2``, ...) - ``cont_lattice``: three real-space vectors for the crystallographic conventional cell (``conv_lattice[0,:]`` is the first vector) - ``conv_positions``: fractional coordinates of atoms in the crystallographic conventional cell - ``conv_types``: list of integer types of the atoms in the crystallographic conventional cell (typically, the atomic numbers) - ``primitive_lattice``: three real-space vectors for the crystallographic primitive cell (``primitive_lattice[0,:]`` is the first vector) - ``primitive_positions``: fractional coordinates of atoms in the crystallographic primitive cell - ``primitive_types``: list of integer types of the atoms in the crystallographic primitive cell (typically, the atomic numbers) - ``reciprocal_primitive_lattice``: reciprocal-cell vectors for the primitive cell (vectors are rows: ``reciprocal_primitive_lattice[0,:]`` is the first vector) - ``primitive_transformation_matrix``: the transformation matrix :math:`P` between the conventional and the primitive cell - ``inverse_primitive_transformation_matrix``: the inverse of the matrix :math:`P` (the determinant is integer and gives the ratio in volume between the conventional and primitive cells) - ``volume_original_wrt_conv``: volume ratio of the user-provided cell with respect to the the crystallographic conventional cell - ``volume_original_wrt_prim``: volume ratio of the user-provided cell with respect to the the crystalloraphic primitive cell :note: An :py:exc:`~seekpath.hpkot.EdgeCaseWarning` is issued for edge cases (e.g. if ``a==b==c`` for orthorhombic systems). In this case, still one of the valid cases is picked.

basic_info.name: QE计算中断后checkpoint重启资格与结果谱系交接

environment.description:
触发: QE的结构优化或MD长作业达到墙时限/请求停止，工作流拟从已有保存状态恢复并交付能量、力或轨迹
对象：旧作业输入和退出原因、checkpoint/outdir、prefix、并行配置、AiiDA子进程/工作流节点与目标输出
目标：判定可原位续算、必须从头重算或需人工调查，并确保交接结果不混入不相容旧状态
输入：旧新input与代码版本、restart_mode/max_seconds或prefix.EXIT记录、处理器与并行分解、checkpoint文件清单、AiiDA exit code/handler及call/input/create/return链接、目标结果完整性规则
步骤/决策：先核QE旧作业的清洁中断证据、prefix/outdir和可读checkpoint，以及新旧处理器数量/并行分解和输入版本是否满足同一计算的restart约束；任一条件缺失则不设置restart_mode='restart'，转从头重算或人工调查。单独核AiiDA失败子进程的exit code与已配置handler：WorkChain重提交只说明工作流重试，不证明PWscf已读旧checkpoint。满足QE条件时才以有版本记录的输入启动续算，MD按nstep重启语义核实际新增步数；保留旧/新CalcJob及工作流链接，完成后核终态、能量/力/轨迹完整性和必要物理一致性，再交下游。
验收：每个续算声明有QE清洁中断、同prefix/outdir、有效checkpoint、同处理器及并行分解的证据，并有运行日志证明恢复而非仅AiiDA重提交；MD实际步数按nstep语义核对；交接输出绑定旧新作业节点、版本和完整终态，数值验收按项目规格。缺checkpoint恢复日志、结果或谱系则HOLD。

environment.description:
触发: 高通量批次的部分材料仅完成结构/SCF或只有DOS、只有band结果，作业队列显示混合成功和失败
对象：批次材料清单、每材料的多阶段工作流图/JobStore任务、阶段输出、退出状态与目标属性入库合同
目标：避免把批内部分完成误写成整条材料计算成功，决定可保存的局部结果、应补跑的阶段和不可入库的记录
输入：材料与批次ID、各阶段任务ID及父子依赖、stdout/stderr/退出状态、结构与SCF/DOS/band输出、目标属性必需阶段和数据库schema版本
步骤/决策：按材料建立预期阶段清单，区分成功、有输出但下游未完成、失败和未提交；检查下游结果是否由相应上游结构/SCF产生；对缺少必需阶段的材料列定向补跑计划，并保留原失败节点；对schema允许的部分数据只标记该属性可用，不把整个材料记录标为完整；缺少任务来源或无法确认上游依赖时隔离待查；补跑后重新按合同验收而非仅看批次总成功率
验收：每项可发布属性关联必需阶段task ID和上游依赖；请求未返回字段与真实缺算分开；只有DOS或只有band时按schema只发布已有属性；批内失败不被总成功率掩盖；补跑后保留旧新节点和最终验收

init_ref_tools.name: Custodian
init_ref_tools.description: Custodian class is the manager for a list of jobs given a list of error handlers.  The way it works is as follows:  1. Let's say you have defined a list of jobs as [job1, job2, job3, ...] and you have defined a list of possible error handlers as [err1, err2, ...] 2. Custodian will run the jobs in the order of job1, job2, ... During each job, custodian will monitor for errors using the handlers that have is_monitor == True. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun. 3. At the end of each individual job, Custodian will run through the list of error handlers that have is_monitor == False. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun.  .. attribute: max_errors  Maximum number of errors allowed.  .. attribute: handlers  All error handlers (including monitors). All error handlers are used to check for errors at the end of a run.  .. attribute: monitors  Error handlers that are Monitors, i.e., handlers that monitors a job as it is being run.  .. attribute: polling_time_step  The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion.  .. attribute: monitor_freq  The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialize a Custodian from a list of jobs and error handlers.

handlers.description: Error handlers. In order of priority of fixing.

jobs.description: Sequence of Jobs to be run. Note that this can be any sequence or even a generator yielding jobs.

max_errors_per_job.description: Maximum number of errors per job allowed before exiting. Defaults to None, which means it is set to be equal to max_errors..

max_errors.description: Maximum number of total errors allowed before exiting. Defaults to 1.

polling_time_step.description: The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion. Defaults to 10 secs.

monitor_freq.description: The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

skip_over_errors.description: If set to True, custodian will skip over error handlers that failed (raised an Exception of some sort). Otherwise, custodian will simply exit on unrecoverable errors. The former will lead to potentially more robust performance, but may make it difficult to improve handlers. The latter will allow one to catch potentially bad error handler implementations. Defaults to False.

scratch_dir.description: If this is set, any files in the current directory are copied to a temporary directory in a scratch space first before any jobs are performed, and moved back to the current directory upon completion of all jobs. This is useful in some setups where a scratch partition has much faster IO. To use this, set scratch_dir=root of directory you want to use for runs. There is no need to provide unique directory names; we will use python's tempfile creation mechanisms. A symbolic link is created during the course of the run in the working directory called "scratch_link" as users may want to sometimes check the output during the course of a run. If this is None (the default), the run is performed in the current working directory.

gzipped_output.description: Whether to gzip the final output to save space. Defaults to False.

checkpoint.description: Whether to checkpoint after each successful Job. Checkpoints are stored as custodian.chk.#.tar.gz files. Defaults to False.

terminate_func.description: A function to be called to terminate a running job. If None, the default is to call Popen.terminate.

terminate_on_nonzero_returncode.description: If True, a non-zero return code on any Job will result in a termination. Defaults to True.

directory.description: The directory to run the jobs in. Defaults to the current working directory. If you would like to have the jobs run in a temporary directory, use `scratch_dir` instead.

kwargs.description: Any other kwargs are ignored. This is to allow for easy subclassing and instantiation from a dict.

environment.description:
触发: VASP批处理作业经Custodian错误处理器自动修正后终态成功，纠错日志显示ISMEAR或其他受控输入可能改变
对象：原始作业规格、每次重试的输入和退出记录、custodian.json纠错记录、最终输出以及批次方法合同
目标：判定自动恢复结果可按原方法入库、需独立方法标签/补算，还是因纠错链或验收证据不足暂缓签收
输入：材料/作业ID、初始与最终INCAR/KPOINTS/POTCAR标识、纠错事件与重试顺序、处理器版本、最终vasprun.xml及数值验收规则、批次允许的输入变更清单
步骤/决策：逐任务以ID、初始/最终INCAR、KPOINTS、POTCAR标识和custodian.json重建重试链；区分已批准的运行恢复改动与改变物理/数值方法的改动，并按项目方法合同判原方法可比、独立方法标签/补算或HOLD。最终还须核VASP求解终态和所需属性证据；日志缺失或改动无法解释不因最后一次作业成功而入库。整批暂停仅在项目预定异常率/聚集规则满足时提出。
验收：每个签收结果绑定任务ID、连续纠错事件、初始/最终INCAR/KPOINTS/POTCAR与最终有效输出；ISMEAR等改动是否可与原批合并须由项目物理方法合同判定，不以Custodian自动修复成功即判等价；缺日志、输入差异或必要数值验收保留HOLD。

init_ref_tools.name: Custodian
init_ref_tools.description: Custodian class is the manager for a list of jobs given a list of error handlers.  The way it works is as follows:  1. Let's say you have defined a list of jobs as [job1, job2, job3, ...] and you have defined a list of possible error handlers as [err1, err2, ...] 2. Custodian will run the jobs in the order of job1, job2, ... During each job, custodian will monitor for errors using the handlers that have is_monitor == True. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun. 3. At the end of each individual job, Custodian will run through the list of error handlers that have is_monitor == False. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun.  .. attribute: max_errors  Maximum number of errors allowed.  .. attribute: handlers  All error handlers (including monitors). All error handlers are used to check for errors at the end of a run.  .. attribute: monitors  Error handlers that are Monitors, i.e., handlers that monitors a job as it is being run.  .. attribute: polling_time_step  The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion.  .. attribute: monitor_freq  The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialize a Custodian from a list of jobs and error handlers.

handlers.description: Error handlers. In order of priority of fixing.

jobs.description: Sequence of Jobs to be run. Note that this can be any sequence or even a generator yielding jobs.

max_errors_per_job.description: Maximum number of errors per job allowed before exiting. Defaults to None, which means it is set to be equal to max_errors..

max_errors.description: Maximum number of total errors allowed before exiting. Defaults to 1.

polling_time_step.description: The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion. Defaults to 10 secs.

monitor_freq.description: The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

skip_over_errors.description: If set to True, custodian will skip over error handlers that failed (raised an Exception of some sort). Otherwise, custodian will simply exit on unrecoverable errors. The former will lead to potentially more robust performance, but may make it difficult to improve handlers. The latter will allow one to catch potentially bad error handler implementations. Defaults to False.

scratch_dir.description: If this is set, any files in the current directory are copied to a temporary directory in a scratch space first before any jobs are performed, and moved back to the current directory upon completion of all jobs. This is useful in some setups where a scratch partition has much faster IO. To use this, set scratch_dir=root of directory you want to use for runs. There is no need to provide unique directory names; we will use python's tempfile creation mechanisms. A symbolic link is created during the course of the run in the working directory called "scratch_link" as users may want to sometimes check the output during the course of a run. If this is None (the default), the run is performed in the current working directory.

gzipped_output.description: Whether to gzip the final output to save space. Defaults to False.

checkpoint.description: Whether to checkpoint after each successful Job. Checkpoints are stored as custodian.chk.#.tar.gz files. Defaults to False.

terminate_func.description: A function to be called to terminate a running job. If None, the default is to call Popen.terminate.

terminate_on_nonzero_returncode.description: If True, a non-zero return code on any Job will result in a termination. Defaults to True.

directory.description: The directory to run the jobs in. Defaults to the current working directory. If you would like to have the jobs run in a temporary directory, use `scratch_dir` instead.

kwargs.description: Any other kwargs are ignored. This is to allow for easy subclassing and instantiation from a dict.

init_ref_tools.description: OSZICAR parser for VASP. init_ref_tools.description: Master VaspErrorHandler class that handles a number of common errors that occur during VASP runs.  Args: is_monitor (bool): This class property indicates whether the error handler is a monitor, i.e., a handler that monitors a job as it is running. If a monitor-type handler notices an error, the job will be sent a termination signal, the error is then corrected, and then the job is restarted. This is useful for catching errors that occur early in the run but do not cause immediate failure. num_sites_kpoint_cutoff (int) : The maximum number of atoms in a structure for which increasing the k-point density is permitted as a possible error correction. init_ref_tools.name: Custodian
init_ref_tools.description: Custodian class is the manager for a list of jobs given a list of error handlers.  The way it works is as follows:  1. Let's say you have defined a list of jobs as [job1, job2, job3, ...] and you have defined a list of possible error handlers as [err1, err2, ...] 2. Custodian will run the jobs in the order of job1, job2, ... During each job, custodian will monitor for errors using the handlers that have is_monitor == True. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun. 3. At the end of each individual job, Custodian will run through the list of error handlers that have is_monitor == False. If an error is detected, corrective measures are taken and the particular job is rerun.  .. attribute: max_errors  Maximum number of errors allowed.  .. attribute: handlers  All error handlers (including monitors). All error handlers are used to check for errors at the end of a run.  .. attribute: monitors  Error handlers that are Monitors, i.e., handlers that monitors a job as it is being run.  .. attribute: polling_time_step  The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion.  .. attribute: monitor_freq  The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialize a Custodian from a list of jobs and error handlers.

handlers.description: Error handlers. In order of priority of fixing.

jobs.description: Sequence of Jobs to be run. Note that this can be any sequence or even a generator yielding jobs.

max_errors_per_job.description: Maximum number of errors per job allowed before exiting. Defaults to None, which means it is set to be equal to max_errors..

max_errors.description: Maximum number of total errors allowed before exiting. Defaults to 1.

polling_time_step.description: The length of time in seconds between steps in which a job is checked for completion. Defaults to 10 secs.

monitor_freq.description: The number of polling steps before monitoring occurs. For example, if you have a polling_time_step of 10 seconds and a monitor_freq of 30, this means that Custodian uses the monitors to check for errors every 30 x 10 = 300 seconds, i.e., 5 minutes.

skip_over_errors.description: If set to True, custodian will skip over error handlers that failed (raised an Exception of some sort). Otherwise, custodian will simply exit on unrecoverable errors. The former will lead to potentially more robust performance, but may make it difficult to improve handlers. The latter will allow one to catch potentially bad error handler implementations. Defaults to False.

scratch_dir.description: If this is set, any files in the current directory are copied to a temporary directory in a scratch space first before any jobs are performed, and moved back to the current directory upon completion of all jobs. This is useful in some setups where a scratch partition has much faster IO. To use this, set scratch_dir=root of directory you want to use for runs. There is no need to provide unique directory names; we will use python's tempfile creation mechanisms. A symbolic link is created during the course of the run in the working directory called "scratch_link" as users may want to sometimes check the output during the course of a run. If this is None (the default), the run is performed in the current working directory.

gzipped_output.description: Whether to gzip the final output to save space. Defaults to False.

checkpoint.description: Whether to checkpoint after each successful Job. Checkpoints are stored as custodian.chk.#.tar.gz files. Defaults to False.

terminate_func.description: A function to be called to terminate a running job. If None, the default is to call Popen.terminate.

terminate_on_nonzero_returncode.description: If True, a non-zero return code on any Job will result in a termination. Defaults to True.

directory.description: The directory to run the jobs in. Defaults to the current working directory. If you would like to have the jobs run in a temporary directory, use `scratch_dir` instead.

kwargs.description: Any other kwargs are ignored. This is to allow for easy subclassing and instantiation from a dict.

basic_info.name: 远程材料计算输出缺失时的谱系定位与条件性重提交

environment.description:
触发: 远程DFT作业在AiiDA中未产出预期结果，准备重跑但失败层尚不明确
对象：CalcJob节点及UUID、scheduler状态、远端RemoteData位置、retrieved输出、输入/Code/Computer版本
目标：查明缺失结果发生于调度器、远端文件、取回还是解析环节，只对可重试情形生成带谱系的新作业
输入：AiiDA进程状态与exit code、scheduler日志、remote_folder/retrieved节点、原输入和代码环境、重试策略
步骤/决策：用进程状态和调度器证据先区分walltime/内存终止与程序失败；比对RemoteData引用的远端目录和retrieved文件清单；若远端文件存在但取回/解析失败则先处理传输或解析，不改物理输入；若资源耗尽且输入本身可信，则以get_builder_restart复制并记录受控资源修改后提交；远端目录消失或原因未明时保留未知状态并升级人工复核
验收：每个重试可追溯原CalcJob UUID及具体失败证据；资源/输入修改显式记录；新作业有独立节点，不能覆盖失败节点；无完整输出不宣称计算成功

init_ref_tools.description: Manager singleton for globally loaded resources.  AiiDA can have the following global resources loaded:  1. A single configuration object that contains:  - Global options overrides - The name of a default profile - A mapping of profile names to their configuration and option overrides  2. A single profile object that contains:  - The name of the profile - The UUID of the profile - The configuration of the profile, for connecting to storage and processing resources - The option overrides for the profile  3. A single storage backend object for the profile, to connect to data storage resources 5. A single daemon client object for the profile, to connect to the AiiDA daemon 4. A single communicator object for the profile, to connect to the process control resources 6. A single process controller object for the profile, which uses the communicator to control process tasks 7. A single runner object for the profile, which uses the process controller to start and stop processes 8. A single persister object for the profile, which can persist running processes to the profile storage

目标：查明缺失结果发生于调度器、远端文件、取回还是解析环节，只对可重试情形生成带谱系的新作业
输入：AiiDA进程状态与exit code、scheduler日志、remote_folder/retrieved节点、原输入和代码环境、重试策略
步骤/决策：用进程状态和调度器证据先区分walltime/内存终止与程序失败；比对RemoteData引用的远端目录和retrieved文件清单；若远端文件存在但取回/解析失败则先处理传输或解析，不改物理输入；若资源耗尽且输入本身可信，则以get_builder_restart复制并记录受控资源修改后提交；远端目录消失或原因未明时保留未知状态并升级人工复核
验收：每个重试可追溯原CalcJob UUID及具体失败证据；资源/输入修改显式记录；新作业有独立节点，不能覆盖失败节点；无完整输出不宣称计算成功

输出：失败层定位报告、原/新UUID和输入/资源差异、条件性重提交或人工阻断状态
可复核验收：每个重试可追溯原CalcJob UUID及具体失败证据；资源/输入修改显式记录；新作业有独立节点，不能覆盖失败节点；无完整输出不宣称计算成功

path.description: A list of the vertices to traverse. Leave empty if you plan on using the method :func:`QueryBuilder.append`.

limit.description: Limit the number of rows to this number. Check :func:`QueryBuilder.limit` for more information.

offset.description: Set an offset for the results returned. Details in :func:`QueryBuilder.offset`.

order_by.description: How to order the results. As the 2 above, can be set also at later stage, check :func:`QueryBuilder.order_by` for more information.

project_map.description: A mapping of the projection input-keys to the output-keys of `dict`/`iterdict`

init_ref_tools.name: Node
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for all nodes in AiiDA.  Stores attributes starting with an underscore.  Caches files and attributes before the first save, and saves everything only on store(). After the call to store(), attributes cannot be changed.  Only after storing (or upon loading from uuid) extras can be modified and in this case they are directly set on the db.  In the plugin, also set the _plugin_type_string, to be set in the DB in the 'type' field.

basic_info.name: DFT作业完成但机器可读证据缺损时的结果入库隔离

environment.description:
触发: 批量VASP任务调度状态成功或已产生日志，但交付目录中vasprun.xml无法加载或关键输出文件缺失
对象：任务终态与运行目录、目标属性、VASP输出文件清单、解析或验证器错误及数据库任务文档
目标：阻止缺证据结果被误签收，并区分传输/归档缺损、输出写入失败和真实计算失败后的补救路径
输入：任务ID及终态、运行目录与归档文件大小/时间/校验和、vasprun.xml解析状态、CONTCAR/OSZICAR/OUTCAR存在性、stdout/stderr尾部、原任务文档与目标属性证据合同
步骤/决策：对同一任务ID核对终态和必需产物，运行文件存在性与XML可读性验证；若归档缺损但原始运行目录有完整一致产物，受控补传并重验；若原始产物即不完整，定位I/O或求解失败并补算/重算；若必要证据始终缺失，保留任务失败事实和HOLD状态，不用单一退出码或其他材料输出填补；修复后重新解析、核对任务来源和属性合同再提交入库
验收：按目标属性的项目证据合同核同一任务ID、指定解析器版本、vasprun.xml可载入及必要VASP文件；原始/归档补传须保留校验和及重新解析结果。仅文件存在和XML可载入不证明电子/离子收敛、数值物理合理或属性计算成功，仍需独立结果验收；原始证据不可恢复则HOLD。

environment.description:

对象：旧新插件版本/提交、工作流定义、AiiDA provenance图、缓存节点及历史输出摘要

basic_info.name: 同一材料EOS任务的跨求解器基准一致性验收

environment.description:
触发: 研发组拟用第二个DFT求解器复算既有材料EOS基准或将两代码结果合并到同一数据集
对象：同一材料结构与体积变形集合、两个求解器的输入/输出、赝势或基组、泛函及运行记录
目标：证明两代码在规定方法层级上的EOS结果可比较，或明确记录方法差异和不可合并状态
输入：结构/体积网格、代码和版本、泛函、赝势/基组标识、k点/截断收敛记录、各体积总能与拟合配置
步骤/决策：先锁定化学组成、晶体结构、泛函和体积网格；逐代码保存赝势/基组和数值收敛证据；在相同体积点拟合EOS并比较能量曲线形状、平衡体积和体模量；若数值设置未收敛或方法层级不同则隔离，不把偏差归为代码误差；只有经项目容差和适用材料集合验收后才允许合并
验收：每个体积点可追溯结构、代码/版本、势或基组及数值收敛记录；共同体积网格完整，拟合残差和EOS派生量差异可重算。仅按项目批准的材料集、方法层级和容差判断可合并；缺任一条件则待判。

Examples -------- >>> from ase.build import bulk >>> from ase.calculators.emt import EMT >>> from pyiron_workflow_atomistics.engine import ASEEngine, CalcInputMinimize, calculate >>> engine = ASEEngine( ... EngineInput=CalcInputMinimize(force_convergence_tolerance=0.05), ... calculator=EMT(), ... working_directory="./_demo", ... ) >>> out = calculate(bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=3.6, cubic=True), engine) # doctest: +SKIP

init_ref_tools.name: Atoms
init_ref_tools.description: Atoms object.  The Atoms object can represent an isolated molecule, or a periodically repeated structure. It has a unit cell and there may be periodic boundary conditions along any of the three unit cell axes. Information about the atoms (atomic numbers and position) is stored in ndarrays. Optionally, there can be information about tags, momenta, masses, magnetic moments and charges.  In order to calculate energies, forces and stresses, a calculator object has to attached to the atoms object.  Parameters ---------- symbols : str | list[str] | list[Atom] Chemical formula, a list of chemical symbols, or list of :class:`~ase.Atom` objects (mutually exclusive with ``numbers``).  - ``'H2O'`` - ``'COPt12'`` - ``['H', 'H', 'O']`` - ``[Atom('Ne', (x, y, z)), ...]``  positions : list[tuple[float, float, float]] Atomic positions in Cartesian coordinates (mutually exclusive with ``scaled_positions``). Anything that can be converted to an ndarray of shape (n, 3) works: [(x0, y0, z0), (x1, y1, z1), ...]. scaled_positions : list[tuple[float, float, float]] Atomic positions in units of the unit cell (mutually exclusive with ``positions``). numbers : list[int] Atomic numbers (mutually exclusive with ``symbols``). tags : list[int] Special purpose tags. momenta : list[tuple[float, float, float]] Momenta for all atoms in Cartesian coordinates (mutually exclusive with ``velocities``). velocities : list[tuple[float, float, float]] Velocities for all atoms in Cartesian coordinates (mutually exclusive with ``momenta``). masses : list[float] Atomic masses in atomic units. magmoms : list[float] | list[tuple[float, float, float]] Magnetic moments. Can be either a single value for each atom for collinear calculations or three numbers for each atom for non-collinear calculations. charges : list[float] Initial atomic charges. cell : 3x3 matrix or length 3 or 6 vector, default: (0, 0, 0) Unit cell vectors. Can also be given as just three numbers for orthorhombic cells, or 6 numbers, where first three are lengths of unit cell vectors, and the other three are angles between them (in degrees), in following order: [len(a), len(b), len(c), angle(b,c), angle(a,c), angle(a,b)]. First vector will lie in x-direction, second in xy-plane, and the third one in z-positive subspace. celldisp : tuple[float, float, float], default: (0, 0, 0) Unit cell displacement vector. To visualize a displaced cell around the center of mass of a Systems of atoms. pbc : bool | tuple[bool, bool, bool], default: False Periodic boundary conditions flags.  - ``True`` - ``False`` - ``0`` - ``1`` - ``(1, 1, 0)`` - ``(True, False, False)``  constraint : constraint object(s) One or more ASE constraints applied during structure optimization. calculator : :class:`~ase.calculators.calculator.BaseCalculator` ASE calculator to obtain energies and atomic forces. info : dict | None, default: None Dictionary with additional information about the system. The following keys may be used by ASE:  - spacegroup: :class:`~ase.spacegroup.Spacegroup` instance - unit_cell: 'conventional' | 'primitive' | int | 3 ints - adsorbate_info: Information about special adsorption sites  Items in the info attribute survives copy and slicing and can be stored in and retrieved from trajectory files given that the key is a string, the value is JSON-compatible and, if the value is a user-defined object, its base class is importable. One should not make any assumptions about the existence of keys.  Examples -------- >>> from ase import Atom  N2 molecule (These three are equivalent):  >>> d = 1.104 # N2 bondlength >>> a = Atoms('N2', [(0, 0, 0), (0, 0, d)]) >>> a = Atoms(numbers=[7, 7], positions=[(0, 0, 0), (0, 0, d)]) >>> a = Atoms([Atom('N', (0, 0, 0)), Atom('N', (0, 0, d))])  FCC gold:  >>> a = 4.05 # Gold lattice constant >>> b = a / 2 >>> fcc = Atoms('Au', ... cell=[(0, b, b), (b, 0, b), (b, b, 0)], ... pbc=True)  Hydrogen wire:  >>> d = 0.9 # H-H distance >>> h = Atoms('H', positions=[(0, 0, 0)], ... cell=(d, 0, 0), ... pbc=(1, 0, 0))

function.name: get_forces
function.description: Calculate atomic forces.  Ask the attached calculator to calculate the forces and apply constraints. Use *apply_constraint=False* to get the raw forces.  For molecular dynamics (md=True) we don't apply the constraint to the forces but to the momenta. When holonomic constraints for rigid linear triatomic molecules are present, ask the constraints to redistribute the forces within each triple defined in the constraints (required for molecular dynamics with this type of constraints).

basic_info.name: SiC颜色中心PL/ODMR峰到缺陷构型的超精细证据筛选

environment.description:
触发: 4H-SiC PL6等颜色中心已有PL/ODMR信号，但DV-antisite与氧空位复合体等多个缺陷模型均可解释部分ZFS/光学特征，需要决定候选构型资格
对象：同一颜色中心的PL零声子线、ODMR D/E和核超精细峰；候选缺陷构型/电荷自旋态的弛豫结果、形成/结合能、计算误差标定样本
目标：排除仅在光学或ZFS上偶然相似的候选，给出带证据范围的最可能构型或未决模型清单
输入：PL/ODMR实验峰与误差、候选的结构/电荷态/自旋多重度、ZFS D/E张量、KS间隙或显式激发态结果、结合/形成能、各核超精细A张量和天然丰度
步骤/决策：先核对候选电荷自旋态是否能产生测得的高自旋ZFS，并用已知中心校准计算偏差；把KS能级差明确标为粗筛光学代理而非真实ZPL；用结合能/形成能排除不稳定复合体；对通过粗筛的候选比较实验可观测核位点Azz的大小与相对位移，并按同位素丰度/测量方向限制可见性；若只匹配ZFS/PL但超精细相矛盾则降级，若缺核位点分辨则保持并列并交接定向ODMR/ENDOR补测
验收：每项匹配回链同一中心/同一计算结构与坐标方向；KS差不可直接宣称真实ZPL；超精细的核位点/同位素可见性及计算偏差明确；单一ZFS或PL峰不构成微观归属，最终确认需独立定向谱学

init_ref_tools.name: rattle
init_ref_tools.description: Given a ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object, apply random displacements to all atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``.

stdev.description: Standard deviation (in Angstroms) of the Gaussian distribution from which random atomic displacement distances are drawn during rattling. Default is set to 10% of the bulk nearest neighbour distance. Note that the average displacement distance will be roughly equal to ``stdev * 1.6``.

d_min.description: Minimum interatomic distance (in Angstroms) in the rattled structure. Monte Carlo rattle moves that put atoms at distances less than this will be heavily penalised. Default is to set this to 80% of the nearest neighbour distance in the defect supercell.

verbose.description: Whether to print information about the rattling process, if rattling initially fails with initial ``d_min``.

n_iter.description: Number of Monte Carlo cycles to perform. (Default: 1)

active_atoms.description: List of which atomic indices should undergo Monte Carlo rattling. If not set, rattles all atoms in the structure. (Default: None)

nbr_cutoff.description: The radial cutoff distance (in Angstroms) used to construct the list of atomic neighbours for checking interatomic distances. (Default: 5)

width.description: Width of the Monte Carlo rattling error function, in Angstroms. (Default: 0.1)

max_attempts.description: Maximum Monte Carlo rattle move attempts allowed for a single atom; if this limit is reached an ``Exception`` is raised. (Default: 5000)

max_disp.description: Maximum atomic displacement (in Angstroms) during Monte Carlo rattling. Rarely occurs and is used primarily as a safety net. (Default: 2.0)

seed.description: Seed for NumPy random state from which random rattle displacements are generated. (Default: 42)

return.description: obj:`Structure`: Rattled ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object

init_ref_tools.name: Distortions
init_ref_tools.description: Class to apply rattle and bond distortion to all defects in ``defect_entries`` (each defect as a ``doped`` or ``pymatgen`` ``DefectEntry`` object).

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialises the relevant information for generating ``ShakeNBreak`` distorted structures for defect entries in ``defect_entries``.  The `default` distortions generated have the bond lengths of ``X`` nearest neighbours distorted by -60% to +60% (``bond_distortions``) in increments of 10% (``distortion_increment``), where ``X`` is equal to the excess charge for that defect species (e.g. ``2`` for ``v_Cd_0``; see SnB tutorial: https://shakenbreak.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ShakeNBreak_Example_Workflow.html or npj theory paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-023-00973-1 for more info). Additionally, a dimer distortion will be included by default for each vacancy defect (see ``distortions.apply_dimer_distortion`` for more info), and distortions which result in inter-atomic distances less than 1 Å are excluded (unless Hydrogen is present).  Rattling is then performed by applying random displacements to atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``. Rattling behaviour can be controlled with ``mc_rattle_kwargs``, see the ``distortions.rattle()`` docstring for more info. Note that by default, rattling is not applied to the defect site or distorted neighbours, but to all other atoms in the supercell, however this can be controlled with the ``active_atoms`` kwarg (in ``mc_rattle_kwargs``).  The nearest neighbours to distort are chosen by taking all sites (or those matching ``distorted_element`` / ``distorted_atoms``, if provided), then sorting by distance to the defect site (rounded to 2 decimal places) and site index, and then taking the first ``num_nearest_neighbours`` of these. If there are multiple non-degenerate combinations of (nearly) equidistant NNs to distort (e.g. cis vs trans when distorting 2 NNs in a 4 NN square coordination), then the combination with distorted NNs closest to each other is chosen.  The bond distortion and rattling approaches are highly customisable via ``kwargs`` to this class and its methods, so see the argument descriptions for more info.

defect_entries.description: Either a ``DefectsGenerator`` object from ``doped``, or a list/dictionary of, or single, ``DefectEntry`` object(s). E.g.: ``[DefectEntry(), DefectEntry(), ...]``, or single ``DefectEntry``. If a ``DefectsGenerator`` object or a dictionary (-> ``{defect_species: DefectEntry}``), the defect folder names will be set equal to ``defect_species`` (with charge states included). If a list or single ``DefectEntry`` object is provided, the defect folder names will be set equal to ``DefectEntry.name`` if the ``name`` attribute is set for all input ``DefectEntry``\s, otherwise generated according to the ``doped`` convention (see: https://doped.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generation_tutorial.html).  Defect charge states (from which bond distortions are determined) are taken from the ``DefectEntry.charge_state`` property.  Alternatively, a defects dict generated by ``ChargedDefectStructures`` from ``PyCDT``/``doped<2.0`` can also be used as input, and the defect names and charge states generated by these codes will be used E.g.: ``{"bulk": {..}, "vacancies": [{...}, {...},], ...}``

oxidation_states.description: Dictionary of oxidation states for species in your material, used to determine the number of defect neighbours to distort (e.g {"Cd": +2, "Te": -2}). If none is provided, the oxidation states will be guessed based on the bulk composition and most common oxidation states of any extrinsic species.

dict_number_electrons_user.description: Optional argument to set the number of extra/missing charge (negative of electron count change) for the input defects in their neutral state, as a dictionary with format {'defect_name': charge_change} where charge_change is the negative of the number of extra/missing electrons. (Default: None)

distortion_increment.description: Bond distortion increment. Distortion factors will range from 0 to +/-0.6, in increments of ``distortion_increment``. Recommended values: 0.1-0.3 (Default: 0.1)

bond_distortions.description: List of bond distortions to apply to nearest neighbours, instead of the default set described above (e.g. [-0.5, 0.5]). (Default: None)

local_rattle.description: Whether to apply random displacements that tail off as we move away from the defect site. Not recommended as typically worsens performance. If False (default), all supercell sites are rattled with the same amplitude (full rattle). (Default: False)

distorted_elements.description: Optional argument to specify the neighbouring elements to distort for each defect, in the form of a dictionary with format {'defect_name': ['element1', 'element2', ...]} (e.g {'vac_1_Cd': ['Te']}). If None, the closest neighbours to the defect are chosen. (Default: None)

distorted_atoms.description: Optional argument to specify the indices of the neighbouring atoms to distort for each defect (with indices starting from 0, matching python / ``pymatgen`` 0-indexing) for each defect, in the form of a dictionary with format: ``{'defect_name': [index_1, index_2, ...]}`` (e.g ``{'vac_1_Cd': [0, 2]}``). If None (default), the closest neighbours to the defect are chosen.

dimer_bond_length.description: The bond length to set generated dimers in dimer distortions to, in Å. If ``None`` (default), uses ``distortions.get_dimer_bond_length`` to estimate the dimer bond length in each case.

mc_rattle_kwargs.description: Additional keyword arguments to pass to ``hiphive``'s ``mc_rattle`` function. These include:  - stdev (:obj:`float`): Standard deviation (in Å) of the Gaussian distribution from which random atomic displacement distances are drawn during rattling. Default is set to 10% of the nearest neighbour distance in the bulk supercell. Note that the average displacement distance will be roughly equal to ``stdev * 1.6``. - d_min (:obj:`float`): Minimum interatomic distance (in Å) in the rattled structure. Monte Carlo rattle moves that put atoms at distances less than this will be heavily penalised. Default is to set this to 80% of the nearest neighbour distance in the bulk supercell. - max_disp (:obj:`float`): Maximum atomic displacement (in Å) during Monte Carlo rattling. Rarely occurs and is used primarily as a safety net. (Default: 2.0) - max_attempts (:obj:`int`): Limit for how many attempted rattle moves are allowed a single atom. - active_atoms (:obj:`list`): List of the atomic indices which should undergo Monte Carlo rattling. By default, all atoms are rattled. (Default: None) - seed (:obj:`int`): Seed from which rattle random displacements are generated. Default is to set ``seed = int(distortion_factor*100``) (i.e. +40% distortion -> distortion_factor = 1.4 -> seed = 140, Rattled -> distortion_factor = 1 (no bond distortion) -> seed = 100)

function.name: apply_distortions
function.description: Applies a range of bond distortions (given by ``self.bond_distortions``) and rattling to the unperturbed defect supercell structures of all defects in ``self.defect_entries``, using ``apply_snb_distortions()``.  Returns a dictionary with the distorted (and undistorted) structures for each charge state of each defect. If file generation is desired, instead use the methods ``write_<code>_files()``.  Note that by default, rattling is not applied to the defect site or distorted neighbours, but to all other atoms in the supercell, however this can be controlled with the ``active_atoms`` kwarg (in ``mc_rattle_kwargs``). Rattling is performed by applying random displacements to atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``. Rattling behaviour can be controlled with ``mc_rattle_kwargs``, see the ``distortions.rattle()`` docstring for more info.  The nearest neighbours to distort are chosen by taking all sites (or those matching ``distorted_element`` / ``distorted_atoms``, if provided), then sorting by distance to the defect site (rounded to 2 decimal places) and site index, and then taking the first ``num_nearest_neighbours`` of these. If there are multiple non-degenerate combinations of (nearly) equidistant NNs to distort (e.g. cis vs trans when distorting 2 NNs in a 4 NN square coordination), then the combination with distorted NNs closest to each other is chosen.  The bond distortion and rattling approaches are highly customisable via ``kwargs`` to this class and its methods, so see the argument descriptions for more info.

verbose.description: Whether to print distortion information (bond atoms and distances) for each charged defect. (Default: None -- medium level verbosity)

return.description: obj:`tuple`: Tuple of a dictionary with the distorted and undistorted structures for each charge state of each defect, in the format: .. code-block:: python {'defect_name': { 'charges': { {charge_state}: { 'structures': {...}, }, }, }} and dictionary with distortion parameters for each defect.

function.name: get_supercell_structure
function.description: Generate the simulation supercell for a defect.  Redefined from the parent class to allow the use of ``target_frac_coords`` to place the defect at the closest equivalent site to the target fractional coordinates in the supercell, while keeping the supercell fixed (to avoid any issues with defect parsing). Also returns information about equivalent defect sites in the supercell.  If ``sc_mat`` is None, then the supercell is generated automatically using the ``doped`` algorithm described in the ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` function docstring in ``doped.generation``.

sc_mat.description: Transformation matrix of ``self.structure`` to create the supercell. If ``None`` (default), then automatically computed using ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` from ``doped.generation``.

target_frac_coords.description: If set, the defect will be placed at the closest equivalent site to these fractional coordinates (using ``self.equivalent_sites``).

return_sites.description: If True, returns a tuple of the defect supercell, defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

min_image_distance.description: Minimum image distance in Å of the generated supercell (i.e. minimum distance between periodic images of atoms/sites in the lattice), if ``sc_mat`` is None. (Default = 10.0)

min_atoms.description: Minimum number of atoms allowed in the generated supercell, if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``. (Default = 50)

force_cubic.description: Enforce usage of ``CubicSupercellTransformation`` from ``pymatgen`` for supercell generation (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = False)

force_diagonal.description: If True, return a transformation with a diagonal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is None). (Default = False)

ideal_threshold.description: Threshold for increasing supercell size (beyond that which satisfies ``min_image_distance`` and `min_atoms``) to achieve an ideal supercell matrix (i.e. a diagonal expansion of the primitive or conventional cell). Supercells up to ``1 + perfect_cell_threshold`` times larger (rounded up) are trialled, and will instead be returned if they yield an ideal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = 0.1; i.e. 10% larger than the minimum size)

dummy_species.description: Dummy species to highlight the defect position (for visualizing vacancies).

return.description: The defect supercell structure. If ``return_sites`` is True, also returns the defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

init_ref_tools.name: IStructure
init_ref_tools.description: Basic immutable Structure object with periodicity. Essentially a sequence of PeriodicSites having a common lattice. IStructure is made to be (somewhat) immutable so that they can function as keys in a dict. To make modifications, use the standard Structure object instead. Structure extends Sequence and Hashable, which means that in many cases, it can be used like any Python sequence. Iterating through a structure is equivalent to going through the sites in sequence.

init_ref_tools.name: rattle
init_ref_tools.description: Given a ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object, apply random displacements to all atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``.

stdev.description: Standard deviation (in Angstroms) of the Gaussian distribution from which random atomic displacement distances are drawn during rattling. Default is set to 10% of the bulk nearest neighbour distance. Note that the average displacement distance will be roughly equal to ``stdev * 1.6``.

d_min.description: Minimum interatomic distance (in Angstroms) in the rattled structure. Monte Carlo rattle moves that put atoms at distances less than this will be heavily penalised. Default is to set this to 80% of the nearest neighbour distance in the defect supercell.

verbose.description: Whether to print information about the rattling process, if rattling initially fails with initial ``d_min``.

n_iter.description: Number of Monte Carlo cycles to perform. (Default: 1)

active_atoms.description: List of which atomic indices should undergo Monte Carlo rattling. If not set, rattles all atoms in the structure. (Default: None)

nbr_cutoff.description: The radial cutoff distance (in Angstroms) used to construct the list of atomic neighbours for checking interatomic distances. (Default: 5)

width.description: Width of the Monte Carlo rattling error function, in Angstroms. (Default: 0.1)

max_attempts.description: Maximum Monte Carlo rattle move attempts allowed for a single atom; if this limit is reached an ``Exception`` is raised. (Default: 5000)

max_disp.description: Maximum atomic displacement (in Angstroms) during Monte Carlo rattling. Rarely occurs and is used primarily as a safety net. (Default: 2.0)

seed.description: Seed for NumPy random state from which random rattle displacements are generated. (Default: 42)

return.description: obj:`Structure`: Rattled ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object

init_ref_tools.name: Distortions
init_ref_tools.description: Class to apply rattle and bond distortion to all defects in ``defect_entries`` (each defect as a ``doped`` or ``pymatgen`` ``DefectEntry`` object).

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialises the relevant information for generating ``ShakeNBreak`` distorted structures for defect entries in ``defect_entries``.  The `default` distortions generated have the bond lengths of ``X`` nearest neighbours distorted by -60% to +60% (``bond_distortions``) in increments of 10% (``distortion_increment``), where ``X`` is equal to the excess charge for that defect species (e.g. ``2`` for ``v_Cd_0``; see SnB tutorial: https://shakenbreak.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ShakeNBreak_Example_Workflow.html or npj theory paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-023-00973-1 for more info). Additionally, a dimer distortion will be included by default for each vacancy defect (see ``distortions.apply_dimer_distortion`` for more info), and distortions which result in inter-atomic distances less than 1 Å are excluded (unless Hydrogen is present).  Rattling is then performed by applying random displacements to atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``. Rattling behaviour can be controlled with ``mc_rattle_kwargs``, see the ``distortions.rattle()`` docstring for more info. Note that by default, rattling is not applied to the defect site or distorted neighbours, but to all other atoms in the supercell, however this can be controlled with the ``active_atoms`` kwarg (in ``mc_rattle_kwargs``).  The nearest neighbours to distort are chosen by taking all sites (or those matching ``distorted_element`` / ``distorted_atoms``, if provided), then sorting by distance to the defect site (rounded to 2 decimal places) and site index, and then taking the first ``num_nearest_neighbours`` of these. If there are multiple non-degenerate combinations of (nearly) equidistant NNs to distort (e.g. cis vs trans when distorting 2 NNs in a 4 NN square coordination), then the combination with distorted NNs closest to each other is chosen.  The bond distortion and rattling approaches are highly customisable via ``kwargs`` to this class and its methods, so see the argument descriptions for more info.

defect_entries.description: Either a ``DefectsGenerator`` object from ``doped``, or a list/dictionary of, or single, ``DefectEntry`` object(s). E.g.: ``[DefectEntry(), DefectEntry(), ...]``, or single ``DefectEntry``. If a ``DefectsGenerator`` object or a dictionary (-> ``{defect_species: DefectEntry}``), the defect folder names will be set equal to ``defect_species`` (with charge states included). If a list or single ``DefectEntry`` object is provided, the defect folder names will be set equal to ``DefectEntry.name`` if the ``name`` attribute is set for all input ``DefectEntry``\s, otherwise generated according to the ``doped`` convention (see: https://doped.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generation_tutorial.html).  Defect charge states (from which bond distortions are determined) are taken from the ``DefectEntry.charge_state`` property.  Alternatively, a defects dict generated by ``ChargedDefectStructures`` from ``PyCDT``/``doped<2.0`` can also be used as input, and the defect names and charge states generated by these codes will be used E.g.: ``{"bulk": {..}, "vacancies": [{...}, {...},], ...}``

oxidation_states.description: Dictionary of oxidation states for species in your material, used to determine the number of defect neighbours to distort (e.g {"Cd": +2, "Te": -2}). If none is provided, the oxidation states will be guessed based on the bulk composition and most common oxidation states of any extrinsic species.

dict_number_electrons_user.description: Optional argument to set the number of extra/missing charge (negative of electron count change) for the input defects in their neutral state, as a dictionary with format {'defect_name': charge_change} where charge_change is the negative of the number of extra/missing electrons. (Default: None)

distortion_increment.description: Bond distortion increment. Distortion factors will range from 0 to +/-0.6, in increments of ``distortion_increment``. Recommended values: 0.1-0.3 (Default: 0.1)

bond_distortions.description: List of bond distortions to apply to nearest neighbours, instead of the default set described above (e.g. [-0.5, 0.5]). (Default: None)

local_rattle.description: Whether to apply random displacements that tail off as we move away from the defect site. Not recommended as typically worsens performance. If False (default), all supercell sites are rattled with the same amplitude (full rattle). (Default: False)

distorted_elements.description: Optional argument to specify the neighbouring elements to distort for each defect, in the form of a dictionary with format {'defect_name': ['element1', 'element2', ...]} (e.g {'vac_1_Cd': ['Te']}). function.name: get_supercell_structure
function.description: Generate the simulation supercell for a defect.  Redefined from the parent class to allow the use of ``target_frac_coords`` to place the defect at the closest equivalent site to the target fractional coordinates in the supercell, while keeping the supercell fixed (to avoid any issues with defect parsing). Also returns information about equivalent defect sites in the supercell.  If ``sc_mat`` is None, then the supercell is generated automatically using the ``doped`` algorithm described in the ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` function docstring in ``doped.generation``.

sc_mat.description: Transformation matrix of ``self.structure`` to create the supercell. If ``None`` (default), then automatically computed using ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` from ``doped.generation``.

target_frac_coords.description: If set, the defect will be placed at the closest equivalent site to these fractional coordinates (using ``self.equivalent_sites``).

return_sites.description: If True, returns a tuple of the defect supercell, defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

min_image_distance.description: Minimum image distance in Å of the generated supercell (i.e. minimum distance between periodic images of atoms/sites in the lattice), if ``sc_mat`` is None. (Default = 10.0)

min_atoms.description: Minimum number of atoms allowed in the generated supercell, if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``. (Default = 50)

force_cubic.description: Enforce usage of ``CubicSupercellTransformation`` from ``pymatgen`` for supercell generation (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = False)

force_diagonal.description: If True, return a transformation with a diagonal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is None). (Default = False)

ideal_threshold.description: Threshold for increasing supercell size (beyond that which satisfies ``min_image_distance`` and `min_atoms``) to achieve an ideal supercell matrix (i.e. a diagonal expansion of the primitive or conventional cell). Supercells up to ``1 + perfect_cell_threshold`` times larger (rounded up) are trialled, and will instead be returned if they yield an ideal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = 0.1; i.e. 10% larger than the minimum size)

dummy_species.description: Dummy species to highlight the defect position (for visualizing vacancies).

return.description: The defect supercell structure. If ``return_sites`` is True, also returns the defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

init_ref_tools.name: IStructure
init_ref_tools.description: Basic immutable Structure object with periodicity. Essentially a sequence of PeriodicSites having a common lattice. IStructure is made to be (somewhat) immutable so that they can function as keys in a dict. To make modifications, use the standard Structure object instead. Structure extends Sequence and Hashable, which means that in many cases, it can be used like any Python sequence. Iterating through a structure is equivalent to going through the sites in sequence.

init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: PL/ODMR、ZFS及天然丰度超精细结果支持氧相关缺陷但无法排除不含氧的DV-antisite模型，需确认氧是否进入微观中心
对象：同批SiC未标记与氧-17离子植入/退火样本、PL6类颜色中心、定向磁场ODMR谱、植入剂量与退火履历
目标：以同位素核自旋指纹直接检验氧参与并决定保留氧空位模型、退回非氧模型或继续补证
输入：标记/未标记样本PL-ZPL与D/E、氧-17含量/植入与退火记录、磁场方向和强度、ODMR峰列及拟合不确定度、候选A张量
步骤/决策：确认标记/未标记样本在光学与ZFS上对应同一中心类型；在定向磁场下拟合氧-17核自旋预期分裂并记录不同ODMR分支；把六线峰和Azz与未标记及其他缺陷对照；若标记样本出现可重复的同位素指纹且中心身份未变，提升氧相关模型资格并与计算核位点对应；若无信号则先核对植入/中心产额和信噪比，不因非检出直接否定氧模型；制备或中心混杂不明则暂停归属
验收：同一中心的PL/ZFS指纹和样本履历可追溯；六线I=5/2结构、峰位/Azz与磁场方向可复核；自然丰度非检出或标记后非检出均不得不经产额/灵敏度检查就确证或否定模型；元素参与证据不自动确定唯一晶格位置

可合成任务：输入：标记/未标记样本PL-ZPL与D/E、氧-17含量/植入与退火记录、磁场方向和强度、ODMR峰列及拟合不确定度、候选A张量
Python核心操作/决策：拟议Python对标记/对照ODMR固定谱做多峰拟合、对齐PL/ZFS及植入元数据、与A张量预测比较；VASP计算/样本植入/ODMR采集均为外部核心
输出：同位素超精细峰拟合、标记-对照差异和氧模型保留/退回/待补证状态

basic_info.name: shakenbreak
basic_info.description: ShakeNBreak 通过缺陷周围的键长畸变与随机扰动生成候选结构，并整理和分析结构弛豫结果，以搜索固体缺陷的低能、基态及亚稳态构型。它支持多种电子结构程序的输入输出及能量和结构比较，实际结构弛豫由外部计算程序完成。

basic_info.name: doped
basic_info.description: doped 是面向固体点缺陷研究的 Python 包，可生成缺陷与电荷态、准备 VASP 计算输入、解析计算结果并执行有限尺寸修正、化学势和缺陷热力学分析。它支持形成能、电荷转变能级、平衡及冻结缺陷浓度和费米能级计算，并可连接 ShakeNBreak 与 py-sc-fermi 等工具。

basic_info.name: pymatgen-core
basic_info.description: pymatgen-core提供晶体、晶格、组成、对称性、文件转换及材料计算结果分析的基础数据结构和方法，作为当前材料场景的统一结构状态。

basic_info.name: 电荷态重构路径与俘获证据复核

environment.description:
触发: 相邻缺陷电荷态的形成能图显示深能级、负U候选或实验出现光/偏压相关亚稳态，需要判断是否存在可达的结构重构路径及俘获证据
对象：同一缺陷位点的两个或多个电荷态弛豫结构、形成能/跃迁能级、超胞取向、局部键合环境和实验工作窗口
目标：交付可重放的电荷态结构取向、配置坐标或NEB路径和相应能量证据；分别判定热力学负U候选、路径/势垒解释与俘获速率证据的可用范围，或退回补算。
输入：不同电荷态缺陷超胞、原子索引和晶格、形成能及参考带边、费米/光激发窗口、结构匹配参数、外部弛豫或NEB结果
步骤/决策：先核对各电荷态已弛豫稳定构型、形成能和共同能量参考，单独记录热力学负U/跃迁能级结论；再对齐同一缺陷位点的原子索引及对称等价取向，生成配置坐标插值或NEB初始路径并提交外部弛豫；检查路径点能量、势能面和收敛；仅在相应非辐射俘获模型及输入验证后讨论俘获速率。路径未收敛不得声称动力学障碍；仅有热力学交点不得声称俘获速率或器件亚稳态。
验收：两端稳定构型、缺陷位置、原子索引和取向可追溯；路径点与外部计算版本可重放，路径/能量收敛按项目规则检查；热力学负U、CC/NEB势垒、模型俘获速率和器件效应分别报告证据等级。负U热力学分类无需NEB路径；无可靠动力学模型不得发布俘获速率；器件性能结论需独立器件/实验依据。

init_ref_tools.name: rattle
init_ref_tools.description: Given a ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object, apply random displacements to all atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``.

stdev.description: Standard deviation (in Angstroms) of the Gaussian distribution from which random atomic displacement distances are drawn during rattling. Default is set to 10% of the bulk nearest neighbour distance. Note that the average displacement distance will be roughly equal to ``stdev * 1.6``.

d_min.description: Minimum interatomic distance (in Angstroms) in the rattled structure. Monte Carlo rattle moves that put atoms at distances less than this will be heavily penalised. Default is to set this to 80% of the nearest neighbour distance in the defect supercell.

verbose.description: Whether to print information about the rattling process, if rattling initially fails with initial ``d_min``.

n_iter.description: Number of Monte Carlo cycles to perform. (Default: 1)

active_atoms.description: List of which atomic indices should undergo Monte Carlo rattling. If not set, rattles all atoms in the structure. (Default: None)

nbr_cutoff.description: The radial cutoff distance (in Angstroms) used to construct the list of atomic neighbours for checking interatomic distances. (Default: 5)

width.description: Width of the Monte Carlo rattling error function, in Angstroms. (Default: 0.1)

max_attempts.description: Maximum Monte Carlo rattle move attempts allowed for a single atom; if this limit is reached an ``Exception`` is raised. (Default: 5000)

max_disp.description: Maximum atomic displacement (in Angstroms) during Monte Carlo rattling. Rarely occurs and is used primarily as a safety net. (Default: 2.0)

seed.description: Seed for NumPy random state from which random rattle displacements are generated. (Default: 42)

return.description: obj:`Structure`: Rattled ``pymatgen`` ``Structure`` object

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initialises the relevant information for generating ``ShakeNBreak`` distorted structures for defect entries in ``defect_entries``.  The `default` distortions generated have the bond lengths of ``X`` nearest neighbours distorted by -60% to +60% (``bond_distortions``) in increments of 10% (``distortion_increment``), where ``X`` is equal to the excess charge for that defect species (e.g. ``2`` for ``v_Cd_0``; see SnB tutorial: https://shakenbreak.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ShakeNBreak_Example_Workflow.html or npj theory paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-023-00973-1 for more info). Additionally, a dimer distortion will be included by default for each vacancy defect (see ``distortions.apply_dimer_distortion`` for more info), and distortions which result in inter-atomic distances less than 1 Å are excluded (unless Hydrogen is present).  Rattling is then performed by applying random displacements to atomic positions, with the displacement distances randomly drawn from a Gaussian distribution of standard deviation ``stdev``, using a Monte Carlo algorithm which disfavours moves that bring atoms closer than ``d_min``. Rattling behaviour can be controlled with ``mc_rattle_kwargs``, see the ``distortions.rattle()`` docstring for more info. Note that by default, rattling is not applied to the defect site or distorted neighbours, but to all other atoms in the supercell, however this can be controlled with the ``active_atoms`` kwarg (in ``mc_rattle_kwargs``).  The nearest neighbours to distort are chosen by taking all sites (or those matching ``distorted_element`` / ``distorted_atoms``, if provided), then sorting by distance to the defect site (rounded to 2 decimal places) and site index, and then taking the first ``num_nearest_neighbours`` of these. If there are multiple non-degenerate combinations of (nearly) equidistant NNs to distort (e.g. cis vs trans when distorting 2 NNs in a 4 NN square coordination), then the combination with distorted NNs closest to each other is chosen.  The bond distortion and rattling approaches are highly customisable via ``kwargs`` to this class and its methods, so see the argument descriptions for more info.

defect_entries.description: Either a ``DefectsGenerator`` object from ``doped``, or a list/dictionary of, or single, ``DefectEntry`` object(s). E.g.: ``[DefectEntry(), DefectEntry(), ...]``, or single ``DefectEntry``. If a ``DefectsGenerator`` object or a dictionary (-> ``{defect_species: DefectEntry}``), the defect folder names will be set equal to ``defect_species`` (with charge states included). If a list or single ``DefectEntry`` object is provided, the defect folder names will be set equal to ``DefectEntry.name`` if the ``name`` attribute is set for all input ``DefectEntry``\s, otherwise generated according to the ``doped`` convention (see: https://doped.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generation_tutorial.html).  Defect charge states (from which bond distortions are determined) are taken from the ``DefectEntry.charge_state`` property.  Alternatively, a defects dict generated by ``ChargedDefectStructures`` from ``PyCDT``/``doped<2.0`` can also be used as input, and the defect names and charge states generated by these codes will be used E.g.: ``{"bulk": {..}, "vacancies": [{...}, {...},], ...}``

oxidation_states.description: Dictionary of oxidation states for species in your material, used to determine the number of defect neighbours to distort (e.g {"Cd": +2, "Te": -2}). If none is provided, the oxidation states will be guessed based on the bulk composition and most common oxidation states of any extrinsic species.

dict_number_electrons_user.description: Optional argument to set the number of extra/missing charge (negative of electron count change) for the input defects in their neutral state, as a dictionary with format {'defect_name': charge_change} where charge_change is the negative of the number of extra/missing electrons. (Default: None)

distortion_increment.description: Bond distortion increment. Distortion factors will range from 0 to +/-0.6, in increments of ``distortion_increment``. Recommended values: 0.1-0.3 (Default: 0.1)

bond_distortions.description: List of bond distortions to apply to nearest neighbours, instead of the default set described above (e.g. [-0.5, 0.5]). (Default: None)

local_rattle.description: Whether to apply random displacements that tail off as we move away from the defect site. Not recommended as typically worsens performance. If False (default), all supercell sites are rattled with the same amplitude (full rattle). (Default: False)

distorted_elements.description: Optional argument to specify the neighbouring elements to distort for each defect, in the form of a dictionary with format {'defect_name': ['element1', 'element2', ...]} (e.g {'vac_1_Cd': ['Te']}). If None, the closest neighbours to the defect are chosen. (Default: None)

distorted_atoms.description: Optional argument to specify the indices of the neighbouring atoms to distort for each defect (with indices starting from 0, matching python / ``pymatgen`` 0-indexing) for each defect, in the form of a dictionary with format: ``{'defect_name': [index_1, index_2, ...]}`` (e.g ``{'vac_1_Cd': [0, 2]}``). If None (default), the closest neighbours to the defect are chosen.

dimer_bond_length.description: The bond length to set generated dimers in dimer distortions to, in Å. If ``None`` (default), uses ``distortions.get_dimer_bond_length`` to estimate the dimer bond length in each case.

mc_rattle_kwargs.description: Additional keyword arguments to pass to ``hiphive``'s ``mc_rattle`` function. These include:  - stdev (:obj:`float`): Standard deviation (in Å) of the Gaussian distribution from which random atomic displacement distances are drawn during rattling. Default is set to 10% of the nearest neighbour distance in the bulk supercell. Note that the average displacement distance will be roughly equal to ``stdev * 1.6``. - d_min (:obj:`float`): Minimum interatomic distance (in Å) in the rattled structure. Monte Carlo rattle moves that put atoms at distances less than this will be heavily penalised. Default is to set this to 80% of the nearest neighbour distance in the bulk supercell. - max_disp (:obj:`float`): Maximum atomic displacement (in Å) during Monte Carlo rattling. Rarely occurs and is used primarily as a safety net. (Default: 2.0) - max_attempts (:obj:`int`): Limit for how many attempted rattle moves are allowed a single atom. - active_atoms (:obj:`list`): List of the atomic indices which should undergo Monte Carlo rattling. By default, all atoms are rattled. (Default: None) - seed (:obj:`int`): Seed from which rattle random displacements are generated. Default is to set ``seed = int(distortion_factor*100``) (i.e. +40% distortion -> distortion_factor = 1.4 -> seed = 140, Rattled -> distortion_factor = 1 (no bond distortion) -> seed = 100)

function.description: Generate the simulation supercell for a defect.  Redefined from the parent class to allow the use of ``target_frac_coords`` to place the defect at the closest equivalent site to the target fractional coordinates in the supercell, while keeping the supercell fixed (to avoid any issues with defect parsing). Also returns information about equivalent defect sites in the supercell.  If ``sc_mat`` is None, then the supercell is generated automatically using the ``doped`` algorithm described in the ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` function docstring in ``doped.generation``.

sc_mat.description: Transformation matrix of ``self.structure`` to create the supercell. If ``None`` (default), then automatically computed using ``get_ideal_supercell_matrix`` from ``doped.generation``.

target_frac_coords.description: If set, the defect will be placed at the closest equivalent site to these fractional coordinates (using ``self.equivalent_sites``).

return_sites.description: If True, returns a tuple of the defect supercell, defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

min_image_distance.description: Minimum image distance in Å of the generated supercell (i.e. minimum distance between periodic images of atoms/sites in the lattice), if ``sc_mat`` is None. (Default = 10.0)

min_atoms.description: Minimum number of atoms allowed in the generated supercell, if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``. (Default = 50)

force_cubic.description: Enforce usage of ``CubicSupercellTransformation`` from ``pymatgen`` for supercell generation (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = False)

force_diagonal.description: If True, return a transformation with a diagonal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is None). (Default = False)

ideal_threshold.description: Threshold for increasing supercell size (beyond that which satisfies ``min_image_distance`` and `min_atoms``) to achieve an ideal supercell matrix (i.e. a diagonal expansion of the primitive or conventional cell). Supercells up to ``1 + perfect_cell_threshold`` times larger (rounded up) are trialled, and will instead be returned if they yield an ideal transformation matrix (if ``sc_mat`` is ``None``). (Default = 0.1; i.e. 10% larger than the minimum size)

dummy_species.description: Dummy species to highlight the defect position (for visualizing vacancies).

return.description: The defect supercell structure. If ``return_sites`` is True, also returns the defect supercell site and list of equivalent supercell sites.

init_ref_tools.name: IStructure
init_ref_tools.description: Basic immutable Structure object with periodicity. Essentially a sequence of PeriodicSites having a common lattice. IStructure is made to be (somewhat) immutable so that they can function as keys in a dict. To make modifications, use the standard Structure object instead. Structure extends Sequence and Hashable, which means that in many cases, it can be used like any Python sequence. Iterating through a structure is equivalent to going through the sites in sequence.
