init_ref_tools.name: add_voltage
init_ref_tools.description: Add a time-dependent voltage to a lead.  Add a lead unit cell to the ``syst`` where ``lead`` is attached, and couple this to ``syst`` with a time-dependent hopping that effectively adds a voltage to the lead.

syst.description: The central system, with its leads already attached. Modified on return.

lead.description: The number of the lead on which to apply the voltage.

phase.description: Function specifying the anti-derivative of the voltage. Takes takes the same extra arguments as the Hamiltonian value functions, starting with the time. Returns either a scalar or a one-dimensional sequence: one element per orbital on a site. Must return 0 (or a sequence of zeros) at time 0.

return.description: The sites added to the system.

init_ref_tools.ori_input: syst, lead, phase
init_ref_tools.ori_description: Add a time-dependent voltage to a lead.  Add a lead unit cell to the ``syst`` where ``lead`` is attached, and couple this to ``syst`` with a time-dependent hopping that effectively adds a voltage to the lead.  Parameters ---------- syst : `kwant.builder.Builder` The central system, with its leads already attached. Modified on return. lead : int The number of the lead on which to apply the voltage. phase : callable Function specifying the anti-derivative of the voltage. Takes takes the same extra arguments as the Hamiltonian value functions, starting with the time. Returns either a scalar or a one-dimensional sequence: one element per orbital on a site. Must return 0 (or a sequence of zeros) at time 0.  Returns ------- tuple The sites added to the system.  Raises ------ ValueError If the ``phase`` argument is not callable, or if sites in the lead interface belong to different domains  Notes ----- Formally, this function adds a single lead cell to the system and attaches the previous lead interface to it with a hopping :math:`(1 \otimes \exp[iX(t)])V`, where V is the hopping between lead unit cells, 1 is the unit matrix over the interface sites and X(t) is a square diagonal matrix over the orbitals on one site, specified by the ``phase`` parameter. This corresponds to adding a voltage X'(t) to each site in the lead. In the most common case of 1 orbital per site X(t) is a scalar.  This function only works if the lead was attached with ``attach_lead``,  If any exceptions are raised in this function there are no guarantees that the system was not modified.

init_ref_tools.name: Model
init_ref_tools.description: A class describing a tight-binding model. It contains methods for modifying the model, evaluating the Hamiltonian or eigenvalues at specific k-points, and writing to and from different file formats.  Parameters ---------- on_site : On-site energy of the states. This is equivalent to having a hopping within the same state and the same unit cell (diagonal terms of the R=(0, 0, 0) hopping matrix). The length of the list must be the same as the number of states. hop : Hopping matrices, as a dict containing the corresponding lattice vector R as a key. size : Number of states. Defaults to the size of the hopping matrices, if such are given. dim : Dimension of the tight-binding model. By default, the dimension is guessed from the other parameters if possible. occ : Number of occupied states. pos : Positions of the orbitals, in reduced coordinates. By default, all orbitals are set to be at the origin, i.e. at [0., 0., 0.]. uc : Unit cell of the system. The unit cell vectors are given as rows in a ``dim`` x ``dim`` array contains_cc : Specifies whether the hopping matrices and on-site energies are given fully (``contains_cc=True``), or the complex conjugate should be added for each term to obtain the full model. The ``on_site`` parameter is not affected by this. cc_check_tolerance : Tolerance when checking if the complex conjugate values (if given) match. sparse : Specifies whether the hopping matrices should be saved in sparse format.

function.name: add_hop
function.description: Adds a hopping term with a given overlap (hopping strength) from ``orbital_2`` (:math:`o_2`), which lies in the unit cell pointed to by ``R``, to ``orbital_1`` (:math:`o_1`) which is in the home unit cell. In other words, ``overlap`` is the matrix element :math:`\mathcal{H}_{o_1,o_2}(\mathbf{R}) = \langle o_1, \mathbf{0} | \mathcal{H} | o_2, \mathbf{R} \rangle`.  The complex conjugate of the hopping is added automatically. That is, the matrix element :math:`\langle o_2, \mathbf{R} | \mathcal{H} | o_1, \mathbf{0} \rangle` does not have to be added manually.  .. note:: This means that adding a hopping of overlap :math:`\epsilon` between an orbital and itself in the home unit cell increases the orbitals on-site energy by :math:`2 \epsilon`.

overlap.description: Strength of the hopping term (in energy units).

R.description: Lattice vector pointing to the unit cell where ``orbital_2`` lies.  .. warning:: The positions given in the constructor of :class:`Model` are automatically mapped into the home unit cell. This has to be taken into account when determining ``R``.

In other words, ``overlap`` is the matrix element :math:`\mathcal{H}_{o_1,o_2}(\mathbf{R}) = \langle o_1, \mathbf{0} | \mathcal{H} | o_2, \mathbf{R} \rangle`.  The complex conjugate of the hopping is added automatically. That is, the matrix element :math:`\langle o_2, \mathbf{R} | \mathcal{H} | o_1, \mathbf{0} \rangle` does not have to be added manually.  .. note:: This means that adding a hopping of overlap :math:`\epsilon` between an orbital and itself in the home unit cell increases the orbitals on-site energy by :math:`2 \epsilon`. scenario_design.scenario_description_raw:
触发: 准垂直GaN PiN达到高反向电压但漏电随器件尺寸变化，需决定侧壁工艺是否具备产品资格
对象：20/36/72 um器件反向I-V、侧壁处理/斜角版本、漏电对1/R缩放、VBR/Ron,sp和TCAD电场图

environment.description:
触发: F离子注入终端高压结果良好，但仅凭击穿电压无法判断电势横向扩展来自表面化学还是体陷阱补偿
对象：注入前后AFM/XPS、TEM、SRP/C-AFM、电势扫描、SBD反向I-V及TCAD空间电荷模型
目标：把表面氮空位导电和体内受主陷阱两种作用分别校准，决定终端模型是否可用于高压设计
输入：N/Ga化学比、表面粗糙度、深度电阻/电流、50 V表面电势、终端结构、TCAD受主/施主陷阱参数
步骤/决策：先以AFM/XPS确认注入粗糙和N缺陷，以SRP/C-AFM确认表面比体区更导电；再将受主陷阱和400 nm N缺陷表层分别纳入TCAD并拟合50 V表面电势；若只拟合击穿却无法复现电势分布，模型不得用于终端尺寸放行；通过SBD反向I-V和场峰位置确认终端是否将峰场移入体区
验收：表面化学、深度导电、电势曲线和TCAD版本逐样品追溯；只凭VBR不能宣称终端模型已校准；项目阈值独立定义

basic_info.name: SiC MOSFET终端场环改版后以HTRB后态确认数值模型资格

environment.description:
触发: 终端区HTRB后BV漂移，拟调整场环间距和外环数量
对象：旧/新终端几何、校准TCAD模型、HTRB前后BV/漏电实测和批次信息
目标：判断终端结构修订是否真正改善应力后电场/击穿稳定性，并界定TCAD预测适用范围
输入：场环几何和掺杂、材料/陷阱参数、TCAD网格及电场/BV输出、HTRB前后实测及产品规格
步骤/决策：用同一物理模型和边界条件仿真旧/新终端的电场与BV，并检查终端尖角/界面附近局部网格收敛；将模型预测与独立器件的初态及HTRB后态BV/漏电对比；若静态仿真改善而后态未改善或漂移超项目规格，则拒绝以仿真放行，修订陷阱/老化机制或设计并补试验；通过仅限已验证应力包络
验收：预测与独立初态/HTRB后态数据均满足项目容差，局部网格收敛且数据批次可追溯；论文报告的2%仅属于其特定器件，不作本项目阈值

basic_info.name: SiC槽栅短路模型的单次拟合与重复脉冲外推分级

environment.description:
触发: 用匹配单次短路电流的TCAD模型筛选对称或非对称槽栅结构，并准备声称重复应力可靠性
对象：两种槽栅结构TCAD、单次短路波形、重复脉冲后的电参数与失效位置记录
目标：明确模型仅能支持单次短路性能还是也能预测重复脉冲退化，阻止无后态数据的外推
输入：几何/网格、热/雪崩/迁移率模型、脉冲条件、单次实测波形、重复应力次数与Vth/Ron/电容/BV序列
步骤/决策：先以独立单次波形验证短路峰值和衰减时序，并检查热热点网格/时间步敏感性；记录模型中衬底厚度等简化假设；对重复脉冲后态逐项比较Vth、Ron、电容和BV趋势及结构间排序；若仅单次吻合而重复退化不吻合或未建老化机制，则限制模型为单次决策并要求实测重复应力，不把外推曲线写成可靠性验证
验收：各声明适用脉冲条件下单次波形与重复后态指标分别满足项目容差；未测重复应力或缺退化机制时仅可发布单次资格；数值网格/时间步敏感性和几何简化记录齐全

对象：两种槽栅结构TCAD、单次短路波形、重复脉冲后的电参数与失效位置记录
目标：明确模型仅能支持单次短路性能还是也能预测重复脉冲退化，阻止无后态数据的外推
输入：几何/网格、热/雪崩/迁移率模型、脉冲条件、单次实测波形、重复应力次数与Vth/Ron/电容/BV序列
步骤/决策：先以独立单次波形验证短路峰值和衰减时序，并检查热热点网格/时间步敏感性；记录模型中衬底厚度等简化假设；对重复脉冲后态逐项比较Vth、Ron、电容和BV趋势及结构间排序；若仅单次吻合而重复退化不吻合或未建老化机制，则限制模型为单次决策并要求实测重复应力，不把外推曲线写成可靠性验证
验收：各声明适用脉冲条件下单次波形与重复后态指标分别满足项目容差；未测重复应力或缺退化机制时仅可发布单次资格；数值网格/时间步敏感性和几何简化记录齐全

Python核心操作/决策：Python对齐TCAD与实测电流波形，分析重复应力后参数轨迹和模型偏差；真正电热/雪崩求解依赖原生商业TCAD

basic_info.name: GaN高功率偏置模型的空间自热适用域放行

environment.description:
触发: 器件模型已在低/中漏偏置下拟合I-V，拟用于高功率或不同栅偏置下评估热风险
对象：同版图/层结构器件的已校准电学模型、热边界与材料参数、目标Vds/Vgs域及可获得的温度映射
目标：界定模型可用于哪些高功率偏置点；无法复现实测温升/热点时暂停模型外推并补热边界或实测

environment.description:
触发: 已有陷阱/电荷捕获TCAD模型准备预测不同门偏置极性、应力保持时间或温度下的阈值漂移与恢复
对象：带陷阱动力学候选模型、相同器件的初始转移曲线、正/负门应力和解除后Vt时间轨迹
目标：确认模型只在有实测支持的应力-温度-读出时间域使用，并决定补测、重估陷阱时间常数或HOLD
输入：应力/恢复电压时序、温度、Vt读出延迟、原始Id-Vg及恒定亚阈值形状验证、TCAD预测轨迹与参数版本
步骤/决策：固定Vt提取定义和读出延迟，核对由电流换算Vt时的亚阈值不变假设；分别比较正负应力的漂移方向、幅度、起始/恢复时间及温度趋势；若模型只拟合长期终点却错过快速恢复或极性反转，则限制使用域并要求短时测量或重新标定动力学；数据无法区分陷阱位置时保留多机制假设，不把单条Vt轨迹确认为具体界面缺陷
验收：模型与实测用同一Vt定义、时序和温度；目标域的漂移方向、时间形状和恢复均满足项目容差；短时读出缺失或换算假设不成立时不得声明模型可预测；固定数据比较不证明新模型实际有效

environment.description:
触发: TCAD优化的LVTSCR或类似钳位已在硅片上制成，准备证明其既能触发保护IO又不在正常偏置下保持闩锁
对象：钳位版图和寄生PNP/NPN路径模型、受保护IO的工作/损伤边界、TLP与应力后漏电实测
目标：决定钳位结构在目标IO电压域可用、需返工还是证据不足，并将TCAD路径解释和硅测阈值分开
输入：TCAD瞬态电流密度与结构版本、TLP逐脉冲I-V/Vt1/Vh/It2、脉冲上升和宽度、应力后漏电、IO工作电压及氧化层/输出级损伤限
步骤/决策：先核对TCAD与流片结构/端口方向一致；从TLP原始曲线识别初始触发、一次/二次snapback、保持与It2，并检查逐级应力后漏电；把实测Vt1/Vh/It2与该产品的IO正常工作和损伤窗口比对；Vh落入正常工作区、触发高于被保护级损伤条件或漏电异常时阻断放行；若实测转折与TCAD寄生BJT/分支路径解释不符，回查结构与模型而非用模拟电流图替代TLP结论
验收：每个阈值可回链原始TLP脉冲和应力后漏电；产品自有工作/损伤窗口已批准；TCAD路径与实测分开记录；若只有模拟没有硅测则仅报告设计候选

触发: TCAD预测器件在辐射环境下有SEB敏感偏置点，目标应用需要确定重离子条件下的可用漏偏置域
对象：额定功率MOSFET结构、重离子LET/入射条件、基准漏偏置与预后测漏电、TCAD电荷沉积和电热模型
目标：把实测SEB阈值与TCAD瞬态电流/热点预测对照，划定被实测支持的偏置与LET域或HOLD
输入：离子种类/LET/通量/入射位置和角度、VDS/VGS、每次事件电流时序、前后漏电与功能检查、TCAD模型/网格/参数、产品辐射需求
步骤/决策：按离子与偏置条件分组核对样品状态；从实测不可恢复漏电/电流定义SEB事件区间，并与同一条件TCAD非恢复电流尾与内部热点比较；若模拟阈值偏高或缺入射位置/角度覆盖，则限制TCAD用于已测域并请求补辐照，不以单个仿真阈值给出整产品耐受电压；设计加固仅有模拟收益时保持下一版候选，不宣布实测通过
验收：每个实测-模拟对应点同时记录LET、离子、通量、位置/角度、VGS/VDS、样本量、失效定义和前后漏电；未覆盖条件输出HOLD，模拟加固不得称已辐照验证。

basic_info.name: SiC MOSFET雪崩模型由单次UIS向重复应力域转移的资格审查

environment.description:
触发: 单次UIS的雪崩能量或TCAD冲击电离结果已取得，系统应用却有重复感性关断脉冲
对象：同结构SiC沟槽MOSFET的单次/重复UIS实测、负载电感、起始电流、环境温度、失效后电测/解封和TCAD冲击电离模型
目标：界定模型是否可用于重复雪崩应力下的器件性能与失效风险，或要求额外循环/失效证据
输入：逐次IDS/VDS雪崩波形、L与脉宽/占空比、Eav计算条件、循环前后Vth/Ron/Igss/体二极管压降、TCAD场/冲击电离分布、解封失效位置
步骤/决策：先用同一L、初始电流、温度和波形定义比较单次UIS的Eav/雪崩持续时间与TCAD；再在已批准的重复脉冲条件下跟踪参数漂移和门漏/体二极管失效，并核对模型高场/冲击电离热点与物理解封；若单次匹配但重复漂移或失效机制未再现，则将模型限定为单次条件并暂停重复域结论；新台阶氧化层等结构仅有仿真收益时列为待流片验证
验收：单次与重复UIS按同一结构和受控L、初始电流、温度/冷却、脉宽/占空比独立验收；没有重复电参/失效证据时不发布重复域模型。

basic_info.name: 横截面EBIC边界误设后的表面/体复合分流

environment.description:
触发: 横截面EBIC拟合得到异常低收集率或复合参数随束能改变，而模型仍沿用二维PN结的周期上下边界或忽略暴露样品表面
对象：有CdS/CdTe等横截面EBIC/CL束位与束能扫描、样品制备方式、二维器件几何及初始漂移扩散模型；表面复合和接触边界处理待核对

basic_info.name: SiC MOSFET反向导通浪涌模型向失效后阻断能力的资格交接

environment.description:
触发: 1.2 kV SiC MOSFET模型拟用于反向导通浪涌额定或选型，已有静态转移/体二极管曲线拟合但尚未确认脉冲后阻断能力
对象：器件结构与TCAD版本、体二极管及沟道反向导通路径、20 ms浪涌波形、逐级浪涌前后静态参数和失效解剖记录
目标：划定反向导通浪涌模型可支持的电流/门极状态/器件结构范围，并决定额定使用、降额或暂缓放行
输入：两种Vgs状态下实测I(t)/Vsd(t)、脉冲宽度和温度、逐级应力后Vgs漏电/体二极管正向压降/反向阻断、TCAD电流密度与温升、解剖照片及器件批次
步骤/决策：先核静态模型与同结构未应力样品；按实测波形分别比较栅关/开TCAD与实测，再逐级核门源漏电、二极管正向与反向阻断。若项目样品呈现逐级劣化则按实测另行调查；若到最大浪涌才突变则记录失效边界和解剖证据。按项目额定、温度/波形及批准限值决定降额、暂停或补测，不移植论文约5倍额定值。
验收：每个拟放行Vgs状态和浪涌波形都有同结构实测与仿真对照及逐级应力后阻断检查；门源短路或体二极管阻断劣化必须按产品限值触发降额或暂停；仅把论文约5倍额定电流作为该样本观察，不移植成通用限值

init_ref_tools.name: Sweep
init_ref_tools.description: A parameter sweep over the input variables of one input file.  One simulation is run for every combination of the swept values, combined as a Cartesian product: sweeping two variables with 3 and 4 values gives 12 simulations.  Building and running are separate steps. `save()` writes one input file per combination, and `execute()` runs those files and collects their output. Calling `execute()` on a sweep that was never saved does not raise: it warns that no input files were created and returns.  Parameters ---------- variables_to_sweep : dict of {str : list} Values to sweep for each input variable, keyed by variable name, as `{'name1': values1, 'name2': values2}`. Every name must already be a variable of the input file, and every value must be iterable. A single string counts as iterable and sweeps its characters, so wrap single values in a list. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the input file to sweep, as for `InputFile`. Without it there are no variables to sweep over, so only an empty `variables_to_sweep` is accepted. configpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the config file, as for `InputFile`. It is handed to every input file the sweep generates, so they all run on the same configuration as the sweep itself.  Attributes ---------- input_file : InputFileTemplate The prototype input file whose variables are swept, parsed once at construction. var_sweep : dict of {str : list} The validated `variables_to_sweep`, keyed by variable name. input_files : list of InputFileTemplate One input file per swept combination. Empty until `save()` has run, which replaces the list on every call. sweep_output_directory : str Directory holding the output of every simulation of the sweep. None until `execute()` has run. sweep_infodict : DictList of dict Variable combination of each generated input file, keyed by that file's path. Empty until `save()` has run. sweep_output_infodict : DictList of dict The same combinations keyed by output folder instead. This is what is written to `sweep_infodict.json` in the sweep directory. Empty until `execute()` has run. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the input file being swept. Read-only. filename_only : str File name of the input file without the extension. Read-only. product : str Detected nextnano product of the input file. Read-only. config : NNConfig The configuration `.input_file` runs on. Settable, but the assignment reaches only `.input_file`: the files `save()` generates take their configuration from the `configpath` given at construction. configpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the configuration file behind `.config`. Read-only.  Raises ------ ValueError If a name in `variables_to_sweep` is not a variable of the input file. TypeError If a value in `variables_to_sweep` is not iterable.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, variables_to_sweep, fullpath = None, configpath = None

function.name: save_sweep
function.description: Write and save on disk one input file per swept combination.  `save()` is the preferred name for this method. `save_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.

delete_old_files.description: If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched.

round_decimal.description: Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. Values that are strings are used as they are.

integer_only_in_name.description: If True, name the files after the input file with an index appended (`example_0.in`, `example_1.in`, ...) instead of after the swept values.

temp.description: If True, write the files into a temporary folder that is removed when the process exits, instead of next to the input file.

variables_comb_screen_fn.description: Filter for the combinations to generate. It is called with one combination of values at a time, in the order of the swept variables, and the combination is kept when the call returns true. If omitted, every combination is generated.

The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_old_files : bool, default=True If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched. round_decimal : int, default=8 Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. See Also -------- save : Preferred name for this method.

In a future patch the two will swap: ``save`` will hold the implementation and ``save_sweep`` will become the mirror, emitting a deprecation warning.

function.name: create_input_files

function.name: execute_sweep
function.description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.

delete_input_files.description: If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed.

overwrite.description: If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart.

show_log.description: If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way.

convergenceCheck.description: If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`.

convergence_check_mode.description: What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script.

parallel_limit.description: Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine.

separate_sweep_dir.description: If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory.

kwargs.description: Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`.

function.ori_description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_input_files : bool, default=False If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed. overwrite : bool, default=False If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart. show_log : bool, default=True If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way. convergenceCheck : bool, default=False If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`. convergence_check_mode : {'pause', 'terminate', 'continue'} What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script. parallel_limit : int, default=1 Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine. separate_sweep_dir : bool, default=True If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory. **kwargs : dict Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`. Nothing is executed, but the sweep directory has already been created.  See Also -------- InputFile.execute : Meaning of the arguments passed on to each simulation. execute : Preferred name for this method.

basic_info.name: 太赫兹QCL阈值偏差的寄生注入与模型误差分流

environment.description:
触发: THz量子级联激光器样品的阈值电流、I-V或反演相关量与同结构输运模拟不一致。
对象：具有层厚、掺杂、周期、偏压和量测数据的已制器件；同结构的能级/波函数、注入分流、载流子占据和电流模拟已获得或待补算。
目标：对已制THz QCL的阈值/I-V与同结构模型预测差异作证据分流，区分可观察的寄生注入线索与尚未确认的模型、接触或生长解释。
输入：外延层厚/成分/掺杂及误差、温度-偏压-I-V/阈值量测、能级与反交叉、上下激光能级占据、注入效率、散射/展宽模型版本。
步骤/决策：先核对样品、层序、掺杂、偏压/温度及模拟版本；分别比较模型预测的能级反交叉、寄生注入、上/下能级占据或反演估计与实际可测阈值/I-V。只有存在可比提取方法时才对照实验反演估计。差异存在时记录载流子密度、展宽、有效面积、寄生电阻和生长厚度等备选解释，并指定可区分的补模拟或独立量测；无新证据时保持根因未归因，不把寄生注入相关性自动确认为样品失效根因。
验收：结构/偏压/温度定义和模型版本可追溯；实测量与模型量不得混称，实验反演仅在提取方法、假设和不确定度可查时比较；每个候选根因有鉴别所需的新证据，缺证不判定制造失效。

init_ref_tools.name: Sweep
init_ref_tools.description: A parameter sweep over the input variables of one input file.  One simulation is run for every combination of the swept values, combined as a Cartesian product: sweeping two variables with 3 and 4 values gives 12 simulations.  Building and running are separate steps. `save()` writes one input file per combination, and `execute()` runs those files and collects their output. Calling `execute()` on a sweep that was never saved does not raise: it warns that no input files were created and returns.  Parameters ---------- variables_to_sweep : dict of {str : list} Values to sweep for each input variable, keyed by variable name, as `{'name1': values1, 'name2': values2}`. Every name must already be a variable of the input file, and every value must be iterable. A single string counts as iterable and sweeps its characters, so wrap single values in a list. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the input file to sweep, as for `InputFile`. Without it there are no variables to sweep over, so only an empty `variables_to_sweep` is accepted. configpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the config file, as for `InputFile`. It is handed to every input file the sweep generates, so they all run on the same configuration as the sweep itself.  Attributes ---------- input_file : InputFileTemplate The prototype input file whose variables are swept, parsed once at construction. var_sweep : dict of {str : list} The validated `variables_to_sweep`, keyed by variable name. input_files : list of InputFileTemplate One input file per swept combination. Empty until `save()` has run, which replaces the list on every call. sweep_output_directory : str Directory holding the output of every simulation of the sweep. None until `execute()` has run. sweep_infodict : DictList of dict Variable combination of each generated input file, keyed by that file's path. Empty until `save()` has run. sweep_output_infodict : DictList of dict The same combinations keyed by output folder instead. This is what is written to `sweep_infodict.json` in the sweep directory. Empty until `execute()` has run. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the input file being swept. Read-only. filename_only : str File name of the input file without the extension. Read-only. product : str Detected nextnano product of the input file. Read-only. config : NNConfig The configuration `.input_file` runs on. Settable, but the assignment reaches only `.input_file`: the files `save()` generates take their configuration from the `configpath` given at construction. configpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the configuration file behind `.config`. Read-only.  Raises ------ ValueError If a name in `variables_to_sweep` is not a variable of the input file. TypeError If a value in `variables_to_sweep` is not iterable.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, variables_to_sweep, fullpath = None, configpath = None

function.name: save_sweep
function.description: Write and save on disk one input file per swept combination.  `save()` is the preferred name for this method. `save_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.

delete_old_files.description: If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched.

round_decimal.description: Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. Values that are strings are used as they are.

integer_only_in_name.description: If True, name the files after the input file with an index appended (`example_0.in`, `example_1.in`, ...) instead of after the swept values.

temp.description: If True, write the files into a temporary folder that is removed when the process exits, instead of next to the input file.

variables_comb_screen_fn.description: Filter for the combinations to generate. It is called with one combination of values at a time, in the order of the swept variables, and the combination is kept when the call returns true. If omitted, every combination is generated.

function.ori_input: self, delete_old_files = True, round_decimal = 8, integer_only_in_name = False, temp = False, variables_comb_screen_fn: Callable[..., Any] = None
function.ori_description: Write and save on disk one input file per swept combination.  `save()` is the preferred name for this method. `save_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_old_files : bool, default=True If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched. round_decimal : int, default=8 Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. Values that are strings are used as they are. integer_only_in_name : bool, default=False If True, name the files after the input file with an index appended (`example_0.in`, `example_1.in`, ...) instead of after the swept values. temp : bool, default=False If True, write the files into a temporary folder that is removed when the process exits, instead of next to the input file. variables_comb_screen_fn : callable, default=None Filter for the combinations to generate. It is called with one combination of values at a time, in the order of the swept variables, and the combination is kept when the call returns true. If omitted, every combination is generated.  See Also -------- save : Preferred name for this method.

function.name: save
function.description: Save the sweep input files. See :meth:`save_sweep` for the parameters.
function.ori_description: Save the sweep input files. See :meth:`save_sweep` for the parameters.  Notes ----- This is the preferred name. For now it simply forwards to :meth:`save_sweep`. In a future patch the two will swap: ``save`` will hold the implementation and ``save_sweep`` will become the mirror, emitting a deprecation warning.

function.name: create_input_files
function.ori_input: self, input_file_path, round_decimal, integer_only_in_name = False, variables_comb_screen_fn: Callable[..., Any] = None

function.name: execute_sweep
function.description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.

delete_input_files.description: If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed.

overwrite.description: If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart.

show_log.description: If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way.

convergenceCheck.description: If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`.

convergence_check_mode.description: What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script.

parallel_limit.description: Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine.

separate_sweep_dir.description: If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory.

kwargs.description: Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`.

function.ori_input: self, delete_input_files = False, overwrite = False, show_log = True, convergenceCheck = False, convergence_check_mode = 'pause', parallel_limit = 1, separate_sweep_dir = True, **kwargs
function.ori_description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_input_files : bool, default=False If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed. overwrite : bool, default=False If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart. show_log : bool, default=True If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way. convergenceCheck : bool, default=False If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`. convergence_check_mode : {'pause', 'terminate', 'continue'} What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script. parallel_limit : int, default=1 Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine. separate_sweep_dir : bool, default=True If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory. **kwargs : dict Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`.  Raises ------ RuntimeError If `convergenceCheck` is True and a simulation did not converge, unless `convergence_check_mode` is 'continue'. The sweep stops at that simulation and the remaining input files are not executed.  Warns ----- UserWarning If no input files were created, i.e. `save()` has not been called. Nothing is executed, but the sweep directory has already been created.  See Also -------- InputFile.execute : Meaning of the arguments passed on to each simulation. execute : Preferred name for this method.

init_ref_tools.name: Sweep
init_ref_tools.description: A parameter sweep over the input variables of one input file.  One simulation is run for every combination of the swept values, combined as a Cartesian product: sweeping two variables with 3 and 4 values gives 12 simulations.  Building and running are separate steps. `save()` writes one input file per combination, and `execute()` runs those files and collects their output. Calling `execute()` on a sweep that was never saved does not raise: it warns that no input files were created and returns.  Parameters ---------- variables_to_sweep : dict of {str : list} Values to sweep for each input variable, keyed by variable name, as `{'name1': values1, 'name2': values2}`. Every name must already be a variable of the input file, and every value must be iterable. A single string counts as iterable and sweeps its characters, so wrap single values in a list. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the input file to sweep, as for `InputFile`. Without it there are no variables to sweep over, so only an empty `variables_to_sweep` is accepted. configpath : str or pathlib.Path, default=None Path to the config file, as for `InputFile`. It is handed to every input file the sweep generates, so they all run on the same configuration as the sweep itself.  Attributes ---------- input_file : InputFileTemplate The prototype input file whose variables are swept, parsed once at construction. var_sweep : dict of {str : list} The validated `variables_to_sweep`, keyed by variable name. input_files : list of InputFileTemplate One input file per swept combination. Empty until `save()` has run, which replaces the list on every call. sweep_output_directory : str Directory holding the output of every simulation of the sweep. None until `execute()` has run. sweep_infodict : DictList of dict Variable combination of each generated input file, keyed by that file's path. Empty until `save()` has run. sweep_output_infodict : DictList of dict The same combinations keyed by output folder instead. This is what is written to `sweep_infodict.json` in the sweep directory. Empty until `execute()` has run. fullpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the input file being swept. Read-only. filename_only : str File name of the input file without the extension. Read-only. product : str Detected nextnano product of the input file. Read-only. config : NNConfig The configuration `.input_file` runs on. Settable, but the assignment reaches only `.input_file`: the files `save()` generates take their configuration from the `configpath` given at construction. configpath : str or pathlib.Path Path of the configuration file behind `.config`. Read-only.  Raises ------ ValueError If a name in `variables_to_sweep` is not a variable of the input file. TypeError If a value in `variables_to_sweep` is not iterable.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, variables_to_sweep, fullpath = None, configpath = None

function.name: save_sweep
function.description: Write and save on disk one input file per swept combination.  `save()` is the preferred name for this method. `save_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.

delete_old_files.description: If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched.

round_decimal.description: Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. Values that are strings are used as they are.

integer_only_in_name.description: If True, name the files after the input file with an index appended (`example_0.in`, `example_1.in`, ...) instead of after the swept values.

temp.description: If True, write the files into a temporary folder that is removed when the process exits, instead of next to the input file.

variables_comb_screen_fn.description: Filter for the combinations to generate. It is called with one combination of values at a time, in the order of the swept variables, and the combination is kept when the call returns true. If omitted, every combination is generated.

function.ori_input: self, delete_old_files = True, round_decimal = 8, integer_only_in_name = False, temp = False, variables_comb_screen_fn: Callable[..., Any] = None
function.ori_description: Write and save on disk one input file per swept combination.  `save()` is the preferred name for this method. `save_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  The files are written next to the input file being swept, with the swept values appended to the name (`example__BIAS_1.5_.in`), and are collected in `.input_files` and `.sweep_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_old_files : bool, default=True If True, delete the input files generated by an earlier `save()` on this sweep before writing the new ones. Files from other sweeps are never touched. round_decimal : int, default=8 Number of decimals the swept values are rounded to in the file names. Values that are strings are used as they are. integer_only_in_name : bool, default=False If True, name the files after the input file with an index appended (`example_0.in`, `example_1.in`, ...) instead of after the swept values. temp : bool, default=False If True, write the files into a temporary folder that is removed when the process exits, instead of next to the input file. variables_comb_screen_fn : callable, default=None Filter for the combinations to generate. It is called with one combination of values at a time, in the order of the swept variables, and the combination is kept when the call returns true. If omitted, every combination is generated.  See Also -------- save : Preferred name for this method.

function.name: save
function.description: Save the sweep input files. See :meth:`save_sweep` for the parameters.
function.ori_description: Save the sweep input files. See :meth:`save_sweep` for the parameters.  Notes ----- This is the preferred name. For now it simply forwards to :meth:`save_sweep`. In a future patch the two will swap: ``save`` will hold the implementation and ``save_sweep`` will become the mirror, emitting a deprecation warning.

function.name: create_input_files
function.ori_input: self, input_file_path, round_decimal, integer_only_in_name = False, variables_comb_screen_fn: Callable[..., Any] = None

function.name: execute_sweep
function.description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.

delete_input_files.description: If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed.

overwrite.description: If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart.

show_log.description: If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way.

convergenceCheck.description: If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`.

convergence_check_mode.description: What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script.

parallel_limit.description: Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine.

separate_sweep_dir.description: If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory.

kwargs.description: Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`.

function.ori_input: self, delete_input_files = False, overwrite = False, show_log = True, convergenceCheck = False, convergence_check_mode = 'pause', parallel_limit = 1, separate_sweep_dir = True, **kwargs
function.ori_description: Execute the input files written by `save()`.  `execute()` is the preferred name for this method. `execute_sweep()` is kept for compatibility and will be deprecated.  Each input file is run in turn, or `parallel_limit` at a time. The output is collected under `.sweep_output_directory` together with `sweep_info.txt` and `sweep_infodict.json`, and every simulation's variable combination is recorded in `.sweep_output_infodict`.  Parameters ---------- delete_input_files : bool, default=False If True, delete the generated input files once they have been executed. overwrite : bool, default=False If True, the output overwrites the old output data. If False, execution creates a new output folder, adding an integer to the folder name. It applies to the sweep folder and to the folder of every simulation in it, so a sweep run with `overwrite=False` writes over no earlier output at either level. The per-file subfolder itself is always created: it is what keeps the sweep points apart. show_log : bool, default=True If True, the simulation log is displayed in the console. If False, only the count of the current simulation is displayed. The log file is written to the output folder either way. convergenceCheck : bool, default=False If True, check the log of every simulation for convergence once it has finished. What happens on a simulation that did not converge is decided by `convergence_check_mode`. convergence_check_mode : {'pause', 'terminate', 'continue'} What to do when a simulation did not converge. Only used when `convergenceCheck` is True.  - 'pause': ask the user how to proceed. If no interactive terminal is attached (e.g. CI, cluster jobs), behaves like 'terminate' instead of blocking on input. - 'terminate': terminate the script. - 'continue': notify the user but continue the script. parallel_limit : int, default=1 Number of simulations to run simultaneously. Especially useful for simple simulations, which may run more efficiently in parallel. Be aware that some nextnano solvers parallelize computations internally in threads (controlled by `threads` in the nextnanopy configuration): to avoid an undesirable slowdown, keep `parallel_limit * threads` at or below the number of physical cores of the machine. separate_sweep_dir : bool, default=True If True, create one directory for the sweep and put every simulation's output folder inside it. If False, the output folders are created directly in the output directory. **kwargs : dict Forwarded to `InputFile.execute()` for every simulation. `outputdirectory` is the exception: it is taken as the parent of the sweep directory rather than passed on, and defaults to the `outputdirectory` of `.config`.  Raises ------ RuntimeError If `convergenceCheck` is True and a simulation did not converge, unless `convergence_check_mode` is 'continue'. The sweep stops at that simulation and the remaining input files are not executed.  Warns ----- UserWarning If no input files were created, i.e. `save()` has not been called. Nothing is executed, but the sweep directory has already been created.  See Also -------- InputFile.execute : Meaning of the arguments passed on to each simulation. execute : Preferred name for this method.

场景要求：触发: 拟改变QCL注入/抽取架构或目标工作温度，候选两阱周期结构需要在流片前比较增益与稳定传输。
对象：候选层序、材料、掺杂与设计偏压；量子态与输运/增益预测需用同一模型版本。

basic_info.name: ZnO电子碰撞电离系数入库后向雪崩光电二极管模型的定向交接

environment.description:
触发: ZnO APD仿真需要电子碰撞电离系数，但现有参数记录缺少晶向、膜结构、提取电场区间或电子/空穴近似说明
对象：候选α(E)数据及来源论文、目标APD材料层与电场方向、增益/击穿模型版本
目标：判定候选ZnO电子碰撞电离参数在目标APD倍增层是否可用，输出带实验假设和适用域的模型参数交接或补测请求

environment.description:
触发: LED效率随注入升高出现droop，原有常数ABC模型无法同时重现实测寿命与IQE，需向器件仿真交付复合参数
对象：同器件/同工况的注入电流密度扫描、小信号频响导出的微分载流子寿命、经校准的绝对IQE及几何/光提取/自热信息
目标：判定注入域内SRH、辐射和高密度非辐射复合模型项是否可辨识，交付有适用范围和不确定度的参数或暂停归因
输入：原始调制频响、微分寿命、绝对IQE与校准来源、注入电流/面积/有效有源层厚度、载流子密度推断、脉冲/温度条件、候选A/B/C及相空间填充或陷阱辅助项
步骤/决策：核对频响到寿命及相对EQE到绝对IQE的测量/校准链，检查脉冲条件下自热和提取效率假设；将寿命与IQE在同一注入密度轴上对齐，分解辐射与非辐射速率；比较常数ABC与允许SRH饱和、辐射相空间填充或缺陷辅助高密度项的模型残差和参数稳定性；若A改变伴随高注入立方项改变而简单ABC不能重现，则将高注入项标为未分离并请求缺陷/样本对照，不能直接写成本征Auger；在实测注入范围及独立条件上复核后输出可用参数或hold
验收：每个复合参数能追溯同一器件的寿命和绝对IQE数据及密度换算；模型同时重现两类响应且留出条件满足项目误差预算；若高注入立方项的缺陷辅助贡献未排除，只能交付合并有效项及限制说明

init_ref_tools.name: OptiStack
init_ref_tools.description: Class that contains an optical structure: a sequence of layers with a thickness and a complex refractive index.  It serves as an intermediate step between solcore layers and materials and the stack of thicknesses and n and k values necessary to run calculations involving TMM. When creating an OptiStack object, the thicknesses of all the layers forming the Solcore structure and the optical data of the materials of the layers are extracted and arranged in such a way they can be easily and fastly read by the TMM functions.  In addition to a solcore structure with Layers, it can also take a list where each element represent a layer written as a list and contains the layer thickness and the dielectrical model, the raw n and k data as a function of wavelengths, or a whole Device structure as the type used in the PDD model.  In summary, this class acepts:  - A solcore structure with layers - A list where each element is [thickness, DielectricModel] - A list where each element is [thickness, wavelength, n, k] - A list mixing the above: [ [thickness, DielectricModel], [thickness, wavelength, n, k], solcore.Layer, solcore.Layer ]  This allows for maximum flexibility when creating the optical model, allowing to construct the stack with experimental data, modelled data and known material properties from the database.  Yet anther way of defining the layers mixes experimental data with a DielectricModel within the same layer but in spectrally distinct regions. The syntaxis for the layer is:  layer = [thickness, wavelength, n, k, DielectricModel, mixing]  where mixing is a list containing three elements: [the mixing point (nm), the mixing width (nm), zero or one] depending if the mixing function should be increasing with the wavelength or decreasing. If increasing (zero), the Dielectric model will be used at long wavelengths and the experimental data at short wavelengths. If decreasing (one) the oposite is done. The mixing point and mixing width control how smooth is the transition between one and the other type of data.  Extra layers such as he semi-infinite, air-like first and last medium, and a back highly absorbing layer are included at runtime to fulfill the requirements of the TMM solver or to solve some of its limitations.

Option is given to indicate if the reflection from the back of the structure must be suppressed, useful for ellipsometry calculations. This is done by creating an artificial highly absorbing but not reflecting layer just at the back.  Alternatively, it can take simply a list of [thickness, DielectricModel] or [thickness, wavelength, n, k] for each layer accounting for the refractive index of the layers. The three options can be mixed for maximum flexibility.

init_ref_tools.name: QWunit
init_ref_tools.description: Assembles a group of layers as a quantum well, calculating its properties as a whole  - It needs a minimum of 3 layers - There must be exactly one layer with the role = "well". - Top and bottom layers are assumed to be the barriers. - Anything not a barrier not a well will be considered as "interlayer".  Since the Poisson - Drift-Diffusion solver can not work with superlattices, there is no point of considering the solution of more than one QW. All QWs entering into the solver are independent, regardless of the width of the barriers.  To account for the possible presence of nearby QWs, perdiodic boundary conditions can be used to solve the Schrodinger equation. If barriers + interlayers are thick enought, this make no difference but if they are thin, it affects the number of confined levels. It does not 'create' minibands, though, so the results with thin barriers must be used with caution.

init_ref_tools.name: solve_tmm
init_ref_tools.description: Calculates the RAT of a solar cell object using the transfer matrix method.  Internally, it creates an OptiStack and then it calculates the optical properties of the whole structure. A substrate can be specified in the SolarCell object, which is treated as a semi-infinite transmission medium. Shading can also be specified (as a fraction).  A coherency_list option can be provided:

wavelength.description: Array of wavelegth at which the optics are calculated.

position.description: Array of positions in the z direction to calculate the absorption vs depth.

BL_correction.description: If is set to True, thick layers (thickness > 10*maximum wavelength) are treated incoherently using the Beer-Lambert law, to avoid the calculation of unphysical interference oscillations in the R/A/T spectra.

theta.description: the polar incidence angle, in degrees, with 0 degrees being normal incidence.

pol.description: the polarization of the light ('s', 'p' or 'u')

zero_threshold.description: when the fraction of incident light absorbed in a layer is less than this value, the absorption profile is completely set to zero for both coherent and incoherent calculations. This is applied on a wavelength-by-wavelength basis and is intended to prevent errors where integrating a weak absorption profile in a layer over many points leads to calculated EQE > total absorption in that layer.

no_back_reflection.description: Sets whether reflections from the back surface are suppressed (if set to True, the default), or taken into account (if set to False).

coherency_list.description: If present, this should have the same number of elements than number of layers (if a Junction contains multiple Layers, each should have its own entry in the coherency list). Each element is either 'c' for coherent treatment of that layer or 'i' for incoherent treatment.

init_ref_tools.ori_input: solar_cell: SolarCell, wavelength: NDArray, position: NDArray, BL_correction: bool = True, theta: float = 0.0, pol: str = 'u', zero_threshold: float = 1e-05, no_back_reflection: bool = True, coherency_list: Optional[List[str]] = None, **kwargs
init_ref_tools.ori_description: Calculates the RAT of a solar cell object using the transfer matrix method.  Internally, it creates an OptiStack and then it calculates the optical properties of the whole structure. A substrate can be specified in the SolarCell object, which is treated as a semi-infinite transmission medium. Shading can also be specified (as a fraction).  A coherency_list option can be provided:  Args: solar_cell: A solar_cell object wavelength: Array of wavelegth at which the optics are calculated. position: Array of positions in the z direction to calculate the absorption vs depth. BL_correction: If is set to True, thick layers (thickness > 10*maximum wavelength) are treated incoherently using the Beer-Lambert law, to avoid the calculation of unphysical interference oscillations in the R/A/T spectra. theta: the polar incidence angle, in degrees, with 0 degrees being normal incidence. pol: the polarization of the light ('s', 'p' or 'u') zero_threshold: when the fraction of incident light absorbed in a layer is less than this value, the absorption profile is completely set to zero for both coherent and incoherent calculations. This is applied on a wavelength-by-wavelength basis and is intended to prevent errors where integrating a weak absorption profile in a layer over many points leads to calculated EQE > total absorption in that layer. no_back_reflection: Sets whether reflections from the back surface are suppressed (if set to True, the default), or taken into account (if set to False). coherency_list: If present, this should have the same number of elements than number of layers (if a Junction contains multiple Layers, each should have its own entry in the coherency list). Each element is either 'c' for coherent treatment of that layer or 'i' for incoherent treatment.  Return: None

init_ref_tools.name: solar_cell_solver
init_ref_tools.description: Solves the properties of a solar cell object  This can be done either calculating its optical properties (R, A and T), its quantum efficiency or its current voltage characteristics in the dark or under illumination. The general options for the solvers are passed as dictionaries or state objects.
init_ref_tools.ori_input: solar_cell: SolarCell, task: str, user_options: Union[Dict, State, None] = None
init_ref_tools.ori_description: Solves the properties of a solar cell object  This can be done either calculating its optical properties (R, A and T), its quantum efficiency or its current voltage characteristics in the dark or under illumination. The general options for the solvers are passed as dictionaries or state objects.  Args: - solar_cell: A solar_cell object - taks: Task to perform. Some of the existing tasks might not be available for all types of junctions. - user_options: A dictionary containing the options for the solver, which will overwrite the default options. basic_info.name: GaN价带模型变更后的空穴迁移率预测资格审查

environment.description:
触发: p-GaN候选应变或赝势/泛函/GW/SOC设置变更后，价带顶部次序和预估空穴迁移率发生变化，准备提出材料/器件设计建议。
对象：同一GaN结构族不同电子态模型的valence band、晶场/SOC分裂、轻/重/分裂空穴分支、电子-声子散射及BTE/Hall输出；实际受应变样品的迁移率未提供。
目标：判断迁移率变化是否由可追溯的价带重排和输运模型共同支撑，还是仅来自计算方法/赝势不一致或未收敛结果；交付有条件的计算预测或补算清单。
输入：结构与应变张量、赝势/泛函/GW和SOC版本、价带标签与k点、晶场/SOC分裂、方向质量、电子-声子矩阵元、漂移/Hall迁移率及散射模型、温度和掺杂假设。
步骤/决策：先核对同一结构/应变定义及SOC所需的非共线/全相对论赝势；比较模型变更前后分裂空穴态与轻/重空穴态的次序和曲率；检查输运使用的带速度、电子-声子散射、Hall因子和温度/掺杂口径与该电子态版本一致；若只替换带隙或SOC标志却沿用旧散射/质量，标记不可比并重算；通过后只提交应变迁移率预测和待实验验证项目，不宣称实际p-GaN器件已改善。
验收：每个迁移率值关联具体电子态和散射输入；分裂能与价带标记、Hall/漂移口径及温度/掺杂一致；迁移率趋势有同方法对照和数值收敛证据；项目容差及实物改善须另由实验/规格确认。

场景要求：触发: p-GaN候选应变或赝势/泛函/GW/SOC设置变更后，价带顶部次序和预估空穴迁移率发生变化，准备提出材料/器件设计建议。
对象：同一GaN结构族不同电子态模型的valence band、晶场/SOC分裂、轻/重/分裂空穴分支、电子-声子散射及BTE/Hall输出；实际受应变样品的迁移率未提供。
目标：判断迁移率变化是否由可追溯的价带重排和输运模型共同支撑，还是仅来自计算方法/赝势不一致或未收敛结果；交付有条件的计算预测或补算清单。
输入：结构与应变张量、赝势/泛函/GW和SOC版本、价带标签与k点、晶场/SOC分裂、方向质量、电子-声子矩阵元、漂移/Hall迁移率及散射模型、温度和掺杂假设。
步骤/决策：先核对同一结构/应变定义及SOC所需的非共线/全相对论赝势；比较模型变更前后分裂空穴态与轻/重空穴态的次序和曲率；检查输运使用的带速度、电子-声子散射、Hall因子和温度/掺杂口径与该电子态版本一致；若只替换带隙或SOC标志却沿用旧散射/质量，标记不可比并重算；通过后只提交应变迁移率预测和待实验验证项目，不宣称实际p-GaN器件已改善。
验收：每个迁移率值关联具体电子态和散射输入；分裂能与价带标记、Hall/漂移口径及温度/掺杂一致；迁移率趋势有同方法对照和数值收敛证据；项目容差及实物改善须另由实验/规格确认。

可合成任务：输入：结构与应变张量、赝势/泛函/GW和SOC版本、价带标签与k点、晶场/SOC分裂、方向质量、电子-声子矩阵元、漂移/Hall迁移率及散射模型、温度和掺杂假设。
Python核心操作/决策：拟议标准库读取固定band/BTE结果表，核对结构/赝势/SOC/散射版本和态次序并输出差异；GW、电子-声子矩阵元及BTE求解不由此纯Python审计层实现。
输出：结构-电子态-散射-BTE版本链、价带排序和迁移率预测对照、不可比设置及补算/实测清单。
可复核验收：每个迁移率值关联具体电子态和散射输入；分裂能与价带标记、Hall/漂移口径及温度/掺杂一致；迁移率趋势有同方法对照和数值收敛证据；项目容差及实物改善须另由实验/规格确认。

basic_info.description: mobilitypy 是面向半导体载流子输运的迁移率计算包，提供体材料与二维电子气中的离化杂质、合金无序、界面粗糙、声学和极性光学声子等散射机制模型，并可组合材料参数、温度和载流子浓度来分析总迁移率及主导散射机制。模型适用范围和材料参数仍需针对具体器件校核。

basic_info.name: 薄膜光电器件TOF瞬态到场依赖迁移率模型的适用性交接

environment.description:
触发: 有机/非晶半导体薄膜的TOF光电流在多个偏压下无清晰平台或拐点，器件模型团队请求迁移率/陷阱相关输运参数
对象：薄膜厚度、电极几何和吸收/激发深度已知的光脉冲瞬态电流，配套偏压/光吸收记录与候选正常或分散输运模型
目标：决定可否用单一飞行时间计算场依赖漂移迁移率，或应以分散/陷阱模型拟合并限制参数用途
输入：暗电流和仪器响应扣除后的I(t)、脉冲能量/波长与吸收深度、厚度及有效电场/偏压、极性、重复测量、时间窗、器件面积和模型边界条件
步骤/决策：核对载流子产生深度是否可近似靠近透明电极、场是否满足使用模型的假设；在各场强下检查线性/对数坐标上的前后transit段和拐点稳定性，复核厚度与偏压缩放；有清晰非分散transit时按几何/场计算迁移率并给不确定度；若脉冲拖尾、深注入或高场非线性明显，则比较含分散指数、生成剖面及陷阱释放的瞬态模型，不能把任意拐点代入简单TOF公式；若候选模型在留出偏压/厚度重放失败，交付unresolved与需补测条件
验收：各参数可追溯原始波形、脉冲和几何/场版本；简单TOF仅在非分散、浅注入及有效边界条件有证据时放行；分散模型需重现实测前后段及留出条件，误差限由项目给定

function.name: get_alloy_params
function.description: This function calculates the parameters for a ternary alloy from its binary component parameters using quadratic interpolation. E.g. for any parameter, P: P_SixGe1-x = x*P_Si + (1-x)*P_Ge - x*(1-x)*P_bowing P_bowing is the quadratic bowing parameter for the parameter P.

system.description: Type of the alloy. E.g. 'ternary'. The default is 'ternary'.

compositions.description: The alloy mole fractions. E.g. x values in Si_xGe_1-x. The default is None. If None, a composition array is generated using `np.linspace(start=0.01, end=0.99, num=101)`.

binaries.description: Name of the corresponding binaries of requested alloy. They should match the names in database. All implemented materials name list can be found in the README. The default is ['AlN', 'GaN'].

alloy.description: The alloy name. The name should match the name in database. All implemented materials name list can be found in the README. Case sensitive. The default is 'AlGaN'.

return.description: Parameters for alloy.

步骤/决策：核对载流子产生深度是否可近似靠近透明电极、场是否满足使用模型的假设；在各场强下检查线性/对数坐标上的前后transit段和拐点稳定性，复核厚度与偏压缩放；有清晰非分散transit时按几何/场计算迁移率并给不确定度；若脉冲拖尾、深注入或高场非线性明显，则比较含分散指数、生成剖面及陷阱释放的瞬态模型，不能把任意拐点代入简单TOF公式；若候选模型在留出偏压/厚度重放失败，交付unresolved与需补测条件

basic_info.name: Hall与SdH分歧下二维沟道迁移率归属复核

environment.description:
触发: InGaN/InN或类似多层异质结的Hall片浓度/迁移率与量子振荡所示界面载流子不一致，准备把迁移率用于沟道设计或报告。
对象：同批/同结构的Hall、低温高磁场磁阻及角度/温度扫描；可能有底层、势垒和表面并行导电；目标2DEG归属尚未确认。
目标：判定报告的是全结构Hall平均输运量还是目标界面2DEG的量子输运量，列出仍不可辨识的散射机制和需补的对照样品。
输入：样品层序和批次、Hall正负磁场数据与几何、磁阻Rxx(B,T,angle)、SdH频谱和Dingle拟合、bare-layer对照、原始单位/温度与磁场范围。
步骤/决策：在同一研究且样品层序/批次可比的证据内分别计算Hall整体输运量和SdH频率/量子迁移率；用角度依赖判二维性并以该研究bare-InN对照辅助频率归属。分别标注Hall与SdH的样品身份、温度、磁场窗口及迁移率定义；同一研究不自动保证同一coupon，不同温度/物理量不直接相减为迁移率损失。频率重叠、角度不足或对照缺失时保留未归属；寿命比仅作散射线索。
验收：每项Hall和SdH结果分别可回链原样品、温度、磁场范围、拟合与对照记录；跨样品或跨温度比较须明确可比性，不用V38-S02另一论文数值作V38-S01对照；不得把Hall输运迁移率与SdH量子迁移率直接相减或把散射线索当唯一根因。

function.name: get_alloy_params
function.description: This function calculates the parameters for a ternary alloy from its binary component parameters using quadratic interpolation. E.g. for any parameter, P: P_SixGe1-x = x*P_Si + (1-x)*P_Ge - x*(1-x)*P_bowing P_bowing is the quadratic bowing parameter for the parameter P.

system.description: Type of the alloy. E.g. 'ternary'. The default is 'ternary'.

compositions.description: The alloy mole fractions. E.g. x values in Si_xGe_1-x. The default is None. If None, a composition array is generated using `np.linspace(start=0.01, end=0.99, num=101)`.

binaries.description: Name of the corresponding binaries of requested alloy. They should match the names in database. All implemented materials name list can be found in the README. The default is ['AlN', 'GaN'].

alloy.description: The alloy name. The name should match the name in database. All implemented materials name list can be found in the README. Case sensitive. The default is 'AlGaN'.

return.description: Parameters for alloy.

environment.description:
触发: MOS栅堆栈、氧化层边界或接触开口设计变更，原网格区域及界面定义已不对应新版截面
对象：新版尺寸表/截面、旧版Gmsh几何、gate/oxide/bulk区域和source/drain/body/gate接触/界面命名契约
目标：生成新版区域相互邻接且接触/界面可识别的原生器件网格，或明确阻断后续物理赋值
输入：受控尺寸与坐标单位、材料区域图、接触开口位置、预期接口对、Gmsh脚本和生成网格
步骤/决策：从受控尺寸表更新gate/oxide/bulk边界并建立共享曲线；生成前检查区域闭合、非重叠、接触所属外边界和预期内部界面；生成后逐项对照Physical Surface/Line及DEVSIM绑定名称；缺少gate-oxide或bulk-oxide界面、接触错区、区域交叠或单位不明时阻断交接并返修几何；保留几何、网格与标签字典版本。此处只验收拓扑契约，薄层分辨率另由U41-002检查。
验收：每个预期区域在输出原生网格中非空、闭合且不重叠；每个接触只附着于批准的外边界，内部界面连接指定相邻区域；尺寸/单位与标签绑定可追溯。任何缺项不得进入物理赋值；本验收不证明薄区分辨率或PDE/I-V收敛。

场景要求：触发: MOS栅堆栈、氧化层边界或接触开口设计变更，原网格区域及界面定义已不对应新版截面
对象：新版尺寸表/截面、旧版Gmsh几何、gate/oxide/bulk区域和source/drain/body/gate接触/界面命名契约
目标：生成新版区域相互邻接且接触/界面可识别的原生器件网格，或明确阻断后续物理赋值
输入：受控尺寸与坐标单位、材料区域图、接触开口位置、预期接口对、Gmsh脚本和生成网格
步骤/决策：从受控尺寸表更新gate/oxide/bulk边界并建立共享曲线；生成前检查区域闭合、非重叠、接触所属外边界和预期内部界面；生成后逐项对照Physical Surface/Line及DEVSIM绑定名称；缺少gate-oxide或bulk-oxide界面、接触错区、区域交叠或单位不明时阻断交接并返修几何；保留几何、网格与标签字典版本。此处只验收拓扑契约，薄层分辨率另由U41-002检查。
验收：每个预期区域在输出原生网格中非空、闭合且不重叠；每个接触只附着于批准的外边界，内部界面连接指定相邻区域；尺寸/单位与标签绑定可追溯。任何缺项不得进入物理赋值；本验收不证明薄区分辨率或PDE/I-V收敛。

输出：新版原生网格、区域-接触-界面邻接与缺项表、放行或返修决定；不声称方程已收敛或I-V合格
可复核验收：每个预期区域在输出原生网格中非空、闭合且不重叠；每个接触只附着于批准的外边界，内部界面连接指定相邻区域；尺寸/单位与标签绑定可追溯。任何缺项不得进入物理赋值；本验收不证明薄区分辨率或PDE/I-V收敛。

environment.description:

basic_info.name: 器件网格交接时核验区域与接触标签

environment.description:
触发: 器件网格需从 Gmsh MSH 转给另一求解器，目标格式或标签编码不同
对象：已有带节点、单元、区域和接触边界标记的源网格；下游求解器格式与单位约定待核对
目标：交付下游可读、几何拓扑和物理标签可追溯的网格，或给出阻断交接的差异清单

basic_info.name: gmsh
basic_info.description: Gmsh 是具有几何建模、二维及三维有限元网格生成和前后处理功能的开源工具，其 Python API 可构建几何实体、定义物理分组、设置网格尺寸、生成并查询节点和单元，以及读写网格文件。本次作为网格生成后端整理；用于 DEVSIM 时需匹配 MSH 格式及器件区域、接触和界面标签。

basic_info.name: meshio
basic_info.description: meshio 是面向多种网格格式的 Python 读写和转换库，使用统一的节点、单元块、点数据、单元数据及集合表示，支持 Gmsh、VTK、VTU、XDMF 等文件及时间序列数据交换。它可连接网格生成和数值分析流程，本身不生成网格，也不求解半导体物理方程。

init_ref_tools.name: SimRunner
init_ref_tools.description: The SimRunner class implements all the methods required for launching batches of Spice simulations.  It is iterable, but with a catch: The iteration will only return the completed tasks (succeeded or not), in the order they were completed. If all completed tasks have been returned, and there are still running tasks, it will wait for the completion of the next task. If you used no callbacks, the result is a tuple with the raw and log file names. If you used callbacks, it will return the return code of the callback function, or None if there was an error. Also see `sim_info()` for more details on the completed tasks.  :param simulator: Forcing a given simulator executable. :type simulator: Simulator, optional :param parallel_sims: Defines the number of parallel simulations that can be executed at the same time. Ideally this number should be aligned to the number of CPUs (processor cores) available on the machine. :type parallel_sims: int, optional :param timeout: Timeout parameter as specified on the OS subprocess.run() function. Default is 600 seconds, i.e. 10 minutes. For no timeout, set to None. :type timeout: float, optional :param verbose: If True, it enables a richer printout of the program execution. :type verbose: bool, optional :param output_folder: specifying which directory shall be used for simulation files (raw and log files). :type output_folder: str, optional :param cwd: The current working directory to run the command in. If None, no change will be done of the working directory. :type cwd: str or pathlib.Path, optional  :raises FileNotFoundError: When the file is not found. !This will be changed.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes a simulation run with the conditions set by the user. Conditions are set by the set_parameter, set_component_value or add_instruction functions.

netlist.description: The name of the netlist can be optionally overridden if the user wants to have a better control of how the simulations files are generated.

wait_resource.description: Setting this parameter to False will force the simulation to start immediately, irrespective of the number of simulations already active. By default, the SimRunner class uses only four processors. This number can be overridden by setting the parameter ´parallel_sims´ to a different number. If there are more than ´parallel_sims´ simulations being done, the new one will be placed on hold till one of the other simulations are finished.

callback.description: The user can optionally give a callback function for when the simulation finishes so that processing can be done immediately. The callback can either be a function or a class derived from ProcessCallback. A callback function must receive two at least input parameters that correspond the raw and log files created by the simulation. These need to be the first two parameters of the callback function. The other parameters are passed as a dictionary or a tuple in the callback_args parameter. If the callback is a class derived from ProcessCallback, then the callback is executed in a separate process. The callback function must be defined in the callback() method of the class. As for the callback function, the first two parameters are the raw and log files. The other parameters are passed as dictionary in the callback_args parameter.

callback_args.description: The callback function arguments. This parameter is passed as keyword arguments to the callback function.

timeout.description: Timeout to be used in waiting for resources. Default time is value defined in this class constructor.

run_filename.description: Name to be used for the log and raw file.

callback_on_error.description: If False (default), the callback function is not called if the simulation fails. If True, the callback function is called even if the simulation fails. Know that in that case it is not guaranteed that the raw and log files will be available.

exe_log.description: If True, the simulator's execution console messages will be written to a log file (named ...exe.log) instead of console. This is especially useful when running under wine or when running simultaneous tasks.

return.description: The task object of type RunTask. For internal use only.

environment.description:

步骤/决策：先核对网表和模型文件及变量输出；解析/缺文件错误先修正输入；若为奇异矩阵或不收敛则检查浮置节点、偏置与模型适用性，再按手册允许的策略复算；退出码为 0 仍检查日志 warning/error、结果是否完整且有限，并同基线/规格核对；证据不足时保留故障状态并要求模型或量测复核
验收：必要输出存在且数值有限；日志中的不可恢复错误和收敛状态已逐项处理；结果满足项目给定的工作点/波形规格或明确保留未通过；退出码 0 不能单独构成通过

init_ref_tools.name: SimRunner
init_ref_tools.description: The SimRunner class implements all the methods required for launching batches of Spice simulations.  It is iterable, but with a catch: The iteration will only return the completed tasks (succeeded or not), in the order they were completed. If all completed tasks have been returned, and there are still running tasks, it will wait for the completion of the next task. If you used no callbacks, the result is a tuple with the raw and log file names. If you used callbacks, it will return the return code of the callback function, or None if there was an error. Also see `sim_info()` for more details on the completed tasks.  :param simulator: Forcing a given simulator executable. :type simulator: Simulator, optional :param parallel_sims: Defines the number of parallel simulations that can be executed at the same time. Ideally this number should be aligned to the number of CPUs (processor cores) available on the machine. :type parallel_sims: int, optional :param timeout: Timeout parameter as specified on the OS subprocess.run() function. Default is 600 seconds, i.e. 10 minutes. For no timeout, set to None. :type timeout: float, optional :param verbose: If True, it enables a richer printout of the program execution. :type verbose: bool, optional :param output_folder: specifying which directory shall be used for simulation files (raw and log files). :type output_folder: str, optional :param cwd: The current working directory to run the command in. If None, no change will be done of the working directory. :type cwd: str or pathlib.Path, optional  :raises FileNotFoundError: When the file is not found. !This will be changed.

netlist.description: The name of the netlist can be optionally overridden if the user wants to have a better control of how the simulations files are generated.

wait_resource.description: Setting this parameter to False will force the simulation to start immediately, irrespective of the number of simulations already active. By default, the SimRunner class uses only four processors. This number can be overridden by setting the parameter ´parallel_sims´ to a different number. If there are more than ´parallel_sims´ simulations being done, the new one will be placed on hold till one of the other simulations are finished.

callback.description: The user can optionally give a callback function for when the simulation finishes so that processing can be done immediately. The callback can either be a function or a class derived from ProcessCallback. A callback function must receive two at least input parameters that correspond the raw and log files created by the simulation. These need to be the first two parameters of the callback function. The other parameters are passed as a dictionary or a tuple in the callback_args parameter. If the callback is a class derived from ProcessCallback, then the callback is executed in a separate process. The callback function must be defined in the callback() method of the class. As for the callback function, the first two parameters are the raw and log files. The other parameters are passed as dictionary in the callback_args parameter.

callback_on_error.description: If False (default), the callback function is not called if the simulation fails. If True, the callback function is called even if the simulation fails. Know that in that case it is not guaranteed that the raw and log files will be available.

exe_log.description: If True, the simulator's execution console messages will be written to a log file (named ...exe.log) instead of console. This is especially useful when running under wine or when running simultaneous tasks.

return.description: The task object of type RunTask. For internal use only.

目标：判断失配异常来自模型面积律而非尺寸选择，并决定暂停HBT匹配优化签核、补充硅片证据或用经批准修订模型重签
输入：模型文件hash与qarea表达式、Nx/El/电流矩阵、固定电流密度的二管ΔVBE样本、名义无失配对照、基准输出MC分布、晶圆配对器件统计（若有）
步骤/决策：核对HBT局部失配与全局工艺变化模型分开；固定电流密度扫发射极面积并重复MC，估计ΔVBE sigma和置信度，检查名义模型零散度对照；若面积增加而局部sigma基本不降，冻结该HBT匹配预算结论并向PDK维护者提供可复现deck；待模型修订和独立实测面积律约束后，复跑基准电路、确认预算与旧证据差异，再发布新签核版本

init_ref_tools.name: SimStepper
init_ref_tools.description: This class is intended to be used for simulations with many parameter sweeps. This provides a more user-friendly interface than the SpiceEditor/SimRunner class when there are many parameters to be stepped.  Using the SpiceEditor/SimRunner classes a loop needs to be added for each dimension of the simulations. A typical usage would be as follows:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") runner = SimRunner(parallel_sims=4) for dmodel in ("BAT54", "BAT46WJ") netlist.set_element_model("D1", model) # Sets the Diode D1 model for res_value1 in sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2): # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments netlist.set_component_value('R1', res_value1) # Updates the resistor R1 value to be 3.3k for temperature in sweep(0, 80, 20): # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 degree steps netlist.set_parameters(temp=80) # Sets the simulation temperature to be 80 degrees for res_value2 in (10, 25, 32): netlist.set_component_value('R2', res_value2) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k runner.run(netlist)  runner.wait_completion() # Waits for the Spice simulations to complete  With SimStepper the same thing can be done as follows, resulting in a cleaner code:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") Stepper = SimStepper(netlist, SimRunner(parallel_sims=4, output_folder="./output")) Stepper.add_model_sweep('D1', "BAT54", "BAT46WJ") Stepper.add_component_sweep('R1', sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2)) # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments Stepper.add_parameter_sweep('temp', sweep(0, 80, 20)) # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 # degree steps Stepper.add_component_sweep('R2', (10, 25, 32)) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k Stepper.run_all()  Another advantage of using SimStepper is that it can optionally use the .SAVEBIAS in the first simulation and then use the .LOADBIAS command at the subsequent ones to speed up the simulation times.

场景要求：触发: IHP SG13G2 HBT配对器件面积放大后，ΔVBE及基准输出电流MC离散几乎不改善，现行模型qarea为与Nx/El无关的固定10% sigma
对象：同版本HBT模型与基准电路、发射极几何和电流密度矩阵、ngspice MC日志、已批准失配预算
目标：判断失配异常来自模型面积律而非尺寸选择，并决定暂停HBT匹配优化签核、补充硅片证据或用经批准修订模型重签
输入：模型文件hash与qarea表达式、Nx/El/电流矩阵、固定电流密度的二管ΔVBE样本、名义无失配对照、基准输出MC分布、晶圆配对器件统计（若有）
步骤/决策：核对HBT局部失配与全局工艺变化模型分开；固定电流密度扫发射极面积并重复MC，估计ΔVBE sigma和置信度，检查名义模型零散度对照；若面积增加而局部sigma基本不降，冻结该HBT匹配预算结论并向PDK维护者提供可复现deck；待模型修订和独立实测面积律约束后，复跑基准电路、确认预算与旧证据差异，再发布新签核版本
验收：发射极面积与偏置电流成比例，MC draw独立且样本数足够；全局/局部模型分开；修复模型需测量支持，不能把1/sqrt(A)当已验证项目参数

可合成任务：输入：模型文件hash与qarea表达式、Nx/El/电流矩阵、固定电流密度的二管ΔVBE样本、名义无失配对照、基准输出MC分布、晶圆配对器件统计（若有）
Python核心操作/决策：Python可生成固定Nx/El/电流矩阵、解析ngspice样本并算样本sigma/置信区间和版本对比；SPICE核心、器件模型与真实硅片量测在外部
输出：面积-ΔVBE方差曲线、受影响电路/签核清单、模型修复或补测状态
可复核验收：发射极面积与偏置电流成比例，MC draw独立且样本数足够；全局/局部模型分开；修复模型需测量支持，不能把1/sqrt(A)当已验证项目参数

init_ref_tools.name: SimStepper
init_ref_tools.description: This class is intended to be used for simulations with many parameter sweeps. This provides a more user-friendly interface than the SpiceEditor/SimRunner class when there are many parameters to be stepped.  Using the SpiceEditor/SimRunner classes a loop needs to be added for each dimension of the simulations. A typical usage would be as follows:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") runner = SimRunner(parallel_sims=4) for dmodel in ("BAT54", "BAT46WJ") netlist.set_element_model("D1", model) # Sets the Diode D1 model for res_value1 in sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2): # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments netlist.set_component_value('R1', res_value1) # Updates the resistor R1 value to be 3.3k for temperature in sweep(0, 80, 20): # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 degree steps netlist.set_parameters(temp=80) # Sets the simulation temperature to be 80 degrees for res_value2 in (10, 25, 32): netlist.set_component_value('R2', res_value2) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k runner.run(netlist)  runner.wait_completion() # Waits for the Spice simulations to complete  With SimStepper the same thing can be done as follows, resulting in a cleaner code:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") Stepper = SimStepper(netlist, SimRunner(parallel_sims=4, output_folder="./output")) Stepper.add_model_sweep('D1', "BAT54", "BAT46WJ") Stepper.add_component_sweep('R1', sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2)) # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments Stepper.add_parameter_sweep('temp', sweep(0, 80, 20)) # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 # degree steps Stepper.add_component_sweep('R2', (10, 25, 32)) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k Stepper.run_all()  Another advantage of using SimStepper is that it can optionally use the .SAVEBIAS in the first simulation and then use the .LOADBIAS command at the subsequent ones to speed up the simulation times.

init_ref_tools.name: RawRead
init_ref_tools.description: Class for reading Spice wave Files. It can read all types of Files, and can handle multiple plots in 1 file. If stepped data is detected, it will also try to read the corresponding LOG file so to retrieve the stepped data.  :param raw_filename: The file containing the RAW data to be read :type raw_filename: str or pathlib.Path :param traces_to_read: A string or a list containing the list of traces to be read. If None is provided, only the header is read and all trace data is discarded. If a '*' wildcard is given or no parameter at all then all traces are read. :type traces_to_read: str, list or tuple :param dialect: The simulator used. Please select from ["ltspice","qspice","ngspice","xyce"]. If not specified, dialect will be auto detected. This is likely only needed for older versions of ngspice and xyce. ltspice and qspice can reliably be auto detected. :type dialect: str | None  :param verbose: If True, then the class will log debug information. Defaults to True. :type verbose: bool  :raises SpiceReadException: in case of a syntax error in the RAW file, or if the encoding is not recognized.
