init_ref_tools.name: SimStepper
init_ref_tools.description: This class is intended to be used for simulations with many parameter sweeps. This provides a more user-friendly interface than the SpiceEditor/SimRunner class when there are many parameters to be stepped.  Using the SpiceEditor/SimRunner classes a loop needs to be added for each dimension of the simulations. A typical usage would be as follows:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") runner = SimRunner(parallel_sims=4) for dmodel in ("BAT54", "BAT46WJ") netlist.set_element_model("D1", model) # Sets the Diode D1 model for res_value1 in sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2): # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments netlist.set_component_value('R1', res_value1) # Updates the resistor R1 value to be 3.3k for temperature in sweep(0, 80, 20): # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 degree steps netlist.set_parameters(temp=80) # Sets the simulation temperature to be 80 degrees for res_value2 in (10, 25, 32): netlist.set_component_value('R2', res_value2) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k runner.run(netlist)  runner.wait_completion() # Waits for the Spice simulations to complete  With SimStepper the same thing can be done as follows, resulting in a cleaner code:  .. code-block:: python  netlist = SpiceEditor("my_circuit.asc") Stepper = SimStepper(netlist, SimRunner(parallel_sims=4, output_folder="./output")) Stepper.add_model_sweep('D1', "BAT54", "BAT46WJ") Stepper.add_component_sweep('R1', sweep(2.2, 2,4, 0.2)) # Steps from 2.2 to 2.4 with 0.2 increments Stepper.add_parameter_sweep('temp', sweep(0, 80, 20)) # Makes temperature step from 0 to 80 degrees in 20 # degree steps Stepper.add_component_sweep('R2', (10, 25, 32)) # Updates the resistor R2 value to be 3.3k Stepper.run_all()  Another advantage of using SimStepper is that it can optionally use the .SAVEBIAS in the first simulation and then use the .LOADBIAS command at the subsequent ones to speed up the simulation times.

init_ref_tools.name: RawRead
init_ref_tools.description: Class for reading Spice wave Files. It can read all types of Files, and can handle multiple plots in 1 file. If stepped data is detected, it will also try to read the corresponding LOG file so to retrieve the stepped data.  :param raw_filename: The file containing the RAW data to be read :type raw_filename: str or pathlib.Path :param traces_to_read: A string or a list containing the list of traces to be read. If None is provided, only the header is read and all trace data is discarded. If a '*' wildcard is given or no parameter at all then all traces are read. :type traces_to_read: str, list or tuple :param dialect: The simulator used. Please select from ["ltspice","qspice","ngspice","xyce"]. If not specified, dialect will be auto detected. This is likely only needed for older versions of ngspice and xyce. ltspice and qspice can reliably be auto detected. :type dialect: str | None  :param verbose: If True, then the class will log debug information. Defaults to True. :type verbose: bool  :raises SpiceReadException: in case of a syntax error in the RAW file, or if the encoding is not recognized.

对象：电路连接方式不变，但分压器实例模型与角落响应变更；有旧版MOS角/温度记录及当前PDK版本

environment.description:
触发: 新post-layout Monte Carlo测试台进入旧报告生成器，报告声称schematic来源并链接不存在的测试台路径
对象：真实提取网表和冻结快照、testbench-postlayout/tb.json、2500条样本日志与已发布错误记录、旧报告渲染器
目标：保证签核记录所称网表、哈希、链接、风险注释和复现命令都指向实际运行输入，并纠正已经发布的误标证据
输入：实验manifest的directory/netlist_provenance/provenance_note、运行参数与输入网表SHA256、快照头、报告正文/链接/复现命令、原始样本日志、已批准记录版本
步骤/决策：从manifest、运行环境哈希、快照和日志独立核对真实netlist；若报告来源或Reproduce解析到旧schematic测试台则阻断其作为post-layout引用，修复报告渲染器按manifest取目录和注释并显式指定非默认复现路径；对已发布不可修改记录生成注明Supersedes的新记录，仅重渲染原始数值而不伪造第二次仿真；用同一原始样本和网表哈希验证数值字节不变及链接/命令可回放
验收：provenance与manifest、实际网表SHA256、快照头三方一致；Reproduce命令解析到实际post-layout测试台；抽取限制注释可见；已发表旧记录保持原样并由Supersedes串联；修正仅改元数据，不声称重跑或增加独立样本；若哈希/日志缺失则不得确认数值身份

init_ref_tools.name: Montecarlo
init_ref_tools.description: Class to automate Montecarlo simulations, where component values and parameters are replaced by a random distribution (either a gaussian or a uniform distribution).  This is a statistical method, hence, it needs a considerable number of simulations to achieve a final gaussian distribution in order to apply this method. If the number of parameters and component values is low, it is better to use a Worst-Case approach.  Like the Worst-Case and Sensitivity analysis, there are two possible approaches to use this class:  Class to automate Worst-Case simulations, where all possible combinations of maximum and minimums possible values of component values and parameters are done.  It is advised to use this algorithm when the number of parameters to be varied is reduced. Typically less than 10 or 12. A higher number will translate into a huge number of simulations. For more than 1000 simulations, it is better to use a statistical method such as the Montecarlo.  Like the Worst-Case and Sensitivity analysis, there are two possible approaches to use this class:  1. Preparing a testbench where all combinations are managed directly by the simulator, replacing parameters and component values by formulas and using a .STEP primitive to cycle through all possible combinations.  2. Launching each simulation separately where the running python script manages all parameter value variations.  The first approach is normally faster, but not possible in all simulators. The second approach is a valid backup when every single simulation takes too long, or when it is prone to crashes and stalls.

environment.description:
触发: 当前设计的Monte Carlo样本全通过或失败太少，置信区间仍跨越项目良率目标，且需要在有限仿真预算内定位最接近失效的规格
对象：冻结的网表和模型版本、逐指标上下限、统计参数定义/协方差、运行条件、现有Monte Carlo样本和预算
目标：找出需优先复核的规格边界与参数组合，或证明当前统计模型不满足距离分析假设并暂缓结论
输入：网表、PDK统计模型及归一化方式、参数独立性或相关结构、性能测量定义、规格限、运行角/工况、已有样本与置信要求
步骤/决策：Freeze netlist, model, specifications and Monte Carlo sampling plan. Audit whether all n draws are iid from the declared fixed PDK distribution and calculate a named exact one-sided binomial interval; if independence, distribution or stopping is not supportable, mark the interval unknown. If the interval cannot establish the project target, document any correlation-to-independent-standard-normal transformation and its validity; otherwise hold WCD interpretation. For each upper/lower specification bound run WCD and record status, sigmaBox, dist, parameter vector and predicted performance. Independently rerun any candidate violating vector with the original circuit solver and inspect convergence, working point and measurement completeness. Confirmed violation becomes a candidate counterexample/weak specification; FAILED, OUTSIDE, no violating point or broken assumptions remain unknown and trigger model review or further sampling, never a yield pass.
验收：All MC samples and interval method/confidence are reproducible; iid population, sample count and stopping rule are recorded. Each WCD result is tied to statistical transformation, PDK/netlist/specification version, sigmaBox and termination status. Candidate violating vectors are independently rerun in SPICE with finite measurements and warnings reviewed. No found violation or large distance cannot by itself satisfy a yield target; only separately justified statistical evidence may support that claim.

init_ref_tools.name: SimRunner
init_ref_tools.description: The SimRunner class implements all the methods required for launching batches of Spice simulations.  It is iterable, but with a catch: The iteration will only return the completed tasks (succeeded or not), in the order they were completed. If all completed tasks have been returned, and there are still running tasks, it will wait for the completion of the next task. If you used no callbacks, the result is a tuple with the raw and log file names. If you used callbacks, it will return the return code of the callback function, or None if there was an error. Also see `sim_info()` for more details on the completed tasks.  :param simulator: Forcing a given simulator executable. :type simulator: Simulator, optional :param parallel_sims: Defines the number of parallel simulations that can be executed at the same time. Ideally this number should be aligned to the number of CPUs (processor cores) available on the machine. :type parallel_sims: int, optional :param timeout: Timeout parameter as specified on the OS subprocess.run() function. Default is 600 seconds, i.e. 10 minutes. For no timeout, set to None. :type timeout: float, optional :param verbose: If True, it enables a richer printout of the program execution. :type verbose: bool, optional :param output_folder: specifying which directory shall be used for simulation files (raw and log files). :type output_folder: str, optional :param cwd: The current working directory to run the command in. If None, no change will be done of the working directory. :type cwd: str or pathlib.Path, optional  :raises FileNotFoundError: When the file is not found. !This will be changed.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes a simulation run with the conditions set by the user. Conditions are set by the set_parameter, set_component_value or add_instruction functions.

netlist.description: The name of the netlist can be optionally overridden if the user wants to have a better control of how the simulations files are generated.

wait_resource.description: Setting this parameter to False will force the simulation to start immediately, irrespective of the number of simulations already active. By default, the SimRunner class uses only four processors. This number can be overridden by setting the parameter ´parallel_sims´ to a different number. If there are more than ´parallel_sims´ simulations being done, the new one will be placed on hold till one of the other simulations are finished.

callback.description: The user can optionally give a callback function for when the simulation finishes so that processing can be done immediately. The callback can either be a function or a class derived from ProcessCallback. A callback function must receive two at least input parameters that correspond the raw and log files created by the simulation. These need to be the first two parameters of the callback function. The other parameters are passed as a dictionary or a tuple in the callback_args parameter. If the callback is a class derived from ProcessCallback, then the callback is executed in a separate process. The callback function must be defined in the callback() method of the class. As for the callback function, the first two parameters are the raw and log files. The other parameters are passed as dictionary in the callback_args parameter.

timeout.description: Timeout to be used in waiting for resources. Default time is value defined in this class constructor.

run_filename.description: Name to be used for the log and raw file.

callback_on_error.description: If False (default), the callback function is not called if the simulation fails. If True, the callback function is called even if the simulation fails. Know that in that case it is not guaranteed that the raw and log files will be available.

exe_log.description: If True, the simulator's execution console messages will be written to a log file (named ...exe.log) instead of console. This is especially useful when running under wine or when running simultaneous tasks.

return.description: The task object of type RunTask. For internal use only.

init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: 当前设计的Monte Carlo样本全通过或失败太少，置信区间仍跨越项目良率目标，且需要在有限仿真预算内定位最接近失效的规格
对象：冻结的网表和模型版本、逐指标上下限、统计参数定义/协方差、运行条件、现有Monte Carlo样本和预算
目标：找出需优先复核的规格边界与参数组合，或证明当前统计模型不满足距离分析假设并暂缓结论
输入：网表、PDK统计模型及归一化方式、参数独立性或相关结构、性能测量定义、规格限、运行角/工况、已有样本与置信要求
步骤/决策：Freeze netlist, model, specifications and Monte Carlo sampling plan. Audit whether all n draws are iid from the declared fixed PDK distribution and calculate a named exact one-sided binomial interval; if independence, distribution or stopping is not supportable, mark the interval unknown. If the interval cannot establish the project target, document any correlation-to-independent-standard-normal transformation and its validity; otherwise hold WCD interpretation. For each upper/lower specification bound run WCD and record status, sigmaBox, dist, parameter vector and predicted performance. Independently rerun any candidate violating vector with the original circuit solver and inspect convergence, working point and measurement completeness. Confirmed violation becomes a candidate counterexample/weak specification; FAILED, OUTSIDE, no violating point or broken assumptions remain unknown and trigger model review or further sampling, never a yield pass.
验收：All MC samples and interval method/confidence are reproducible; iid population, sample count and stopping rule are recorded. Each WCD result is tied to statistical transformation, PDK/netlist/specification version, sigmaBox and termination status. Candidate violating vectors are independently rerun in SPICE with finite measurements and warnings reviewed. No found violation or large distance cannot by itself satisfy a yield target; only separately justified statistical evidence may support that claim.

可合成任务：输入：网表、PDK统计模型及归一化方式、参数独立性或相关结构、性能测量定义、规格限、运行角/工况、已有样本与置信要求
Python核心操作/决策：PyOPUS WorstCaseDistance编排每规格边界搜索和参数向量审计，标准库/数值统计计算样本置信界；实际电路性能由外部SPICE求解器计算
输出：Per-specification exact interval and its iid/sample assumptions; WCD status/distance and bounded parameter vector; independent SPICE rerun log/performance or an explicit model/search-unknown state. No WCD distance is converted to a yield estimate or release guarantee.
可复核验收：All MC samples and interval method/confidence are reproducible; iid population, sample count and stopping rule are recorded. Each WCD result is tied to statistical transformation, PDK/netlist/specification version, sigmaBox and termination status. Candidate violating vectors are independently rerun in SPICE with finite measurements and warnings reviewed. No found violation or large distance cannot by itself satisfy a yield target; only separately justified statistical evidence may support that claim.

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for simulator classes.  Every simulator is equipped with a *simulatorID* unique for every simulator in every Python process on every host. The format of the simulatorID is  ``<locationID>_simulatorObjectNumber``  ``<locationID>`` is generated by the :func:`pyopus.misc.locationID` function. It containes the information on the hosts and the task within which the simulator object was created.  A different simulator object number is assigned to every simulator object of a given type in one Python interpreter.  All intermediate files resulting from the actions performed by a simulator object have their name prefixed by *simulatorID*.  Every simulator can hold result groups from several jobs. One of these groups is the active result group.  The *binary* argument gives the full path to the simulator executable. *args* is a list of additional command line parameters passed to the simulator executable at simulator startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed to standard output.

function.name: cleanup
function.description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).
function.ori_description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).

function.name: setJobList
function.description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.
function.ori_description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

function.name: jobGroup
function.description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.
function.ori_description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.

function.description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.
function.ori_description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.

function.name: readResults
function.description: Read results of job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results.

init_ref_tools.name: Optimizer
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for unconstrained optimization algorithms.  *function* is the cost function (Python function or any other callable object) which should be minimzied.  If *debug* is greater than 0, debug messages are printed at standard output.  *fstop* specifies the cost function value at which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the algorithm is never stopped regardless of how low the cost function's value gets.  *maxiter* specifies the number of cost function evaluations after which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the number of cost function evaluations is unlimited.  *nanBarrier* specifies if nan function values should be treated as infinite thus resulting in an extreme barrier.  *cache* turns on local point caching. Currently works only for algorithms that do not use remote evaluations. See the :mod:`~pyopus.optimizer.cache` module for more information.  The following members are available in every object of the :class:`Optimizer` class  * :attr:`ndim` - dimension of the problem. Updated when the :meth:`reset` method is called. * :attr:`niter` - the consecutive number of cost function evaluation. * :attr:`x` - the argument to the cost function resulting in the best-yet (lowest) value. * :attr:`f` - the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`bestIter` - the iteration in which the best-yet value of the cost function was found. * :attr:`bestAnnotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`stop` - boolean flag indicating that the algorithm should stop. * :attr:`annotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the last evaluated cost function value * :attr:`annGrp` - :class:`AnnotatorGroup` object that holds the installed annotators * :attr:`plugins` - a list of installed plugin objects  Plugin objects are called at every cost function evaluation or whenever a remotely evaluated cost function value is registered by the :meth:`newResult` method.  Values of *x* and related members are arrays.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, function, debug = 0, fstop = None, maxiter = None, nanBarrier = False, cache = False

function.name: check
function.description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.
function.ori_description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.

function.name: fun
function.description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.
function.ori_description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.

function.name: updateBest
function.description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.
function.ori_description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.

function.name: reset
function.description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).
function.ori_description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).

function.description: Runs the optimization algorithm.

触发: 首硅采用模拟pile-up/多周期CDS时，累加次数增加使输出提前触及摆幅界限，低噪声目标因此无法按设计达到
对象：积分器、复位、极性翻转和ADC范围设计资料；首硅零输入/信号输入循环记录；本项目无真实波形
目标：判明可累加样本数受残余失调、开关注入、CCD基线、控制序列还是下游限幅所限，并决定可用读出模式与改版需求
输入：逐周期积分器输出、复位状态、POL极性、零输入与已知输入记录、反馈RC和开关布局、ADC范围、前后芯片相同条件测试
步骤/决策：先检查每周期复位和ADC量程；令输入差分为零并在POL=0、POL=1和周期交替三组下记录逐周期输出，比较斜率和对称性；若零输入仍积累且极性关联，分别用注入/开关模型和版图寄生检查残余失调；若只在真实传感器出现则优先查基线与传感器，若积分器节点正常而数字值触顶则查ADC/采集链；记录最坏情况下剩余信号摆幅及可用周期数；针对有证据的机制比较开关对称、反馈电容或版图调整，再以新旧硅片同条件零输入及实际信号试验确认
验收：逐周期节点、POL和复位状态可追溯；故障机制须由独立零输入或节点证据支持；前后版以同样测试序列比较最大可用累加次数、残余斜率和信号余量，满足项目指标才可放行；论文数字仅为案例

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for simulator classes.  Every simulator is equipped with a *simulatorID* unique for every simulator in every Python process on every host. The format of the simulatorID is  ``<locationID>_simulatorObjectNumber``  ``<locationID>`` is generated by the :func:`pyopus.misc.locationID` function. It containes the information on the hosts and the task within which the simulator object was created.  A different simulator object number is assigned to every simulator object of a given type in one Python interpreter.  All intermediate files resulting from the actions performed by a simulator object have their name prefixed by *simulatorID*.  Every simulator can hold result groups from several jobs. One of these groups is the active result group.  The *binary* argument gives the full path to the simulator executable. *args* is a list of additional command line parameters passed to the simulator executable at simulator startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed to standard output.

function.name: cleanup
function.description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).
function.ori_description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).

function.name: setJobList
function.description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.
function.ori_description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

function.name: jobGroup
function.description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.
function.ori_description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.

function.name: runJobGroup
function.description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.
function.ori_description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.

function.name: readResults
function.description: Read results of job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results.
function.ori_description: Read results of job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results.

init_ref_tools.name: Optimizer
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for unconstrained optimization algorithms.  *function* is the cost function (Python function or any other callable object) which should be minimzied.  If *debug* is greater than 0, debug messages are printed at standard output.  *fstop* specifies the cost function value at which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the algorithm is never stopped regardless of how low the cost function's value gets.  *maxiter* specifies the number of cost function evaluations after which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the number of cost function evaluations is unlimited.  *nanBarrier* specifies if nan function values should be treated as infinite thus resulting in an extreme barrier.  *cache* turns on local point caching. Currently works only for algorithms that do not use remote evaluations. See the :mod:`~pyopus.optimizer.cache` module for more information.  The following members are available in every object of the :class:`Optimizer` class  * :attr:`ndim` - dimension of the problem. Updated when the :meth:`reset` method is called. * :attr:`niter` - the consecutive number of cost function evaluation. * :attr:`x` - the argument to the cost function resulting in the best-yet (lowest) value. * :attr:`f` - the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`bestIter` - the iteration in which the best-yet value of the cost function was found. * :attr:`bestAnnotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`stop` - boolean flag indicating that the algorithm should stop. * :attr:`annotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the last evaluated cost function value * :attr:`annGrp` - :class:`AnnotatorGroup` object that holds the installed annotators * :attr:`plugins` - a list of installed plugin objects  Plugin objects are called at every cost function evaluation or whenever a remotely evaluated cost function value is registered by the :meth:`newResult` method.  Values of *x* and related members are arrays.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, function, debug = 0, fstop = None, maxiter = None, nanBarrier = False, cache = False

function.name: check
function.description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.
function.ori_description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.

function.name: fun
function.description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.
function.ori_description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.

function.name: updateBest
function.description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.
function.ori_description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.

function.name: reset
function.description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).
function.ori_description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).

function.name: run
function.description: Runs the optimization algorithm.
function.ori_description: Runs the optimization algorithm.

场景要求：触发: 首硅采用模拟pile-up/多周期CDS时，累加次数增加使输出提前触及摆幅界限，低噪声目标因此无法按设计达到
对象：积分器、复位、极性翻转和ADC范围设计资料；首硅零输入/信号输入循环记录；本项目无真实波形
目标：判明可累加样本数受残余失调、开关注入、CCD基线、控制序列还是下游限幅所限，并决定可用读出模式与改版需求
输入：逐周期积分器输出、复位状态、POL极性、零输入与已知输入记录、反馈RC和开关布局、ADC范围、前后芯片相同条件测试
步骤/决策：先检查每周期复位和ADC量程；令输入差分为零并在POL=0、POL=1和周期交替三组下记录逐周期输出，比较斜率和对称性；若零输入仍积累且极性关联，分别用注入/开关模型和版图寄生检查残余失调；若只在真实传感器出现则优先查基线与传感器，若积分器节点正常而数字值触顶则查ADC/采集链；记录最坏情况下剩余信号摆幅及可用周期数；针对有证据的机制比较开关对称、反馈电容或版图调整，再以新旧硅片同条件零输入及实际信号试验确认
验收：逐周期节点、POL和复位状态可追溯；故障机制须由独立零输入或节点证据支持；前后版以同样测试序列比较最大可用累加次数、残余斜率和信号余量，满足项目指标才可放行；论文数字仅为案例

可合成任务：输入：逐周期积分器输出、复位状态、POL极性、零输入与已知输入记录、反馈RC和开关布局、ADC范围、前后芯片相同条件测试
Python核心操作/决策：拟议标准库按周期和极性分组、计算线性趋势/残余摆幅与模式差异；真实模拟节点测量、电路仿真和物理改版依赖外部工具
输出：按零输入/极性/周期分支的残余失调证据、可用累加次数限制或待改版单、前后硅片动态余量报告
可复核验收：逐周期节点、POL和复位状态可追溯；故障机制须由独立零输入或节点证据支持；前后版以同样测试序列比较最大可用累加次数、残余斜率和信号余量，满足项目指标才可放行；论文数字仅为案例

basic_info.name: PyOPUS
basic_info.description: PyOPUS 是面向仿真驱动设计与优化的 Python 框架，提供 ngspice、Xyce、HSPICE、Spectre 等电路仿真器接口、波形性能度量、角点与 Monte Carlo 分析、灵敏度和最坏情况分析，以及多种局部和全局优化算法。外部仿真器、MPI 和部分图形组件需要单独安装。

basic_info.name: 传感前端间歇性饱和的输入电流与偏置余量故障诊断

environment.description:
触发: 硅后联机运行中部分前端通道周期性低增益低噪声且对外部校准脉冲无响应，之后自行恢复
对象：带偏压传感器、前端ASIC及其可追溯偏置配置、通道级原始波形；本项目未提供芯片或波形
目标：区分前端输入饱和、传感器外部电流、偏置误设、读出链掉数及永久损坏，决定复设、补测或限制使用
输入：逐通道原始波形、外部脉冲响应、ASIC输入偏置及传感器高压状态、传感器尺寸或电容、前放节点/输出示波波形、台架注入测试、变更前后运行记录
步骤/决策：先用脉冲和原始波形识别低增益低RMS且可恢复的失响应时段，排除ADC或采集链掉数；比较有偏压与零偏压、不同传感器长度/电容及前放偏置档位的异常发生率；在批准硬件范围内用台架受控输入电流复现前放限幅并核对现场偏置实际配置；若仅偏置变更可减轻而仍有异常通道，应继续查外部瞬态、线缆和传感器，不宣称机械运动已证实；记录偏置提高造成的噪声代价，并以长期运行和脉冲恢复结果决定可用性
验收：低增益低噪声和脉冲不响应须在原始记录共同出现；偏置及高压状态可追溯；受控注入支持输入饱和机制且排除读出链故障；更改后按项目窗口复测脉冲响应、异常率及噪声，残余异常不得强行归因或放行

environment.description:
触发: 首硅或系统投运后多个通道出现同步低频基线噪声，噪声分组与ASIC/服务板供电域相近
对象：通道-ASIC-服务板-调节器映射、原始静默与真实信号波形、供电测试点；本项目无实际数据
目标：判断相干噪声是供电注入、真实共时传感信号、时钟/采集链还是传感器耦合，并决定硬件或滤波处置
输入：多通道同时间轴原始波形、频谱、供电域拓扑与调节器波形、校准脉冲和真实事件、滤波前后信号幅度及形状、硬件改动记录
步骤/决策：先在静默时段比较同供电域与跨供电域通道的相关性和频谱，核对噪声随服务板而非物理相邻传感器分组；用供电测点和调节器替换/隔离或受控台架试验确认注入路径；若共模样式可能含真实事件，保留受影响区段而不直接相减；评估硬件治理与每组估计噪声的离线修正，利用独立脉冲和真实事件检查滤波前后信号效率、幅值与时形；未证实供电路径时继续查时钟、DAQ及传感器
验收：供电分组与噪声相关性可重复且由测点或受控变更支持；真实信号区段的幅度、形状及检出效率按项目门槛复核；不能以噪声RMS单独验收滤波；未证实根因时标为待查

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for simulator classes.  Every simulator is equipped with a *simulatorID* unique for every simulator in every Python process on every host. The format of the simulatorID is  ``<locationID>_simulatorObjectNumber``  ``<locationID>`` is generated by the :func:`pyopus.misc.locationID` function. It containes the information on the hosts and the task within which the simulator object was created.  A different simulator object number is assigned to every simulator object of a given type in one Python interpreter.  All intermediate files resulting from the actions performed by a simulator object have their name prefixed by *simulatorID*.  Every simulator can hold result groups from several jobs. One of these groups is the active result group.  The *binary* argument gives the full path to the simulator executable. *args* is a list of additional command line parameters passed to the simulator executable at simulator startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed to standard output.

function.name: cleanup
function.description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).
function.ori_description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).

function.name: setJobList
function.description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.
function.ori_description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

function.name: jobGroup
function.description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.
function.ori_description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.

function.name: runJobGroup
function.description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.
function.ori_description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.

function.name: readResults
function.description: Read results of job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results.
function.ori_description: Read results of job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results.

init_ref_tools.name: Optimizer
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for unconstrained optimization algorithms.  *function* is the cost function (Python function or any other callable object) which should be minimzied.  If *debug* is greater than 0, debug messages are printed at standard output.  *fstop* specifies the cost function value at which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the algorithm is never stopped regardless of how low the cost function's value gets.  *maxiter* specifies the number of cost function evaluations after which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the number of cost function evaluations is unlimited.  *nanBarrier* specifies if nan function values should be treated as infinite thus resulting in an extreme barrier.  *cache* turns on local point caching. Currently works only for algorithms that do not use remote evaluations. See the :mod:`~pyopus.optimizer.cache` module for more information.  The following members are available in every object of the :class:`Optimizer` class  * :attr:`ndim` - dimension of the problem. Updated when the :meth:`reset` method is called. * :attr:`niter` - the consecutive number of cost function evaluation. * :attr:`x` - the argument to the cost function resulting in the best-yet (lowest) value. * :attr:`f` - the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`bestIter` - the iteration in which the best-yet value of the cost function was found. * :attr:`bestAnnotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`stop` - boolean flag indicating that the algorithm should stop. * :attr:`annotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the last evaluated cost function value * :attr:`annGrp` - :class:`AnnotatorGroup` object that holds the installed annotators * :attr:`plugins` - a list of installed plugin objects  Plugin objects are called at every cost function evaluation or whenever a remotely evaluated cost function value is registered by the :meth:`newResult` method.  Values of *x* and related members are arrays.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, function, debug = 0, fstop = None, maxiter = None, nanBarrier = False, cache = False

function.name: check
function.description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.
function.ori_description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.

function.name: fun
function.description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.
function.ori_description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.

function.name: updateBest
function.description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.
function.ori_description: Updates best yet function value. Returns ``True`` if an update takes place.

function.name: reset
function.description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).
function.ori_description: Puts the optimizer in its initial state and sets the initial point to be the 1-dimensional array or list *x0*. The length of the array becomes the dimension of the optimization problem (:attr:`ndim` member).

function.name: run
function.description: Runs the optimization algorithm.
function.ori_description: Runs the optimization algorithm.

init_ref_tools.description: Generates the Ngspice simulator command that invokes the small signal (AC) analysis. init_ref_tools.name: Ngspice
init_ref_tools.description: A class for interfacing with the Ngspice simulator in batch mode.  *binary* is the path to the Ngspice simulator binary. If it is not given the ``NGSPICEPATH`` environmental variable is used as the path to the Ngspice binary. If ``NGSPICEPATH`` is not defined the binary is assumed to be in the current working directory.  *args* apecifies a list of additional arguments passed to the simulator binary at startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed at the standard output. If it is above 1 a part of the simulator output is also printed. If *debug* is above 2 full simulator output is printed.  The save directives from the simulator job description are evaluated in an environment where the following objects are available:  * ``all`` - a reference to the :func:`save_all` function * ``v`` - a reference to the :func:`save_voltage` function * ``i`` - a reference to the :func:`save_current` function * ``p`` - a reference to the :func:`save_property` function * ``ipath`` - a reference to the :func:`ipath` function  Similarly the environment for evaluating the analysis command given in the job description consists of the following objects:  * ``op`` - a reference to the :func:`an_op` function * ``dc`` - a reference to the :func:`an_dc` function * ``tf`` - a reference to the :func:`an_tf` function * ``ac`` - a reference to the :func:`an_ac` function * ``tran`` - a reference to the :func:`an_tran` function * ``noise`` - a reference to the :func:`an_noise` function * ``ipath`` - a reference to the :func:`ipath` function * ``param`` - a dictionary containing the members of the ``params`` entry in the simulator job description together with the parameters from the dictionary passed at the last call to the :meth:`setInputParameters` method. The parameters values given in the job description take precedence over the values passed to the :meth:`setInputParameters` method.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, binary = None, args = [], debug = 0, timeout = None

function.name: findSimulator
function.description: Finds the simulator. Location is defined by the NGSPICEPATH environmental variable. If the binary is not found there the system path is used.
function.ori_description: Finds the simulator. Location is defined by the NGSPICEPATH environmental variable. If the binary is not found there the system path is used.

function.name: writeFile
function.description: Prepares the simulator input file for running the *i*-th job group.  The file is named ``simulatorID.group_i.cir`` where *i* is the index of the job group.  All output files with simulation results are .raw files in binary format.  System description modules are converted to ``.include`` and ``.lib`` simulator directives.  Simulator options are set with the ``set`` simulator command. Integer, real, and string simulator options are converted with the :meth:`__str__` method before they are written to the file. Boolean options are converted to ``set`` or ``unset`` commands depending on whether they are ``True`` or ``False``.  The parameters set with the last call to :meth:`setInputParameters` method are joined with the parameters in the job description. The values from the job description take precedence over the values specified with the :meth:`setInputParameters` method. All parameters are written to the input file in form of ``.param`` simulator directives.  The ``temperature`` parameter is treated differently. It is written to the input file in form if a ``set`` simulator command preceding its corresponding analysis command.  Save directives are written as a series of ``save`` simulator commands.  Every analysis command is evaluated in its corresponding environment taking into account the parameter values passed to the :meth:`setInputParameters` method.  Every analysis is followed by a ``write`` command that stores the results in a file named ``simulatorID.job_j.jobName.raw`` where *j* denotes the job index from which the analysis was generated. *jobName* is the ``name`` member of the job description.  The function returns the name of the simulator input file it generated.

Every analysis command is evaluated in its corresponding environment taking into account the parameter values passed to the :meth:`setInputParameters` method. function.name: runFile
function.description: Runs the simulator on the input file given by *fileName*.  Returns ``True`` if the simulation finished successfully. This does not mean that any results were produced. It only means that the return code from the simuator was 0 (OK).
function.ori_description: Runs the simulator on the input file given by *fileName*.  Returns ``True`` if the simulation finished successfully. This does not mean that any results were produced. It only means that the return code from the simuator was 0 (OK).

function.name: runJobGroup
function.description: Runs the *i*-th job group.  First calls the :meth:`writeFile` method followed by the :meth:`cleanupResults` method that removes any old results produced by previous runs of the jobs in *i*-th job group. Finally the :meth:`runFile` method is invoked. Its return value is stored in the :attr:`lastRunStatus` member.  The function returns a tuple (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of job indices corresponding to the *i*-th job group. *status* is the status returned by the :meth:`runFile` method.
function.ori_description: Runs the *i*-th job group.  First calls the :meth:`writeFile` method followed by the :meth:`cleanupResults` method that removes any old results produced by previous runs of the jobs in *i*-th job group. Finally the :meth:`runFile` method is invoked. Its return value is stored in the :attr:`lastRunStatus` member.  The function returns a tuple (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of job indices corresponding to the *i*-th job group. *status* is the status returned by the :meth:`runFile` method.

function.name: readResults
function.description: Read results of a job with given *jobIndex*.  *runOK* specifies the status returned by the :meth:`runJobGroup` method which produced the results. If not specified the run status stored by the simulator is used.  Returns an object of the class :class:`NgspiceSimulationResults`. If the run failed or the results file cannot be read the ``None`` is returned.

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for simulator classes.  Every simulator is equipped with a *simulatorID* unique for every simulator in every Python process on every host. The format of the simulatorID is  ``<locationID>_simulatorObjectNumber``  ``<locationID>`` is generated by the :func:`pyopus.misc.locationID` function. It containes the information on the hosts and the task within which the simulator object was created.  A different simulator object number is assigned to every simulator object of a given type in one Python interpreter.  All intermediate files resulting from the actions performed by a simulator object have their name prefixed by *simulatorID*.  Every simulator can hold result groups from several jobs. One of these groups is the active result group.  The *binary* argument gives the full path to the simulator executable. *args* is a list of additional command line parameters passed to the simulator executable at simulator startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed to standard output.

function.name: cleanup
function.description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).
function.ori_description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).

function.name: setJobList
function.description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job. If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

init_ref_tools.name: Optimizer
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for unconstrained optimization algorithms.  *function* is the cost function (Python function or any other callable object) which should be minimzied.  If *debug* is greater than 0, debug messages are printed at standard output.  *fstop* specifies the cost function value at which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the algorithm is never stopped regardless of how low the cost function's value gets.  *maxiter* specifies the number of cost function evaluations after which the algorithm is stopped. If it is ``None`` the number of cost function evaluations is unlimited.  *nanBarrier* specifies if nan function values should be treated as infinite thus resulting in an extreme barrier.  *cache* turns on local point caching. Currently works only for algorithms that do not use remote evaluations. See the :mod:`~pyopus.optimizer.cache` module for more information.  The following members are available in every object of the :class:`Optimizer` class  * :attr:`ndim` - dimension of the problem. Updated when the :meth:`reset` method is called. * :attr:`niter` - the consecutive number of cost function evaluation. * :attr:`x` - the argument to the cost function resulting in the best-yet (lowest) value. * :attr:`f` - the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`bestIter` - the iteration in which the best-yet value of the cost function was found. * :attr:`bestAnnotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the best-yet value of the cost function. * :attr:`stop` - boolean flag indicating that the algorithm should stop. * :attr:`annotations` - a list of annotations produced by the installed annotators for the last evaluated cost function value * :attr:`annGrp` - :class:`AnnotatorGroup` object that holds the installed annotators * :attr:`plugins` - a list of installed plugin objects  Plugin objects are called at every cost function evaluation or whenever a remotely evaluated cost function value is registered by the :meth:`newResult` method.  Values of *x* and related members are arrays.

function.name: __init__
function.ori_input: self, function, debug = 0, fstop = None, maxiter = None, nanBarrier = False, cache = False

function.name: check
function.description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.
function.ori_description: Checks the optimization algorithm's settings and raises an exception if something is wrong.

function.name: fun
function.description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.
function.ori_description: Evaluates the cost function at *x* (array). If *count* is ``True`` the :meth:`newResult` method is invoked with *x*, the obtained cost function value, and *annotations* argument set to ``None``. This means that the result is registered (best-yet point information are updated), the plugins are calls and the annotators are invoked to produce annotations.  Use ``False`` for *count* if you need to evaluate the cost function for debugging purposes.  Returns the value of the cost function at *x*.

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Base class for simulator classes.  Every simulator is equipped with a *simulatorID* unique for every simulator in every Python process on every host. The format of the simulatorID is  ``<locationID>_simulatorObjectNumber``  ``<locationID>`` is generated by the :func:`pyopus.misc.locationID` function. It containes the information on the hosts and the task within which the simulator object was created.  A different simulator object number is assigned to every simulator object of a given type in one Python interpreter.  All intermediate files resulting from the actions performed by a simulator object have their name prefixed by *simulatorID*.  Every simulator can hold result groups from several jobs. One of these groups is the active result group.  The *binary* argument gives the full path to the simulator executable. *args* is a list of additional command line parameters passed to the simulator executable at simulator startup.  If *debug* is greater than 0 debug messages are printed to standard output.

function.name: cleanup
function.description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).
function.ori_description: Removes all intermediate files created as a result of actions performed by this simulator object (files with filenames that have *simulatorID* for prefix).

function.name: setJobList
function.description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.
function.ori_description: Sets *jobList* to be the job list for batch simulation. If the ``options``, ``params``, ``saves``, or ``variables`` member is missing in any of the jobs, an empty dictionary/list is added to that job.  The job list is marked as fresh meaning that a new set of simulator input files needs to be created. Files are created the first time a job group is run.  If *optimize* is ``True`` the optimized job sequence is computed by calling the :meth:`optimizedJobSequence` method. If *optimize* is ``True`` an unoptimized job sequence is produced by calling the :meth:`unoptimizedJobSequence` method.

function.name: jobGroup
function.description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.
function.ori_description: Returns a structure describing the *i*-th job group.

function.name: runJobGroup
function.description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.
function.ori_description: Runs the jobs in the *i*-th job group. Returns a tuple of the form (*jobIndices*, *status*) where *jobIndices* is a list of indices corresponding to the jobs that ran. *status* is ``True`` if everything is OK.

init_ref_tools.name: MonteCarlo
init_ref_tools.description: See :class:`~pyopus.evaluator.performance.PerformanceEvaluator` for details on *heads*, *analyses*, *measures*, *coprners*, and *variables*.  Statistical parameters and operating parameters are given by dictionaries *statParamDesc* and *opParamDesc*. These dictionaries have parameter name for key and parameter property dictionary with *lo* and *hi* specifying the lower and the upper bound. The nominal value is given by the ``init`` member.  Fixed parameters are given by *fixedParams* - a dictionary with parameter name for key and parameter value for value. Alternatively the value can be a dictionary in which case the ``init`` member specifies the parameter value.  If *fixedParams* is a list the members of this list must be dictionaries describing parameters. The set of fixed parameters is obtained by merging the information from these dictionaries.  Setting *debug* to a value greater than 0 turns on debug messages. The verbosity is proportional to the specified number.  Setting *debug* to a value greater than 0 turns on debug messages. The verbosity is proportional to the specified number.  *nSamples* is the number of Monte Carlo samples.  By setting *storeStatSamples* to ``True`` storing of the vector of statistical parameters in the :attr:`statSamples` member is enabled. The first index is the sample index, while the second index is the parameter index. Parameters are ordered according to the *statNames* list.  *storeOpParams* turns on storing of the worst operating parameters in the results structure.  *storeWcEvals* turns on storing the number of performance measure evaluations in the results structure.  *wcOptions* are the worst case analysis options passed to the :class:`~pyopus.design.wc.WorstCase` object performing the worst case analysis in the space of the operating parameters.  This is a callable object with at most one argument. If given the argument is a list of entries. Every entry is  * a tuple of the form (name,type), where name is the measure name and type is ``lower`` or ``upper`` * a string specifying the measure name. In this case the type of the performance costraint for which the Monte-Carlo analysis is performed is given by the presence of the ``lower`` and the ``upper`` entries in the performance measure's description. A separate yield is computed for ``lower`` and ``upper``.  If no argument is specified, all yields corresponding to lower/upper bounds of all performance *measures* are computed.  Results are stored in a results dictionary with pairs of the form (name,type) for key. Values are a dictionaries with the following members:  * ``samples`` - a vector of peformance measure values * ``op`` - 2-dimensional array with worst operating parameter values. The first index is the sample index. The second index is the parameter index. The parameters are ordered according to the *opNames* member of the object. This member is available if ``storeOpParams* is set to ``True``. * ``evals`` - array with the number of performance measure evaluations corresponding to individual samples. Available if *storeWcEvals* is set to ``True``. * ``feasible`` - number of feasible samples (samples satisfying the performance constraint). * ``failed`` - number of failed samples for which the evaluation failed. * ``yield`` - yield obtained by dividing teh number of feasible samples with *nSamples*  The results are stored in the :attr:`results` member. The number of analyses performed during the last call to the :class:`MonteCarlo` object are stored in the :attr:`analysisCount` member.  A call to an object of this class returns a tuple holding the results structure and the analysisCount dictionary.  The :attr:`totalCheck` member holds an array of booleans. Every entry corresponds to one evaluated sample. ``True`` means that a sample satisfies all performance constraints.  The :attr:`totalYield` member holds the total yield obtained by the analysis (share of the samples that satisfy all performance constraints).  The :attr:`statSamples` member is a 2-dimensional array holding the stored statistical parameter samples. The first index is the sample index while the second index is the statistical parameter index. The ordering of statistical parameters is given by the *statNames* member. This member is available if *storeStatSamples* is set to ``True``.  Setting *spawnerLevel* to a value not bigger than 1 distributes the evaluations across available computing nodes.

function.ori_input: self, heads, analyses, measures, corners, statParamDesc, opParamDesc, fixedParams = {}, variables = {}, debug = 0, nSamples = 1000, storeStatSamples = False, storeOpParams = False, storeWcEvals = False, wcOptions = {}, spawnerLevel = 1

function.name: formatResults
function.description: Formats the results as a string.  *nMeasureName* specifies the formatting width for the performance measure name.  *nResult* and *nPrec* specify the formatting width and the number of significant digits for the performance measure values.  *nPrec* specifies the number of significant digits for the results.  *nSamplePrec* specifies the formatting width for the sample count.
function.ori_description: Formats the results as a string.  *nMeasureName* specifies the formatting width for the performance measure name.  *nResult* and *nPrec* specify the formatting width and the number of significant digits for the performance measure values.  *nPrec* specifies the number of significant digits for the results.  *nSamplePrec* specifies the formatting width for the sample count.

init_ref_tools.name: Network
init_ref_tools.description: An n-port electrical network.  For instructions on how to create Network see :func:`__init__`. An n-port network [#TwoPortWiki]_ may be defined by three quantities  * network parameter matrix (s, z, or y-matrix) * port characteristic impedance matrix * frequency information  The :class:`Network` class stores these data structures internally in the form of complex :class:`numpy.ndarray`'s. These arrays are not interfaced directly but instead through the use of the properties:  ===================== ============================================= Property Meaning ===================== ============================================= :attr:`s` Scattering parameter matrix. :attr:`z0` Characteristic impedance matrix. :attr:`f` Frequency vector. ===================== =============================================  Although these docs focus on s-parameters, other equivalent network representations such as :attr:`z` and :attr:`y` are available. Scalar projections of the complex network parameters are accessible through properties as well. These also return :class:`numpy.ndarray`'s.  ===================== ============================================= Property Meaning ===================== ============================================= :attr:`s_re` Real part of the s-matrix. :attr:`s_im` Imaginary part of the s-matrix. :attr:`s_mag` Magnitude of the s-matrix. :attr:`s_db` Magnitude in log scale of the s-matrix. :attr:`s_deg` Phase of the s-matrix in degrees. ===================== =============================================  The following operations act on the networks s-matrix.  ===================== ============================================= Operator Function ===================== ============================================= \+ Element-wise addition of the s-matrix. \- Element-wise difference of the s-matrix. \* Element-wise multiplication of the s-matrix. \/ Element-wise division of the s-matrix. \*\* Cascading (only for 2-ports). \// De-embedding (for 2-ports, see :attr:`inv`). ===================== =============================================  Different components of the :class:`Network` can be visualized through various plotting methods. These methods can be used to plot individual elements of the s-matrix or all at once. For more info about plotting see the :doc:`../../tutorials/Plotting` tutorial.  ========================= ============================================= Method Meaning ========================= ============================================= :func:`plot_s_smith` Plot complex s-parameters on smith chart. :func:`plot_s_re` Plot real part of s-parameters vs frequency. :func:`plot_s_im` Plot imaginary part of s-parameters vs frequency. :func:`plot_s_mag` Plot magnitude of s-parameters vs frequency. :func:`plot_s_db` Plot magnitude (in dB) of s-parameters vs frequency. :func:`plot_s_deg` Plot phase of s-parameters (in degrees) vs frequency. :func:`plot_s_deg_unwrap` Plot phase of s-parameters (in unwrapped degrees) vs frequency. ========================= =============================================  :class:`Network` objects can be created from a touchstone or pickle file (see :func:`__init__`), by a :class:`~skrf.media.media.Media` object, or manually by assigning the network properties directly. :class:`Network` objects can be saved to disk in the form of touchstone files with the :func:`write_touchstone` method.  An exhaustive list of :class:`Network` Methods and Properties (Attributes) are given below  References ---------- .. [#TwoPortWiki] http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-port_network

目标：识别稳健通过、稳健不通过和需复测的频段，保留测量重复性证据

init_ref_tools.name: NetworkSet
init_ref_tools.description: A set of Networks.  This class allows functions on sets of Networks, such as mean or standard deviation, to be calculated conveniently. The results are returned in :class:`~skrf.network.Network` objects, so that they may be plotted and saved in like :class:`~skrf.network.Network` objects.  This class also provides methods which can be used to plot uncertainty bounds for a set of :class:`~skrf.network.Network`.  The names of the :class:`NetworkSet` properties are generated dynamically upon initialization, and thus documentation for individual properties and methods is not available. However, the properties do follow the convention::  >>> my_network_set.function_name_network_property_name  For example, the complex average (mean) :class:`~skrf.network.Network` for a :class:`NetworkSet` is::  >>> my_network_set.mean_s  This accesses the property 's', for each element in the set, and **then** calculates the 'mean' of the resultant set. The order of operations is important.  Results are returned as :class:`~skrf.network.Network` objects, so they may be plotted or saved in the same way as for :class:`~skrf.network.Network` objects::  >>> my_network_set.mean_s.plot_s_mag() >>> my_network_set.mean_s.write_touchstone('mean_response')  If you are calculating functions that return scalar variables, then the result is accessible through the Network property .s_re. For example::  >>> std_s_deg = my_network_set.std_s_deg  This result would be plotted by::  >>> std_s_deg.plot_s_re()  The operators, properties, and methods of NetworkSet object are dynamically generated by private methods  * :func:`~NetworkSet.__add_a_operator` * :func:`~NetworkSet.__add_a_func_on_property` * :func:`~NetworkSet.__add_a_element_wise_method` * :func:`~NetworkSet.__add_a_plot_uncertainty`  thus, documentation on the individual methods and properties are not available.

environment.description:
触发: 三端口balun或单端转差分前级的两路输出幅度接近，但系统级差分性能或共模抑制异常
对象：单端输入端口、两个平衡输出物理端口、VNA逻辑端口映射与三端口校准结果
目标：判定失衡是DUT电性异常还是端口映射/测量链错误，决定复测、返修或按项目规格发布
输入：三端口S矩阵、端口映射、两路输出幅相、仪器imbalance/CMRR结果、校准验证件和频段规格
步骤/决策：锁定single-ended/balanced拓扑及物理到逻辑端口映射；检查两条传输路径幅度、相位及平衡端的差模/共模指标；若映射交换或某一路校准/连接失效，先修映射或测量链并复测；若独立验证件正常而DUT失衡/CMRR仍超项目限，归为DUT待调查；仅按项目定义的频带/容差发布，不以四端口差分到差分转换结论替代三端口验收
验收：物理端口到逻辑端口映射可回链；幅度与相位、共模和差模均在项目频段按规格评价；仪器/工装异常先复测再归因DUT；无产品限值只报告实测与待判状态

basic_info.name: 脉冲功放峰值功率与平均功率混读时的量测资格恢复

environment.description:
触发: 脉冲工作器件切换脉宽/周期或外部IF门，量测报告中的功率偏低或与连续波结果不一致
对象：脉宽、周期、RF/IF触发延迟和门宽、窄带/宽带检测模式、脉冲校准状态与功率显示模式
目标：确定报告为真实脉冲峰值还是占空比平均功率，并恢复与目标规格同义的可发布测量
输入：脉冲设置及其校准快照、检测模式、IF门宽/延迟、显示True Power选项与仪器型号、测得功率、项目规定峰值或平均功率及容差
步骤/决策：先把产品规格标成峰值或平均功率并记录占空比；检查窄带/宽带及设备是否支持True Power显示，外部IF门时核对门宽已输入测量时序；任何PRF、脉宽、延迟、IF门控变化后按实际脉冲配置重新校准；验证接收窗位于目标脉冲平台而非边沿，检查功率显示语义与规格一致；当仪器/模式无法证明峰值换算或校准前后设置不一致时隔离结果并重测
验收：每条发布结果具脉宽/周期/占空比、检测模式、门控、功率语义及对应脉冲配置校准记录；外部IF门宽缺失或模式不支持所需功率语义时暂缓；规格阈值由项目指定

scenario_design.scenario_description_raw:
触发: 脉冲工作器件切换脉宽/周期或外部IF门，量测报告中的功率偏低或与连续波结果不一致
对象：脉宽、周期、RF/IF触发延迟和门宽、窄带/宽带检测模式、脉冲校准状态与功率显示模式
目标：确定报告为真实脉冲峰值还是占空比平均功率，并恢复与目标规格同义的可发布测量
输入：脉冲设置及其校准快照、检测模式、IF门宽/延迟、显示True Power选项与仪器型号、测得功率、项目规定峰值或平均功率及容差

environment.description:
触发: 为加快噪声系数测试而修改Noise Bandwidth后，器件通带边缘NF出现异常峰或相对旧批次偏移
对象：旧/新噪声带宽、校准快照、S21频率曲线、NF逐点曲线、窄带补偿设置
目标：确认异常是否来自校准带宽不一致和跨带宽增益变化，给出可比的NF结果或暂缓
输入：校准与测量Noise Bandwidth、实际接收带宽、DUT通带宽度/S21斜率、NF频点、仪器选件、补偿可用带宽、产品NF规格
步骤/决策：逐测次核校准与实测Noise Bandwidth，核仪器实际生效带宽及选件；不一致则冻结旧NF并按目标带宽重校。确认噪声带宽小于DUT带宽，检查边缘频点S21跨接收带宽变化；仅在选件和带宽支持时启用Narrowband Compensation，否则收窄带宽并重新量测；用独立验证件和项目NF规格判定，无证则待测。
验收：校准和测量噪声带宽一致且小于DUT带宽；边缘频点有跨带宽增益评估及适用的补偿/收窄带宽证据；仅按项目NF限值发布，缺证据时暂缓

basic_info.name: 高增益RF器件NF测试中无告警接收机压缩的复测分流

environment.description:
触发: 更换高增益器件或改变源功率/接收衰减后，NF与增益出现异常平坦或批次偏移但仪器没有过载告警
对象：带电DUT、NF通道S参数测量的B接收机电平、源/接收衰减及校准/测量开关状态
目标：排除VNA接收机压缩造成的伪增益与伪NF，再决定DUT合格或复测
输入：B,1绝对接收功率、DUT输出功率及已知压缩边界、源/接收衰减、校准与测量路径开关状态、S21/NF曲线和产品限值
步骤/决策：在带电DUT下显示B,1并记录接收电平；核对接收电平落在手册建议的低抖动且未压缩区间，并让DUT输出远离自身压缩点；若B接收机过高，调整源/接收衰减并检查校准与测量步进衰减器和开关位置一致；重新执行受影响NF校准及量测，交叉检查独立参考件/基线；无法证明接收机线性时，不用无告警NF或S21值放行DUT
验收：记录带电DUT的B,1接收电平、DUT输出相对其压缩点的余量，以及校准/测量步进衰减器和配置开关状态；以对应固件/选件的线性边界及项目规格复测S21/NF。无S参数压缩告警不等于线性；缺状态或复测证据时仅待判。

init_ref_tools.name: Circuit
init_ref_tools.description: Creates a circuit made of a set of N-ports networks.  For instructions on how to create Circuit see :func:`__init__`.  A Circuit object is representation a circuit assembly of an arbitrary number of N-ports networks connected together via an arbitrary topology.  The algorithm used to calculate the resultant network can be found in [#]_.  References ---------- .. [#] P. Hallbjörner, Microw. Opt. Technol. Lett. 38, 99 (2003).

function.name: __init__
function.description: Circuit constructor. Creates a circuit made of a set of N-ports networks.

connections.description: Description of circuit connections. Each connection is a described by a list of tuple. Each tuple contains (network, network_port_nb). Port number indexing starts from zero. Network's port not explicitly listed will be treated as matched. Network's port listed individually will be treated as open.

name.description: Name assigned to the circuit (Network). Default is None.

auto_reduce.description: If True, the circuit will be automatically reduced using :func:`reduce_circuit`. This will change the circuit connections description, affecting inner current and voltage distributions. Suitable for cases where only the S-parameters of the final circuit ports are of interest. Default is False. If `check_duplication`, `split_ground` or `max_nports` are provided as kwargs, `auto_reduce` will be automatically set to True, as this indicates an intent to use the `reduce_circuit` method.

kwargs.description: keyword arguments passed to `reduce_circuit` method.  check_duplication : boolean. Default is True. Controls whether to check the connections have duplicate names. split_ground : boolean. Default is False. Controls whether to split the global ground connection to independent. split_multi : boolean, optional. If True, use a splitter to handle connections involving more than two components. This approach increases the computational load for individual computations. However, it proves advantageous for batch processing by enabling a more comprehensive reduction of circuits, leading to more efficiency in batch computations. Default is False. max_nports : int. Default is 20. Controls the maximum number of ports of a Network that can be reduced in circuit. If a Network in the circuit has a number of ports (nports), using the Network.connect() method to reduce the circuit's dimensions becomes less efficient compared to directly calculating it with Circuit.s_external. This value depends on the performance of the computer and the scale of the circuit. dynamic_networks : tuple. Default is an empty tuple. Sequence of Networks to be skipped during the reduction process.

Examples -------- Example of connections between two 1-port networks::  connections = [ [(network1, 0), (network2, 0)], ]  Example of a connection between three 1-port networks connected to a single node::  connections = [ [(network1, 0), (network2, 0), (network3, 0)] ]  Example of a connection between two 1-port networks (port1 and port2) and two 2-ports networks (ntw1 and ntw2)::  connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw1, 0)], [(ntw1, 1), (ntw2, 0)], [(ntw2, 1), (port2, 0)] ]  Example of a connection between three 1-port networks (port1, port2 and port3) and a 3-ports network (ntw)::  connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw, 0)], [(port2, 0), (ntw, 1)], [(port3, 0), (ntw, 2)] ]  Example of a connection between three 1-port networks (port1, port2 and open) and a 3-ports network (ntw)::  connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw, 0)], [(open, 0), (ntw, 1)], [(port2, 0), (ntw, 2)] ] # or equivalently connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw, 0)], [(ntw, 1)], [(port2, 0), (ntw, 2)] ]  Example of a connection between three 1-port networks (port1, port2 and match) and a 3-ports network (ntw)::  connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw, 0)], [(match, 0), (ntw, 1)], [(port2, 0), (ntw, 2)] ] # or equivalently connections = [ [(port1, 0), (ntw, 0)], [(port2, 0), (ntw, 2)] ]  NB1: Creating 1-port network to be used as a port should be made with :func:`Port`  NB2: The external ports indexing is defined by the order of appearance of the ports in the connections list. Thus, the first network identified as a port will be the 1st port of the resulting network (index 0), the second network identified as a port will be the second port (index 1), etc.  NB3: When a port of a network is listed individually in the connections, the circuit will treat this port with a reflection coefficient of 1, equivalent to an Open. Conversely, if a port is not explicitly included in the connections,the circuit will treat it as matched.

init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: 更换高增益器件或改变源功率/接收衰减后，NF与增益出现异常平坦或批次偏移但仪器没有过载告警
对象：带电DUT、NF通道S参数测量的B接收机电平、源/接收衰减及校准/测量开关状态
目标：排除VNA接收机压缩造成的伪增益与伪NF，再决定DUT合格或复测
输入：B,1绝对接收功率、DUT输出功率及已知压缩边界、源/接收衰减、校准与测量路径开关状态、S21/NF曲线和产品限值
步骤/决策：在带电DUT下显示B,1并记录接收电平；核对接收电平落在手册建议的低抖动且未压缩区间，并让DUT输出远离自身压缩点；若B接收机过高，调整源/接收衰减并检查校准与测量步进衰减器和开关位置一致；重新执行受影响NF校准及量测，交叉检查独立参考件/基线；无法证明接收机线性时，不用无告警NF或S21值放行DUT
验收：记录带电DUT的B,1接收电平、DUT输出相对其压缩点的余量，以及校准/测量步进衰减器和配置开关状态；以对应固件/选件的线性边界及项目规格复测S21/NF。无S参数压缩告警不等于线性；缺状态或复测证据时仅待判。

可合成任务：输入：B,1绝对接收功率、DUT输出功率及已知压缩边界、源/接收衰减、校准与测量路径开关状态、S21/NF曲线和产品限值
Python核心操作/决策：Python可审计功率/衰减/状态日志并标记可疑频点；实际接收机线性验证及NF实测需VNA
输出：接收机线性资格、受影响S21/NF测次、重校/复测或DUT放行决定
可复核验收：记录带电DUT的B,1接收电平、DUT输出相对其压缩点的余量，以及校准/测量步进衰减器和配置开关状态；以对应固件/选件的线性边界及项目规格复测S21/NF。无S参数压缩告警不等于线性；缺状态或复测证据时仅待判。

environment.description:
触发: 变频器/封装测试更换外部LO为仪器内部源或改变LO分配链后，NFX噪声系数升高而转换损耗变化不明显
对象：LO源型号及连接、LO驱动设定、原始/新NFX校准与NF/SC21曲线
目标：判断NF升高是否由LO源噪声污染而非DUT缺陷，并恢复可比较的器件验收
输入：LO来源和相噪/噪声证据、LO功率/频率配置、输入输出频率映射、NF及转换损耗、NFX校准状态、产品LO条件与NF限值
步骤/决策：确认测试前后LO源、频率和功率及变频映射；对相同DUT用受控低噪声LO和新LO交替测NF/转换损耗，保持其余路径和温度不变；若NF随LO更换而变化，先按项目指定LO源恢复并按该配置重校复测，不把新LO下NF升高直接归因器件；若稳定低噪声LO和独立验证件通过后DUT仍不合格，再交DUT调查；未有指定LO条件或源噪声证据时标为待判
验收：LO源/功率/频率和测试拓扑绑定每次NF数据；对照试验控制DUT与路径条件；LO噪声改变时旧NF不直接用于器件淘汰；按指定LO条件和项目限值最终签核
