function.description: @brief Iterates over the nets of the circuit
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over the nets of the circuit

function.name: net_by_name
function.description: @brief Gets the net object for a given name. If the ID is not a valid net name, nil is returned.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the net object for a given name. If the ID is not a valid net name, nil is returned.

function.name: nets_by_name
function.description: @brief Gets the net objects for a given name filter. The name filter is a glob pattern. This method will return all \Net objects matching the glob pattern. The 'case_sensitive' argument will control whether the name is looked up in a case sensitive way or not. Note that with case insensitive search on a netlist that is case sensitive, the same name may render more than one hit. By default, case sensitivity is taken from the netlist.  This method has been introduced in version 0.27.3. The 'case_sensitive' argument has been added in version 0.30.2.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the net objects for a given name filter. The name filter is a glob pattern. This method will return all \Net objects matching the glob pattern. The 'case_sensitive' argument will control whether the name is looked up in a case sensitive way or not. Note that with case insensitive search on a netlist that is case sensitive, the same name may render more than one hit. By default, case sensitivity is taken from the netlist.  This method has been introduced in version 0.27.3. The 'case_sensitive' argument has been added in version 0.30.2.

Terminals are connections made to specific terminals of devices.  Net objects are created inside a circuit with \Circuit#create_net. To connect a net to a terminal of a device, use \Device#connect_terminal, to disconnect a net from a terminal of a device, use \Device#disconnect_terminal. environment.description:

init_ref_tools.name: LayoutToNetlist
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A framework for extracting netlists from layouts  This class provides a framework for extracting a netlist from a layout.  A LayoutToNetlist object extracts a netlist from an external \Layout. To do so, it keeps an internal copy with an optimized representation of the original layout. When a netlist is extracted the net geometries can be recovered from that internal layout. In addition to that layout, it keeps the extracted netlist. Netlist and internal layout form a pair and there are references between them. For example, the \Circuit objects from the netlist have an attribute \cell_index, which tells what cell from the internal layout the circuit was derived from. In the same way, subcircuit references refer to cell instances and nets keep a reference to the shapes they were derived from.  LayoutToNetlist can also operate in detached mode, when there is no external layout. In this mode, layers are created inside the internal layout only. As there is no input hierarchy, operation is necessarily flat in that case. Single \Region and \Texts shape collections can be introduced into the LayoutToNetlist objects from external sources to populate the layers from the internal layout. For detached mode, use the 'LayoutToNetlist(topcell, dbu)' constructor.  Usually, the internal layout is stored inside an internal \DeepShapeStore object, which supplies additional services such as layer lifetime management and maintains the connection to and from the external layout. However, you can also use the extractor with an existing \DeepShapeStore object. In that case, this external \DeepShapeStore object is used instead of the internal one.  The LayoutToNetlist object can be persisted into a 'Layout to netlist database' file. This database is a storage for both the netlist and the net or circuit geometries. When reading such file into a new LayoutToNetlist object, there will be no connection to any external layout, but all the essential netlist and geometry information will be available.  The \LayoutToNetlist object is also the entry point for netlist-driven algorithms such as antenna checks.  The use model of the LayoutToNetlist object consists of five steps which need to be executed in this order.  @ul @li @b Configuration: @/b In this step, the LayoutToNetlist object is created and if required, configured. Methods to be used in this step are \threads=, \area_ratio= or \max_vertex_count=. The constructor for the LayoutToNetlist object receives a \RecursiveShapeIterator object which basically supplies the hierarchy and the external layout taken as input. The constructor will initialize the internal layout and connect it to the external one. @/li @li @b Preparation: @/b In this step, the device recognition and extraction layers are drawn from the framework. Derived layers can now be computed using boolean operations. Methods to use in this step are \make_layer and its variants. \make_layer will either create a new, empty layer or pull a layer from the external layout into the internal layout. Derived layers are computed using the \Region or \Texts objects representing existing layers. If derived layers are to be used in connectivity, they need to be registered using \register. This makes the LayoutToNetlist object the owner of the layer (the layer is said to be persisted then). Registered layers can or should be given a name. That helps indentifying them later. Layer preparation is not necessarily required to happen before all other steps. Layers can be computed shortly before they are required. @/li @li @b Device extraction: @/b Following the preparation, the devices can be extracted using \extract_devices. This method needs to be called for each device extractor required. Each time, a device extractor needs to be given, plus a map of device layers. The device layers are device extractor specific. Either original or derived layers may be specified here. Layer preparation may happen between calls to \extract_devices. @/li @li @b Connectivity definition: @/b Once the devices are derived, the netlist connectivity can be defined and the netlist extracted. The connectivity is defined with \connect and its flavours. The actual netlist extraction happens with \extract_netlist. @/li @li @b Netlist extraction: @/b After netlist extraction, the information is ready to be retrieved. The produced netlist is available with \netlist. The Shapes of a specific net are available with \shapes_of_net. \probe_net allows finding a net by probing a specific location. @/li @/ul  Once the extraction is done, you can persist the \LayoutToNetlist object using \write and restore it using \read. You can use the query API (see below) to analyze the LayoutToNetlist database.  The query API of the \LayoutToNetlist object consists of the following parts:  @ul @li Net shape retrieval: \build_all_nets, \build_nets, \build_net and \shapes_of_net @/li @li Layers: \layer_by_index, \layer_by_name, \layer_indexes, \layer_names, \layer_info, \layer_name @/li @li Log entries: \each_log_entry @/li @li Probing (get net from position): \probe_net @/li @li Netlist: \netlist @/li @li Internal shape storage: \internal_layout, \internal_top_cell @/li @li Helper functions: \cell_mapping_into, \const_cell_mapping_into @/li @/ul  Layers stored inside the LayoutToNetlist object are addressed in three ways:  @ul @li Through a layer index: this is an integer number that addresses the layer. Technically this is the layer index inside the internal layout (see \internal_layout). To get a layer index from a shape collection or name use \layer_index. To get all layer indexes available, use \layer_indexes. Note, that \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer and \make_text_layer also take a layer index, but this the layer index of layer in the \original_layout. @/li @li Through a name: Alternatively to the layer index, a layer can be addressed by name, provided one was assigned. To assign a name, specify one when creating a layer with \register, \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer or \make_text_layer. To get the layer index of a named layer, use \layer_index. To get the name of a layer use \layer_name. To get the names of all layers, use \layer_names. @/li @li As a shape collection: a layer can also be represented by a shape collection. A shape collection is either a \Region or a \Texts object. These objects do not only represent a layer, but can be used to derive new layers or do computations on layers. In order to assign names to derived shape collections, use \register. To create a new layer and a corresponding shape collection object, use \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer or \make_text_layer. To get the shape collection for a given layer index, use \layer_index, to get layer name from a shape collection, use \layer_name. To get a shape collection from a layer index, use \layer_by_index, \polygons_by_index or \texts_by_index. @/li @/ul  This class has been introduced in version 0.26.

function.name: __init__
function.description: @brief Creates a new extractor object reusing an existing \DeepShapeStore object This constructor can be used if there is a DSS object already from which the shapes can be taken. This version can only be used with \register to add layers (regions) inside the 'dss' object.  The make_... methods will not create new layers as there is no particular place defined where to create the layers.  The extractor will not take ownership of the dss object unless you call \keep_dss.
function.ori_description: @brief Creates a new extractor object reusing an existing \DeepShapeStore object This constructor can be used if there is a DSS object already from which the shapes can be taken. This version can only be used with \register to add layers (regions) inside the 'dss' object.  The make_... methods will not create new layers as there is no particular place defined where to create the layers.  The extractor will not take ownership of the dss object unless you call \keep_dss.

function.name: register
function.description: @brief Names the given layer

return.description: The index of the layer registered 'l' must be a \Region or \Texts object. Flat regions or text collections must be registered with this function, before they can be used in \connect. Registering will copy the shapes into the LayoutToNetlist object in this step to enable netlist extraction.  External \Region or \Texts objects that are registered are persisted. This means the LayoutToNetlist object becomes owner of them and they are not discarded when the Region or Text object is destroyed.  Naming a layer allows allows retrieving the layer later, for example after the LayoutToNetlist object has been written to a file and restored from that file (during this process, the layer indexes will change).  If no name is given, the system will assign a name automatically. It is recommended to specify a name if it is required to identify the layer later - for example for retrieving shapes from it.  This method has been generalized in version 0.27. Starting with version 0.29.3, the index of the layer is returned.

init_ref_tools.name: Net
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A single net. A net connects multiple pins or terminals together. Pins are either pin or subcircuits of outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in. Terminals are connections made to specific terminals of devices.  Net objects are created inside a circuit with \Circuit#create_net.  To connect a net to an outgoing pin of a circuit, use \Circuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from an outgoing pin use \Circuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a terminal of a device, use \Device#connect_terminal, to disconnect a net from a terminal of a device, use \Device#disconnect_terminal.  This class has been added in version 0.26.

function.name: qname
function.description: @brief Gets the qualified name. The qualified name is like the expanded name, but the circuit's name is preceded (i.e. 'CIRCUIT:NET') if available.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the qualified name. The qualified name is like the expanded name, but the circuit's name is preceded (i.e. 'CIRCUIT:NET') if available.

function.name: each_pin
function.description: @brief Iterates over all outgoing pins the net connects. Pin connections are described by \NetPinRef objects. Pin connections are connections to outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in.
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over all outgoing pins the net connects. Pin connections are described by \NetPinRef objects. Pin connections are connections to outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in.

function.name: each_terminal
function.description: @brief Iterates over all terminals the net connects. Terminals connect devices. Terminal connections are described by \NetTerminalRef objects.
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over all terminals the net connects. Terminals connect devices. Terminal connections are described by \NetTerminalRef objects.

function.description: @brief Returns the number of outgoing pins connected by this net.
function.ori_description: @brief Returns the number of outgoing pins connected by this net.

function.name: terminal_count
function.description: @brief Returns the number of terminals connected by this net.
function.ori_description: @brief Returns the number of terminals connected by this net.

function.name: is_floating

function.ori_description: @brief Returns true, if the net is floating. Floating nets are those which don't have any device or subcircuit on it and are not connected through a pin.

init_ref_tools.name: Netlist
init_ref_tools.description: @brief The netlist top-level class A netlist is a hierarchical structure of circuits. At least one circuit is the top-level circuit, other circuits may be referenced as subcircuits. Circuits are created with \create_circuit and are represented by objects of the \Circuit class.  Beside circuits, the netlist manages device classes. Device classes describe specific types of devices. Device classes are represented by objects of the \DeviceClass class and are created using \create_device_class.  The netlist class has been introduced with version 0.26.

function.description: @brief Iterates over the circuits of the netlist
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over the circuits of the netlist

function.ori_description: @brief Gets the top circuit. This method will return nil, if there is no top circuit. It will raise an error, if there is more than a single top circuit.  This convenience method has been added in version 0.29.5.

init_ref_tools.name: Net
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A single net. A net connects multiple pins or terminals together. Pins are either pin or subcircuits of outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in. Terminals are connections made to specific terminals of devices.  Net objects are created inside a circuit with \Circuit#create_net.  To connect a net to an outgoing pin of a circuit, use \Circuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from an outgoing pin use \Circuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a terminal of a device, use \Device#connect_terminal, to disconnect a net from a terminal of a device, use \Device#disconnect_terminal.  This class has been added in version 0.26.

environment.description:
触发: 宏内部被blackbox替换后，目标PDK衬底/pwell层在每个宏仍形成抽取pin或隐式连接，LVS报告存在无名substrate网/警告

init_ref_tools.name: Box
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A box class with integer coordinates This object represents a box (a rectangular shape). The definition of the attributes is: p1 is the lower left point, p2 the upper right one. If a box is constructed from two points (or four coordinates), the coordinates are sorted accordingly. A box can be empty. An empty box represents no area (not even a point). Empty boxes behave neutral with respect to most operations. Empty boxes return true on \empty?. A box can be a point or a single line. In this case, the area is zero but the box still can overlap other boxes for example and it is not empty. See @The Database API@ for more details about the database objects.

init_ref_tools.name: Circuit
init_ref_tools.description: @brief Circuits are the basic building blocks of the netlist A circuit has pins by which it can connect to the outside. Pins are created using \create_pin and are represented by the \Pin class.  Furthermore, a circuit manages the components of the netlist. Components are devices (class \Device) and subcircuits (class \SubCircuit). Devices are basic devices such as resistors or transistors. Subcircuits are other circuits to which nets from this circuit connect. Devices are created using the \create_device method. Subcircuits are created using the \create_subcircuit method.  Devices are connected through 'terminals', subcircuits are connected through their pins. Terminals and pins are described by integer ID's in the context of most methods.  Finally, the circuit consists of the nets. Nets connect terminals of devices and pins of subcircuits or the circuit itself. Nets are created using \create_net and are represented by objects of the \Net class. See there for more about nets.  The Circuit object is only valid if the netlist object is alive. Circuits must be added to a netlist using \Netlist#add to become part of the netlist.  The Circuit class has been introduced in version 0.26.

function.name: each_net
function.description: @brief Iterates over the nets of the circuit
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over the nets of the circuit

function.name: net_by_name
function.description: @brief Gets the net object for a given name. If the ID is not a valid net name, nil is returned.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the net object for a given name. If the ID is not a valid net name, nil is returned.

function.name: nets_by_name
function.description: @brief Gets the net objects for a given name filter. The name filter is a glob pattern. This method will return all \Net objects matching the glob pattern. The 'case_sensitive' argument will control whether the name is looked up in a case sensitive way or not. Note that with case insensitive search on a netlist that is case sensitive, the same name may render more than one hit. By default, case sensitivity is taken from the netlist.  This method has been introduced in version 0.27.3. The 'case_sensitive' argument has been added in version 0.30.2.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the net objects for a given name filter. The name filter is a glob pattern. This method will return all \Net objects matching the glob pattern. The 'case_sensitive' argument will control whether the name is looked up in a case sensitive way or not. Note that with case insensitive search on a netlist that is case sensitive, the same name may render more than one hit. By default, case sensitivity is taken from the netlist.  This method has been introduced in version 0.27.3. The 'case_sensitive' argument has been added in version 0.30.2.

function.name: net_by_cluster_id
function.description: @brief Gets the net object corresponding to a specific cluster ID If the ID is not a valid pin cluster ID, nil is returned.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the net object corresponding to a specific cluster ID If the ID is not a valid pin cluster ID, nil is returned.

function.name: each_pin
function.description: @brief Iterates over the pins of the circuit
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over the pins of the circuit

function.name: pin_count
function.description: @brief Gets the number of pins in the circuit
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the number of pins in the circuit

init_ref_tools.name: Net
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A single net. A net connects multiple pins or terminals together. Pins are either pin or subcircuits of outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in. Terminals are connections made to specific terminals of devices.  Net objects are created inside a circuit with \Circuit#create_net.  To connect a net to an outgoing pin of a circuit, use \Circuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from an outgoing pin use \Circuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#connect_pin, to disconnect a net from a pin of a subcircuit, use \SubCircuit#disconnect_pin. To connect a net to a terminal of a device, use \Device#connect_terminal, to disconnect a net from a terminal of a device, use \Device#disconnect_terminal.  This class has been added in version 0.26.

function.name: qname
function.description: @brief Gets the qualified name. The qualified name is like the expanded name, but the circuit's name is preceded (i.e. 'CIRCUIT:NET') if available.
function.ori_description: @brief Gets the qualified name. The qualified name is like the expanded name, but the circuit's name is preceded (i.e. 'CIRCUIT:NET') if available.

function.name: each_pin
function.description: @brief Iterates over all outgoing pins the net connects. Pin connections are described by \NetPinRef objects. Pin connections are connections to outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in.
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over all outgoing pins the net connects. Pin connections are described by \NetPinRef objects. Pin connections are connections to outgoing pins of the circuit the net lives in.

function.name: each_terminal
function.description: @brief Iterates over all terminals the net connects. Terminals connect devices. Terminal connections are described by \NetTerminalRef objects.
function.ori_description: @brief Iterates over all terminals the net connects. Terminals connect devices. Terminal connections are described by \NetTerminalRef objects.

function.name: pin_count
function.description: @brief Returns the number of outgoing pins connected by this net.
function.ori_description: @brief Returns the number of outgoing pins connected by this net.

function.name: terminal_count
function.description: @brief Returns the number of terminals connected by this net.
function.ori_description: @brief Returns the number of terminals connected by this net.

function.name: is_floating
function.description: @brief Returns true, if the net is floating. Floating nets are those which don't have any device or subcircuit on it and are not connected through a pin.
function.ori_description: @brief Returns true, if the net is floating. Floating nets are those which don't have any device or subcircuit on it and are not connected through a pin.

init_ref_tools.name: LayoutToNetlist
init_ref_tools.description: @brief A framework for extracting netlists from layouts  This class provides a framework for extracting a netlist from a layout.  A LayoutToNetlist object extracts a netlist from an external \Layout. To do so, it keeps an internal copy with an optimized representation of the original layout. When a netlist is extracted the net geometries can be recovered from that internal layout. In addition to that layout, it keeps the extracted netlist. Netlist and internal layout form a pair and there are references between them. For example, the \Circuit objects from the netlist have an attribute \cell_index, which tells what cell from the internal layout the circuit was derived from. In the same way, subcircuit references refer to cell instances and nets keep a reference to the shapes they were derived from.  LayoutToNetlist can also operate in detached mode, when there is no external layout. In this mode, layers are created inside the internal layout only. As there is no input hierarchy, operation is necessarily flat in that case. Single \Region and \Texts shape collections can be introduced into the LayoutToNetlist objects from external sources to populate the layers from the internal layout. For detached mode, use the 'LayoutToNetlist(topcell, dbu)' constructor.  Usually, the internal layout is stored inside an internal \DeepShapeStore object, which supplies additional services such as layer lifetime management and maintains the connection to and from the external layout. However, you can also use the extractor with an existing \DeepShapeStore object. In that case, this external \DeepShapeStore object is used instead of the internal one.  The LayoutToNetlist object can be persisted into a 'Layout to netlist database' file. This database is a storage for both the netlist and the net or circuit geometries. When reading such file into a new LayoutToNetlist object, there will be no connection to any external layout, but all the essential netlist and geometry information will be available.  The \LayoutToNetlist object is also the entry point for netlist-driven algorithms such as antenna checks.  The use model of the LayoutToNetlist object consists of five steps which need to be executed in this order.  @ul @li @b Configuration: @/b In this step, the LayoutToNetlist object is created and if required, configured. Methods to be used in this step are \threads=, \area_ratio= or \max_vertex_count=. The constructor for the LayoutToNetlist object receives a \RecursiveShapeIterator object which basically supplies the hierarchy and the external layout taken as input. The constructor will initialize the internal layout and connect it to the external one. @/li @li @b Preparation: @/b In this step, the device recognition and extraction layers are drawn from the framework. Derived layers can now be computed using boolean operations. Methods to use in this step are \make_layer and its variants. \make_layer will either create a new, empty layer or pull a layer from the external layout into the internal layout. Derived layers are computed using the \Region or \Texts objects representing existing layers. If derived layers are to be used in connectivity, they need to be registered using \register. This makes the LayoutToNetlist object the owner of the layer (the layer is said to be persisted then). Registered layers can or should be given a name. That helps indentifying them later. Layer preparation is not necessarily required to happen before all other steps. Layers can be computed shortly before they are required. @/li @li @b Device extraction: @/b Following the preparation, the devices can be extracted using \extract_devices. This method needs to be called for each device extractor required. Each time, a device extractor needs to be given, plus a map of device layers. The device layers are device extractor specific. Either original or derived layers may be specified here. Layer preparation may happen between calls to \extract_devices. @/li @li @b Connectivity definition: @/b Once the devices are derived, the netlist connectivity can be defined and the netlist extracted. The connectivity is defined with \connect and its flavours. The actual netlist extraction happens with \extract_netlist. @/li @li @b Netlist extraction: @/b After netlist extraction, the information is ready to be retrieved. The produced netlist is available with \netlist. The Shapes of a specific net are available with \shapes_of_net. \probe_net allows finding a net by probing a specific location. @/li @/ul  Once the extraction is done, you can persist the \LayoutToNetlist object using \write and restore it using \read. You can use the query API (see below) to analyze the LayoutToNetlist database.  The query API of the \LayoutToNetlist object consists of the following parts:  @ul @li Net shape retrieval: \build_all_nets, \build_nets, \build_net and \shapes_of_net @/li @li Layers: \layer_by_index, \layer_by_name, \layer_indexes, \layer_names, \layer_info, \layer_name @/li @li Log entries: \each_log_entry @/li @li Probing (get net from position): \probe_net @/li @li Netlist: \netlist @/li @li Internal shape storage: \internal_layout, \internal_top_cell @/li @li Helper functions: \cell_mapping_into, \const_cell_mapping_into @/li @/ul  Layers stored inside the LayoutToNetlist object are addressed in three ways:  @ul @li Through a layer index: this is an integer number that addresses the layer. Technically this is the layer index inside the internal layout (see \internal_layout). To get a layer index from a shape collection or name use \layer_index. To get all layer indexes available, use \layer_indexes. Note, that \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer and \make_text_layer also take a layer index, but this the layer index of layer in the \original_layout. @/li @li Through a name: Alternatively to the layer index, a layer can be addressed by name, provided one was assigned. To assign a name, specify one when creating a layer with \register, \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer or \make_text_layer. To get the layer index of a named layer, use \layer_index. To get the name of a layer use \layer_name. To get the names of all layers, use \layer_names. @/li @li As a shape collection: a layer can also be represented by a shape collection. A shape collection is either a \Region or a \Texts object. These objects do not only represent a layer, but can be used to derive new layers or do computations on layers. In order to assign names to derived shape collections, use \register. To create a new layer and a corresponding shape collection object, use \make_layer, \make_polygon_layer or \make_text_layer. To get the shape collection for a given layer index, use \layer_index, to get layer name from a shape collection, use \layer_name. To get a shape collection from a layer index, use \layer_by_index, \polygons_by_index or \texts_by_index. @/li @/ul  This class has been introduced in version 0.26.

init_ref_tools.name: Circuit
init_ref_tools.description: @brief Circuits are the basic building blocks of the netlist A circuit has pins by which it can connect to the outside. Pins are created using \create_pin and are represented by the \Pin class.  Furthermore, a circuit manages the components of the netlist. Components are devices (class \Device) and subcircuits (class \SubCircuit). Devices are basic devices such as resistors or transistors. Subcircuits are other circuits to which nets from this circuit connect. Devices are created using the \create_device method. Subcircuits are created using the \create_subcircuit method.  Devices are connected through 'terminals', subcircuits are connected through their pins. Terminals and pins are described by integer ID's in the context of most methods.  Finally, the circuit consists of the nets. Nets connect terminals of devices and pins of subcircuits or the circuit itself. Nets are created using \create_net and are represented by objects of the \Net class. See there for more about nets.  The Circuit object is only valid if the netlist object is alive. Circuits must be added to a netlist using \Netlist#add to become part of the netlist.  The Circuit class has been introduced in version 0.26.

Note that with case insensitive search on a netlist that is case sensitive, the same name may render more than one hit. By default, case sensitivity is taken from the netlist. init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: LVS connectivity规则报告must-connect未满足、出现意外软连接或布线断裂
对象：版图几何、连接规则、抽取网表、原理图网络和connectivity报告
目标：区分真实断线/短接、工艺允许软连接与抽取规则错误，并决定返修或改规则配置
输入：must-connect/soft-connect报告、层间过孔、端口标签、版图层级、PDK连接规则
步骤/决策：按LVS连接报告与交叉引用定位网络、层级和几何；对connect_implicit检查待连接分段在上层是否真实合并，顶层剩余警告按项目top_level策略阻断；对soft_connect区分金属通路与well/implant/substrate高阻通路，核端口标签、过孔和PDK连接语句。几何未接或误短则返修版图；抽取规则与工艺事实不符则先冻结签核并由PDK负责人修规则；复抽取、复比较并保留连接告警处置证据。
验收：每条隐式或软连接告警回链层级、几何和PDK规则；子电路待连接应在批准的更高层闭合，顶层未闭合不得冒充clean；关键网络不可仅靠高阻soft path宣称金属连接；修复后完整LVS和连接告警按项目规则复核。

可合成任务：输入：must-connect/soft-connect报告、层间过孔、端口标签、版图层级、PDK连接规则
Python核心操作/决策：解析connectivity报告并生成网络图差异；版图连接抽取由KLayout/PDK原生引擎执行
输出：受影响网络、几何证据、连接规则依据、重抽取LVS结果
可复核验收：每条隐式或软连接告警回链层级、几何和PDK规则；子电路待连接应在批准的更高层闭合，顶层未闭合不得冒充clean；关键网络不可仅靠高阻soft path宣称金属连接；修复后完整LVS和连接告警按项目规则复核。

验收：复现引用同一GDS和PDK提交；两个deck的规则ID/标记可回溯；任何例外有所有者和版本；只有批准后受影响图形与回归均重跑；GitHub讨论中的个人解释不得直接当官方放行

basic_info.name: GF180提取规则升级后的逐单元LVS参考网表重定标

environment.description:
触发: 为取得新版ERC井/衬底tie能力升级GF180 klayout-tools，六个非冻结单元重新提取后四个LVS从match变mismatch
对象：固定原理图、同一版GDS、旧/新deck版本与哈希、参考网表生成脚本、六单元DRC/LVS和提取网表
目标：使参考网表准确表达新版提取deck的器件参数及真实体/井连接，并给出逐单元可解释LVS结论
输入：MiM几何面积/周长及电容系数、提取的a/p参数、NMOS/BJT体与井节点、每单元tap图形、旧参考变换规则、新旧LVS差异和deck哈希
步骤/决策：冻结原理图/GDS及旧新deck版本，重跑两套提取与LVS；逐失配核对MiM a/p及电容系数、实际tap几何和body/well连接，分离参考语义漂移、版图真缺陷和未判；只对几何/设计证据支持的单元修订参考变换，不能全局消除body_unverified；按新版deck逐单元复跑DRC/LVS并记录仍未判的连接；来源issue的诊断不能代替本项目验证。
验收：六单元均以同一记录的deck/工具版本和GDS复核；四个失配逐项归因，MiM参考a/p和电容律与新版提取一致；有真实tap与无tap单元分别处理，不能全局抹除body_unverified；最终LVS匹配或明确阻断，DRC全净不能替代此门

basic_info.name: 器件版图已补齐后撤销过时的原理图理想器件拼接

environment.description:
触发: GF180模拟块的版图器件覆盖扩展后，旧composite_netlist.py在当前.reference.spice上五单元皆解析失败，同时其拼接清单仍声称已画电阻未画
对象：有旧版MOS-only提取假设和复合拼接脚本、当前golden原理图/参考网表、当前GDS及提取报告、每单元已画/未画器件清单
目标：确保post-layout网表每个golden器件恰好来自正确的实物提取或明确标注的理想补件，并能在ngspice运行
输入：原理图和参考网表的M/R/Q/C/X器件、提取网表和device_classes、实例及层级映射、版图/PDK/deck版本、旧splice清单、LVS和smoke日志
步骤/决策：锁定同版原理图与GDS，逐单元比较golden器件多重集与实际提取器件；定位旧脚本对新C卡的KeyError和已画分压电阻的重复拼接风险；若仍有未画器件，逐一核准可否物理补画及理想拼接的节点映射/声明，若器件已全提取则撤销复合求解器；由LVS提供经验证的层级/匿名节点对应，转换为PDK可仿真卡并保留几何参数；重建网表、审核每种器件来源，跑LVS与nominal smoke及受影响后仿矩阵
验收：每个golden器件只出现一次且来源为drawn-extracted或经批准的ideal；新增C/R/Q类型不导致解析盲区；匿名及层级节点关联由LVS对应/可验证拓扑而非仅名称猜测；若仍有理想器件，所有后仿声明列出其范围；版本与网表哈希齐全且nominal仿真收敛，性能放行另需完整角落

basic_info.name: PDK MiM抽取规则修订后寄生电容归属与后仿资格复核

environment.description:
触发: IHP SG13G2 PDK/Magic抽取tech更版，或MiM电容附近布线的PEX网表出现与器件模型叠加的异常电容及TOP/BOT耦合归属颠倒
对象：冻结的MiM GDS测试图形、源网表和器件模型、旧新PDK/Magic版本、LVS/CDL与PEX提取变体、信号TOP/底板BOT/邻近BUS节点
目标：确认MiM模型本体与寄生只计一次，底板屏蔽和实际节点耦合归属正确；决定既有后仿/签核是否失效及何时可用新版证据替换
输入：issue复现几何和原始PEX网表、Magic抽取tech的variants/defaultareacap规则、MiM模型及尺寸、FasterCap或其它独立参考、旧新PEX网表、受影响电路测试台/规格
步骤/决策：锁定GDS、PDK/Magic和模型版本；分别抽取仅MiM及MiM下方布线的对照图形，在LVS/CDL和普通PEX变体记录器件模型电容与寄生卡；按节点对统计TOP-sub、TOP-BUS、BOT-BUS及TOP-BOT，核查旧版重复计数和底板屏蔽错分配；将修订版与解析估值/独立场求解参考比较，确认修订未让LVS/CDL所需值缺失；清点使用旧deck的后仿结果，重跑受影响的提取和电路指标，只有节点归属及规格均满足项目门限时重新签核；任何例外记录版本和批准人
验收：在同一GDS、模型、Magic和固定PDK提交上分别核LVS/CDL与普通PEX变体；关键电容卡按无向节点对追溯物理来源，MiM模型主电容不得以TOP-sub寄生重复出现，底板屏蔽下BUS耦合不得错归TOP；旧后仿按受影响deck版本清点并在目标电路重抽取/重仿后才可更新签核。PR已合并或main规则变化本身不等于目标设计通过。

environment.description:
触发: 布线与DRC/LVS已通过后，PDK的RC提取规则或校准模型更新，准备把新的SPEF交给STA
对象：同一已冻结路由布局、旧/新提取规则版本、已批准时序约束和旧签核SPEF/报告
目标：判定新RC规则造成的寄生与时序变化是否可接受，或保持旧版PDK并要求重新校准/签核
输入：布局及LEF/DEF哈希、旧新RC规则/PDK提交哈希、各批准角落SPEF、Liberty/SDC版本和路径报告
步骤/决策：固定同一布局及STA输入，用旧新RC规则分别抽取并生成SPEF；按net/path比较电阻、耦合/对地电容和关键路径裕量；若新增约束违规或超项目校准容差，暂停新PDK交接并维持已批准版本，要求校准证据或设计修复后全量重签；若通过项目门槛，记录规则版本和下游STA签核结果后切换版本
验收：新旧抽取和STA比较绑定同一布局、Liberty、SDC及各角落；每份SPEF/时序报告回链RC规则、PDK提交及工具版本；新增违规或超项目容差不得以DRC/LVS clean放行；回退旧版时旧规则/SPEF/报告必须同版，修复后再按批准范围重签。

environment.description:
触发: 升级PDK后，使用标准单元的抽取SPICE网表在ngspice中行为异常，但此前布线和版图签核完成
对象：同一设计的前后PDK标准单元LEF/CDL/SPICE视图、Magic抽取网表、ngspice测试平台和旧版仿真基线
目标：判断异常是否来自特定流的pin映射错误，选择修视图/转换器并重验或回退PDK
输入：单元各视图端口语义与顺序、实例连接、抽取网表、测试激励和期望波形、PDK提交哈希
步骤/决策：固定设计和激励，定位首个行为异常单元；按端口名称和功能比较LEF、CDL、SPICE定义与实际提取实例的节点位置；用最小单元测试验证假设，不单凭文本顺序差异判bug；若映射导致错误，修视图/转换规则并重跑抽取和仿真，未批准前保持旧PDK；若映射正确则转电路/模型调试；通过后记录受影响单元范围和完整回归结果
验收：单元端口功能、LEF/CDL/SPICE定义、Magic抽取X实例位置和ngspice .SUBCKT映射可逐项回链；相同设计/激励下最小单元和受影响设计在修复后满足项目参考行为；未证实映射因果时不声明pin-order根因或新版仿真签核通过；回退旧PDK须和旧签核包同版。

basic_info.name: 外部子电路实现替换后的引脚契约与功能仿真发布

environment.description:
触发: 层次原理图中已用的模拟宏需要改用第三方或另一团队交付的外部SPICE子电路实现
对象：旧原理图/网表、外部.subckt定义、Xschem符号、端口合同、受控测试台与现用PDK
目标：确认替换后端口连线和功能指标仍符合模块合同，决定发布或退回外部实现
输入：子电路端口顺序/名称、符号pinlist/sim_pinnumber、顶层连接、旧/新网表、PDK模型、相同激励/负载和规格
步骤/决策：先逐项核对外部.subckt声明的端口名称/顺序、Xschem符号I/O与顶层网络；若使用sim_pinnumber，所有符号引脚都须配置且编号不重复，否则明确按实际网表端口顺序检查。映射缺失、重复或对调时阻断；生成替换后层次网表并记录模型和测试台版本；以同一受控激励/负载和项目规格运行旧/新实现的指定工作点、AC或瞬态分析；检查ngspice日志错误、预期输出向量及数值结果，不能仅凭退出码0通过；缺真实仿真时只交付静态映射待验证。
验收：外部.subckt每个端口与符号引脚、顶层网络一一对应且实际网表顺序可复核；测试台、模型版本、激励/负载和项目规格锁定；替换后真实SPICE运行须有完整工作点/波形/指标，日志无阻断错误且按项目规格通过，失败或缺输出则回退/待验；静态引脚核查不等于功能发布。

init_ref_tools.name: netlist
init_ref_tools.description: Netlist proto-Package `pkg` to destination `dest`.  Example usages: ```python h.netlist(pkg, dest=open('mynetlist.v', 'w'), fmt='verilog') ``` ```python s = StringIO() h.netlist(pkg, dest=s, fmt='spectre') ``` ```python import sys h.netlist(pkg, dest=sys.stdout, fmt='spice') ```  Primary argument `pkg` must be a `vlsir.circuit.Package`. Destination `dest` may be anything that supports the `typing.IO` bundle, commonly including open file-handles. `StringIO` is particularly helpful for producing a netlist in an in-memory string. init_ref_tools.name: ExternalModule
init_ref_tools.description: # External Module  Wrapper for circuits defined outside Hdl21, such as: * Inclusion of existing SPICE or Verilog netlists * Foundry or technology-specific primitives  Unlike `Modules`, `ExternalModules` include parameters to support legacy HDLs. Said parameters may only take on a limited number of datatypes, and may not be nested. Each `ExternalModule` stores a parameter-type field `paramtype`. Parameter types may be either `hdl21.paramclass`es or the built-in `dict`. Parameter-values are checked to be instances of `paramtype` at creation time.

init_ref_tools.description: # Hdl21 Netlisting  Netlist one or more Hdl21 `Elaboratable`s - typically `Module`s - or a VLSIR `Package` to destination `dest`. init_ref_tools.name: netlist
init_ref_tools.description: Netlist proto-Package `pkg` to destination `dest`.  Example usages: ```python h.netlist(pkg, dest=open('mynetlist.v', 'w'), fmt='verilog') ``` ```python s = StringIO() h.netlist(pkg, dest=s, fmt='spectre') ``` ```python import sys h.netlist(pkg, dest=sys.stdout, fmt='spice') ```  Primary argument `pkg` must be a `vlsir.circuit.Package`. Destination `dest` may be anything that supports the `typing.IO` bundle, commonly including open file-handles. `StringIO` is particularly helpful for producing a netlist in an in-memory string. Format-specifier `fmt` may be any of the `NetlistFormatSpec` enumerated values or their string equivalents.
init_ref_tools.ori_input: pkg: Netlistable, dest: IO, fmt: NetlistFormatSpec = 'spectre', opts: Optional[NetlistOptions] = None
init_ref_tools.ori_description: Netlist proto-Package `pkg` to destination `dest`.  Example usages: ```python h.netlist(pkg, dest=open('mynetlist.v', 'w'), fmt='verilog') ``` ```python s = StringIO() h.netlist(pkg, dest=s, fmt='spectre') ``` ```python import sys h.netlist(pkg, dest=sys.stdout, fmt='spice') ```  Primary argument `pkg` must be a `vlsir.circuit.Package`. Destination `dest` may be anything that supports the `typing.IO` bundle, commonly including open file-handles. `StringIO` is particularly helpful for producing a netlist in an in-memory string. Format-specifier `fmt` may be any of the `NetlistFormatSpec` enumerated values or their string equivalents.

basic_info.name: Xschem版本漂移后阻断不可仿真的原理图网表

environment.description:
触发: 夜间网表检查将未改动的四个TRNG单元标为STALE，重新导出的sky130器件面积参数变为expr(...)字符串
对象：冻结的四份原理图和既有可仿真提交网表、PDK版本、CI中的Xschem版本以及ngspice测试台
目标：判断差异是设计变更还是网表器语义漂移，保证交给仿真和下游版图流程的网表可执行

init_ref_tools.name: Simulator
init_ref_tools.description: Simulator(toplevel)  Simulator for Amaranth designs.  The simulator accepts a *top-level design* (an :ref:`elaboratable <lang-elaboration>`), *processes* that replace circuits with behavioral code, *clocks* that drive clock domains, and *testbenches* that exercise the circuits and verify that they work correctly.  The simulator lifecycle consists of four stages:  1. The simulator is created: ::  sim = Simulator(design)  2. Processes, clocks, and testbenches are added as necessary: ::  sim.add_clock(1e-6) sim.add_clock(1e-7, domain="fast") sim.add_process(process_instr_decoder) sim.add_testbench(testbench_cpu_execute)  3. The simulation is run: ::  with sim.write_vcd("waveform.vcd"): sim.run()  4. (Optional) The simulator is reset: ::  sim.reset()  After the simulator is reset, it may be reused to run the simulation again.  .. note::  Resetting the simulator can also be used to amortize the startup cost of repeatedly simulating a large design.  Arguments --------- toplevel : :class:`~amaranth.hdl.Elaboratable` Simulated design.

function.name: add_clock
function.description: Add a clock to the simulation.  Adds a stimulus that toggles the clock signal of :py:`domain` at a 50% duty cycle.  The driven clock signal will toggle every half-:py:`period` seconds starting at :py:`phase` seconds after the beginning of the simulation; if not specified, :py:`phase` defaults to half-:py:`period` to avoid coinciding the first active edge with the beginning of the simulation.  The clock domain to drive is selected by the :py:`domain` argument, which may be a :class:`~amaranth.hdl.ClockDomain` object or a :class:`str`. If it is a string, the clock domain with that name is retrieved from the :py:`toplevel` elaboratable.
function.ori_input: self, period, *, phase = None, domain = 'sync', if_exists = False
function.ori_description: Add a clock to the simulation.  Adds a stimulus that toggles the clock signal of :py:`domain` at a 50% duty cycle.  The driven clock signal will toggle every half-:py:`period` seconds starting at :py:`phase` seconds after the beginning of the simulation; if not specified, :py:`phase` defaults to half-:py:`period` to avoid coinciding the first active edge with the beginning of the simulation.  The clock domain to drive is selected by the :py:`domain` argument, which may be a :class:`~amaranth.hdl.ClockDomain` object or a :class:`str`. If it is a string, the clock domain with that name is retrieved from the :py:`toplevel` elaboratable.  Raises ------ :exc:`NameError` If :py:`domain` is a :class:`str`, the :py:`toplevel` elaboratable does not have a clock domain with that name, and :py:`if_exists` is :py:`False`. :exc:`~amaranth.hdl.DriverConflict` If :py:`domain` already has a clock driving it. :exc:`RuntimeError` If the simulation has been advanced since its creation or last reset.

function.name: add_testbench
function.description: Add a testbench to the simulation.  Adds a testbench that runs concurrently with the :py:`toplevel` elaboratable and is able to manipulate its inputs, outputs, and state.  The behavior of the testbench is defined by its *constructor function*, which is an :py:`async` function that takes a single argument, the :class:`SimulatorContext`: ::  async def testbench(ctx): ... await ctx.tick() ...  sim.add_testbench(testbench)  This method does not accept coroutines. Rather, the provided :py:`constructor` coroutine function is called immediately when the testbench is added to create a coroutine, as well as by the :meth:`reset` method.  The testbench can be *critical* (the default) or *background* (if the :py:`background=True` argument is specified). The :meth:`run` method will continue advancing the simulation while any critical testbenches or processes are running, and will exit when only background testbenches or processes remain. A background testbench can temporarily become critical using the :meth:`~SimulatorContext.critical` context manager.  At each point in time, all of the non-waiting testbenches are executed in the order in which they were added. If two testbenches share state, or must manipulate the design in a coordinated way, they may rely on this execution order for correctness.

Rather, the provided :py:`constructor` coroutine function is called immediately when the testbench is added to create a coroutine, as well as by the :meth:`reset` method.  The testbench can be *critical* (the default) or *background* (if the :py:`background=True` argument is specified). The :meth:`run` method will continue advancing the simulation while any critical testbenches or processes are running, and will exit when only background testbenches or processes remain. A background testbench can temporarily become critical using the :meth:`~SimulatorContext.critical` context manager.  At each point in time, all of the non-waiting testbenches are executed in the order in which they were added. If two testbenches share state, or must manipulate the design in a coordinated way, they may rely on this execution order for correctness.  Raises ------ :exc:`RuntimeError` If the simulation has been advanced since its creation or last reset.

function.name: run
function.description: Run the simulation indefinitely.  This method advances the simulation while any critical testbenches or processes continue executing. It is equivalent to::  while self.advance(): pass
function.ori_description: Run the simulation indefinitely.  This method advances the simulation while any critical testbenches or processes continue executing. It is equivalent to::  while self.advance(): pass

function.name: write_vcd
function.description: write_vcd(vcd_file, gtkw_file=None, *, traces=())  Capture waveforms to a file.  This context manager captures waveforms for each signal and memory that is referenced from :py:`toplevel`, as well as any additional signals or memories specified in :py:`traces`, and saves them to :py:`vcd_file`. If :py:`gtkw_file` is provided, it is populated with a GTKWave save file displaying :py:`traces` when opened.  Use this context manager to wrap a call to :meth:`run` or :meth:`run_until`: ::  with sim.write_vcd("simulation.vcd"): sim.run()  The :py:`vcd_file` and :py:`gtkw_file` arguments accept either a :term:`python:file object` or a filename. If a file object is provided, it is closed when exiting the context manager (once the simulation completes or encounters an error).  The :py:`traces` argument accepts a *trace specification*, which can be one of:  * A :class:`~amaranth.hdl.ValueLike` object, such as a :class:`~amaranth.hdl.Signal`; * A :class:`~amaranth.hdl.MemoryData` object or an individual row retrieved from one; * A :class:`tuple` or :class:`list` containing trace specifications; * A :class:`dict` associating :class:`str` names to trace specifications; * An :ref:`interface object <wiring>`.

function.description: Reset the simulation.  This method reverts the simulation to its initial state:  * The value of each signal is changed to its initial value; * The contents of each memory is changed to its initial contents; * Each clock, testbench, and process is restarted.

basic_info.name: 层级RAL可取指权限遗漏导致chip级错误预测的回归资格

environment.description:
触发: chip级TL错误回归随机生成CSR取指，rv_dm debug memory窗口内的合法取指被scoreboard预测为错误，多个seed失败；block级修复已存在但未传播至chip层级模型。
对象：chip级RAL及子块层级、各寄存器块allows_csr_fetch配置、随机非法/错误事务序列、scoreboard预测逻辑、DUT debug-enable状态和失败seed日志。
目标：在不放宽真实debug权限约束的情况下，使随机错误事务只对确实不可取指的寄存器产生d_error预测，并证明层级模型配置与DUT状态一致。
输入：issue复现seed和TL日志、chip/block RAL层级、寄存器所属block/祖先列表、allows_csr_fetch/nofetch过滤结果、DUT生命周期debug-enable配置、修复PR提交和VCS回归结果。
步骤/决策：先按失败seed复现并将每个预测事务关联到寄存器、所属block及DUT地址窗口；检查生成器是否从UVM_HIER枚举寄存器而只读取顶层权限；将可取指属性沿祖先块传播并在chip级rv_dm_mem配置，保留scoreboard对实际debug-enable的状态条件；修复后对原失败seed和随机多seed重跑，区分生成器不再发非法事务、预测正确但DUT拒绝、以及权限状态证据不足三类；若chip/block RAL或DUT生命周期配置版本不一致则冻结回归结论，不以少数通过seed放行。
验收：逐事务可回链RAL祖先属性、DUT地址窗口和debug-enable；原失败seed在对应修复提交和配置下复测，真实禁止取指仍受覆盖；超出PR已报告的seed/配置须实际补跑，Darjeeling未测不得标通过。

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: Lock
init_ref_tools.description: A mutual exclusion lock.  Guarantees fair scheduling. Lock acquisition is given in order of attempted lock acquisition.  Usage: By directly calling :meth:`acquire` and :meth:`release`.  .. code-block:: python  lock = Lock() ... await lock.acquire() try: # do some stuff ... finally: lock.release()  Or...  .. code-block:: python  async with Lock(): # do some stuff ...  .. versionchanged:: 1.4  The lock can be used as an asynchronous context manager in an :keyword:`async with` statement

basic_info.name: 复位拓扑变更后的复位源交叉测试与状态捕获签核

environment.description:
触发: POR、软件复位、外设复位或CPU复位的源/级联关系或捕获时序在规格/RTL中发生变更
对象：新旧复位拓扑规格、RTL版本、复位输入/输出矩阵、reset_info与状态捕获CSR、现有测试计划
目标：证明指定复位源、重叠时序和释放路径的输出/状态捕获行为符合新规格，或定位阻断签核的未覆盖分支
输入：复位拓扑表、源优先级/级联规则、稳定周期条件、CSR预期、SVA、测试序列与覆盖报告
步骤/决策：从新旧规格差异列出受影响复位源、目标域和状态捕获条件；生成单源及相邻/重叠复位序列，检查源触发、级联与释放后的已知状态；对reset_info及CPU/alert状态捕获与清除逐项断言；若某源组合未覆盖、输出未知或CSR不符合预期则保留失败波形并阻断签核；复跑受影响序列及复位类型交叉覆盖
验收：每个变更源和目标域有明确预期与证据；释放后输出已知且级联/CSR捕获符合项目规格；未覆盖或失败组合不因总体覆盖率高而放行；项目阈值另给

init_ref_tools.name: Range
init_ref_tools.description: Variant of :class:`range` with inclusive right bound.  In Python, :class:`range` and :class:`slice` have a non-inclusive right bound. In both Verilog and VHDL, ranges and arrays have an inclusive right bound. This type mimics Python's :class:`range` type, but implements HDL-like inclusive right bounds, using the names :attr:`left` and :attr:`right` as replacements for ``start`` and ``stop`` to match VHDL. Range directionality can be specified using ``'to'`` or ``'downto'`` between the left and right bounds. Not specifying directionality will cause the directionality to be inferred.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(-2, 3) >>> r.left, r.right, len(r) (-2, 3, 6)  >>> s = Range(8, "downto", 1) >>> s.left, s.right, len(s) (8, 1, 8)  :meth:`from_range` and :meth:`to_range` can be used to convert from and to :class:`range`.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(-2, 3) >>> r.to_range() range(-2, 4)  :class:`Range` supports "null" ranges as seen in VHDL. "null" ranges occur when a left bound cannot reach a right bound with the given direction. They have a length of ``0``, but the :attr:`left`, :attr:`right`, and :attr:`direction` values remain as given.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(1, "to", 0) # no way to count from 1 'to' 0 >>> r.left, r.direction, r.right (1, 'to', 0) >>> len(r) 0  .. note:: This is only possible when specifying the direction.  Ranges also support all the features of :class:`range` including, but not limited to:  - ``value in range`` to see if a value is in the range, - ``range.index(value)`` to see what position in the range the value is,  The typical use case of this type is in conjunction with :class:`~cocotb.types.Array`.  Args: left: Leftmost bound of range. direction: ``'to'`` if values are ascending, ``'downto'`` if descending. right: Rightmost bound of range (inclusive).

验收：gold/gate/工具/假设及复位序列可复现；所有必须partition已证明而非仅运行完成；任何初态假设收窄有规格依据；失败trace被定位和修复后重证；证明结论限于配置覆盖域

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: Lock
init_ref_tools.description: A mutual exclusion lock.  Guarantees fair scheduling. Lock acquisition is given in order of attempted lock acquisition.  Usage: By directly calling :meth:`acquire` and :meth:`release`.  .. code-block:: python  lock = Lock() ... await lock.acquire() try: # do some stuff ... finally: lock.release()  Or...  .. code-block:: python  async with Lock(): # do some stuff ...  .. versionchanged:: 1.4  The lock can be used as an asynchronous context manager in an :keyword:`async with` statement

environment.description:
触发: 低功耗入口、唤醒源同步或电源/时钟握手逻辑改变，唤醒可能贴近入睡申请到达
对象：新旧低功耗状态机、唤醒使能/捕获规格、clock/power status握手、仿真测试计划
目标：确认入睡-唤醒竞争下状态机不挂起、不跳过握手且输出有合法终态，或阻断低功耗功能签核

init_ref_tools.name: Range
init_ref_tools.description: Variant of :class:`range` with inclusive right bound.  In Python, :class:`range` and :class:`slice` have a non-inclusive right bound. In both Verilog and VHDL, ranges and arrays have an inclusive right bound. This type mimics Python's :class:`range` type, but implements HDL-like inclusive right bounds, using the names :attr:`left` and :attr:`right` as replacements for ``start`` and ``stop`` to match VHDL. Range directionality can be specified using ``'to'`` or ``'downto'`` between the left and right bounds. Not specifying directionality will cause the directionality to be inferred.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(-2, 3) >>> r.left, r.right, len(r) (-2, 3, 6)  >>> s = Range(8, "downto", 1) >>> s.left, s.right, len(s) (8, 1, 8)  :meth:`from_range` and :meth:`to_range` can be used to convert from and to :class:`range`.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(-2, 3) >>> r.to_range() range(-2, 4)  :class:`Range` supports "null" ranges as seen in VHDL. "null" ranges occur when a left bound cannot reach a right bound with the given direction. They have a length of ``0``, but the :attr:`left`, :attr:`right`, and :attr:`direction` values remain as given.  .. code-block:: pycon3  >>> r = Range(1, "to", 0) # no way to count from 1 'to' 0 >>> r.left, r.direction, r.right (1, 'to', 0) >>> len(r) 0  .. note:: This is only possible when specifying the direction.  Ranges also support all the features of :class:`range` including, but not limited to:  - ``value in range`` to see if a value is in the range, - ``range.index(value)`` to see what position in the range the value is,  The typical use case of this type is in conjunction with :class:`~cocotb.types.Array`.  Args: left: Leftmost bound of range. direction: ``'to'`` if values are ascending, ``'downto'`` if descending. right: Rightmost bound of range (inclusive).

environment.description:
触发: 异步FIFO的读写时钟、任一侧复位、深度参数或指针实现发生变更，准备重新交付跨时钟接口
对象：旧/新FIFO RTL、读写时钟与复位波形、深度/宽度参数、valid-ready协议、CDC约束和参考模型
目标：证明复位域独立变化和参数变更不会产生伪满/伪空、丢数/重复读或未初始化输出，或阻断集成
输入：独立rst_wr/rst_rd、异步时钟比例/相位、突发读写、参数约束、Gray指针与同步器波形、FIFO深度/数据参考模型
步骤/决策：先核对深度满足实现约束且读写复位均能将本侧指针与同步状态置零；在各时钟比例下施加写满/读空、单侧复位、复位交错和边界突发；检查valid/ready、空满/深度与参考模型，观察Gray指针跨域是否单调且无非法多位变化；若一侧复位后另一侧仍可见旧数据或输出未知/重复，则保存波形和断言并阻断参数或CDC交付
验收：深度/参数约束检查通过；独立复位和复位交错下空满/深度与参考模型一致；无丢失、重复或未知输出；CDC/断言结果和工具版本可追溯；项目边界以规格为准

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

environment.description:
触发: USB协议处理、FIFO reset控制或设备重新配置逻辑变更，需确认总线复位后能恢复通信且局部FIFO复位不污染协议状态
对象：USBDEV协议状态机、bus reset检测、软件FIFO reset控制、Available OUT/SETUP/Rx FIFO、配置寄存器和主机重配置序列
目标：明确外部bus reset与局部FIFO reset的状态边界，证明恢复路径不会丢弃保留数据或误分配FIFO槽位，或阻断版本交付
输入：bus reset/disconnect波形、主机重新枚举/配置、各FIFO占用、局部reset选择、协议CSR和scoreboard状态
步骤/决策：分别运行bus reset后重配置、软件选择FIFO reset、局部reset与数据流重叠序列；按规格检查地址/配置和协议状态、各FIFO等级、SETUP专用槽位及scoreboard期望；若bus reset恢复失败、局部reset影响未选FIFO或OUT数据占用SETUP保留槽位则保存事务/波形并阻断；仅在协议重新配置、FIFO等级和响应一致后提交
验收：外部bus reset后重新配置和通信恢复符合项目协议；局部FIFO reset仅影响批准对象且FIFO等级/SETUP槽位规则满足；scoreboard无未解释事务差异；缺证据不得以单次恢复通过放行

触发: 覆盖数据库显示目标bin已命中，但贡献该命中的一个或多个UVM/cocotb回归作业存在scoreboard mismatch、断言失败或测试异常终止
对象：版本化RTL与测试平台、每作业coverage.dat/UCIS结果、xUnit或等效测试结果、seed/配置/测试名及目标覆盖点

步骤/决策：先用job ID连接覆盖文件和测试结果；把失败/中止作业的命中留作诊断证据但从正式闭合汇总中隔离；定位scoreboard预期/实际分歧或断言失败类别，不以覆盖命中替代功能正确；修复DUT、检查器或刺激后用相同目标条件重跑；仅当通过的作业再次命中目标bin且版本/配置一致时更新闭合状态，若修复导致bin不再命中则重新开缺口
验收：每个计入签核的bin命中可回链同RTL/coverage模型/配置版本、job ID和通过结果；失败命中与之后的无命中通过不得拼成通过证据；原失败作业保留。

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

scenario_design.scenario_description_raw:
触发: 覆盖数据库显示目标bin已命中，但贡献该命中的一个或多个UVM/cocotb回归作业存在scoreboard mismatch、断言失败或测试异常终止
对象：版本化RTL与测试平台、每作业coverage.dat/UCIS结果、xUnit或等效测试结果、seed/配置/测试名及目标覆盖点
目标：决定哪些覆盖命中可用于验证闭合，并在修复失效后取得通过性与覆盖同时成立的证据
输入：每作业唯一ID、RTL/coverage model/scoreboard版本、仿真器配置、原始覆盖文件、测试通过/失败状态、失败签名、重跑记录
步骤/决策：先用job ID连接覆盖文件和测试结果；把失败/中止作业的命中留作诊断证据但从正式闭合汇总中隔离；定位scoreboard预期/实际分歧或断言失败类别，不以覆盖命中替代功能正确；修复DUT、检查器或刺激后用相同目标条件重跑；仅当通过的作业再次命中目标bin且版本/配置一致时更新闭合状态，若修复导致bin不再命中则重新开缺口

environment.description:
触发: 多个RTL参数、协议模式或IP实例配置的回归完成，准备合并覆盖数据库并签发验证闭合报告
对象：各配置的RTL和UVM环境版本、coverage model与coverage_enable设置、测试名单和每作业覆盖文件
目标：按验证计划区分共享目标与配置专有目标，避免跨版本/跨模式合并掩盖未测功能
输入：配置清单、设计参数/feature flags、coverage model hash、仿真器版本、每作业覆盖点元数据、测试通过性和验证目标矩阵
步骤/决策：先按RTL、覆盖模型、协议模式和agent配置建立兼容分组；对于只在某配置有效的bin设置该配置自己的分母，并保留禁用覆盖的显式原因；仅对结构与语义一致的分组调用覆盖合并；逐配置核对功能目标与代码覆盖的异常背离，若功能覆盖满而代码覆盖极低则复审覆盖模型缺项；不同版本同名bin不可凭名称合并，需映射与重新验证；输出逐配置签核而非单一总百分比
验收：每个覆盖目标绑定适用配置和模型版本；同名bin跨配置/版本不凭名称合并；禁用原因可审计；逐配置缺口不被其他配置命中掩盖。

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: uvm_root
init_ref_tools.description: F.7. We do not use ``uvm_pkg`` to hold ``uvm_root``. Instead it is a class variable of uvm_component. This avoids circular reference issues regarding uvm_pkg.  Plus, it's cleaner.  ``uvm_root`` is still a singleton that you access through its constructor instead of through a ``get()`` method.  Much of the functionality in Annex F delivers functionality in SystemVerilog that is already built into Python. So we're going to skip much of that Annex.

init_ref_tools.name: uvm_driver
init_ref_tools.description: The base class for drivers that initiate requests for new transactions via a :class:`~uvm_seq_item_pull_port`. The ports are typically connected to the exports of an appropriate sequencer component.  This driver operates in pull mode. Its ports are typically connected to the corresponding exports in a pull sequencer as follows:  .. code-block:: python  driver.seq_item_port.connect(sequencer.seq_item_export) driver.rsp_port.connect(sequencer.rsp_export)  The ``rsp_port`` needs connecting only if the driver will use it to write responses to the analysis export in the sequencer.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: with_timeout
init_ref_tools.description: Wait on any awaitable, throw an exception if it waits longer than the given time.  When a :term:`python:coroutine` is passed, the callee coroutine is started, the caller blocks until the callee completes, and the callee's result is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the callee is killed and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  When a :term:`task` is passed, the caller blocks until the callee completes and the callee's result is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the callee `continues to run` and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  If a :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Trigger` or :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Waitable` is passed, the caller blocks until the trigger fires, and the trigger is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the trigger is cancelled and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  Usage: .. code-block:: python  await with_timeout(coro, 100, "ns") await with_timeout(First(coro, event.wait()), 100, "ns")

trigger.description: A single object that could be right of an :keyword:`await` expression in cocotb.

timeout_time.description: Simulation time duration before timeout occurs.

timeout_unit.description: Unit of timeout_time, accepts any unit that :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Timer` does.

round_mode.description: String specifying how to handle time values that sit between time steps (one of ``'error'``, ``'round'``, ``'ceil'``, ``'floor'``, ``None``). A ``None`` argument is converted to the current value of :attr:`.Timer.round_mode`.

return.description: First trigger that completed if timeout did not occur.

init_ref_tools.name: uvm_sequencer
init_ref_tools.description: The uvm_sequencer arbitrates between multiple sequences that want to send items to driver (connected to seq_export) It exposes put_req, get_next_item, get_response from the export. The sequence will use these to coordinate items with the sequencer.

init_ref_tools.name: uvm_driver
init_ref_tools.description: The base class for drivers that initiate requests for new transactions via a :class:`~uvm_seq_item_pull_port`. The ports are typically connected to the exports of an appropriate sequencer component.  This driver operates in pull mode. Its ports are typically connected to the corresponding exports in a pull sequencer as follows:  .. code-block:: python  driver.seq_item_port.connect(sequencer.seq_item_export) driver.rsp_port.connect(sequencer.rsp_export)  The ``rsp_port`` needs connecting only if the driver will use it to write responses to the analysis export in the sequencer.

basic_info.name: APB外设地址图变更后的访问路由与空洞隔离

environment.description:
触发: APB外设新增、基址/窗口重排或AXI到APB桥地址解码规则变更
对象：旧新地址图、桥路由规则、外设实例/寄存器清单及软件可见基址
目标：确认有效AXI访问只落在目标APB外设，未映射地址无APB选择且返回项目约定的错误状态
输入：AXI/APB地址宽度、解码窗口、从设备索引、寄存器偏移、受控读写探针序列、各PSEL与响应轨迹
步骤/决策：先记录桥变体、NoRules/地址规则与从设备数；仅在启用地址解码时生成边界及空洞探针并核对无PSEL和对应响应；NoRules==0时按单从设备全地址转发检查，不宣称存在解码空洞；其余重叠、别名和实际PSEL由目标RTL仿真验证。
验收：有解码规则时未映射地址无PSEL，并按桥变体核SLVERR或DECERR；NoRules==0单从设备模式时所有地址转发，应以该配置的允许范围和软件地址图另行验收；无目标波形不得宣称通过。

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: APB外设新增、基址/窗口重排或AXI到APB桥地址解码规则变更
对象：旧新地址图、桥路由规则、外设实例/寄存器清单及软件可见基址
目标：确认有效AXI访问只落在目标APB外设，未映射地址无APB选择且返回项目约定的错误状态
输入：AXI/APB地址宽度、解码窗口、从设备索引、寄存器偏移、受控读写探针序列、各PSEL与响应轨迹
步骤/决策：先记录桥变体、NoRules/地址规则与从设备数；仅在启用地址解码时生成边界及空洞探针并核对无PSEL和对应响应；NoRules==0时按单从设备全地址转发检查，不宣称存在解码空洞；其余重叠、别名和实际PSEL由目标RTL仿真验证。
验收：有解码规则时未映射地址无PSEL，并按桥变体核SLVERR或DECERR；NoRules==0单从设备模式时所有地址转发，应以该配置的允许范围和软件地址图另行验收；无目标波形不得宣称通过。

可合成任务：输入：AXI/APB地址宽度、解码窗口、从设备索引、寄存器偏移、受控读写探针序列、各PSEL与响应轨迹
Python核心操作/决策：Python解析受控地址图和固定总线轨迹，生成边界探针与预期外设矩阵；实际AXI/APB交易由外部RTL仿真器或硬件测试环境执行
输出：地址窗口与PSEL实测矩阵、空洞隔离结果、别名/重叠清单和映射发布hold/pass建议
