basic_info.name: 宽AXI访问拆分后APB读敏感寄存器的副作用隔离

environment.description:
触发: 宽AXI4主机接入窄APB4外设后，驱动准备读取窄状态寄存器或RX数据寄存器
对象：桥数据宽度比、目标与邻接APB寄存器副作用定义、驱动读取宽度及PSEL/PADDR轨迹
目标：避免一次上游窄读被桥扩展为对相邻读敏感寄存器的额外APB读，造成FIFO数据消耗或状态变化
输入：AXI beat大小与地址、APB bank数/宽度、寄存器布局、读副作用说明、仿真APB访问序列和外设状态前后快照
步骤/决策：列出每个AXI读beat实际会触及的APB bank；将其与寄存器副作用表相交；如邻接bank含读敏感寄存器，则改用访问粒度/地址布局/桥类型的受控设计方案并复测；在仿真中核对只有预期寄存器被读且FIFO/状态前后变化符合规格；无外设副作用规范或尚未复测时hold驱动集成
验收：记录上游读宽、下游全部PADDR/PSEL和真实APB寄存器副作用；无实际目标APB端点或未复测时只报潜在风险，不写已发生丢FIFO数据。

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

environment.description:
触发: 主机适配器版本变更或总线故障注入计划要求证明异常设备响应不会成为有效读数据
对象：有请求跟踪表的TL-UL主机、设备响应通道和告警/中断路径
目标：隔离孤儿及opcode错配响应，并以独立告警记录故障
输入：已接受请求ID/opcode集合、注入的d_source/d_opcode/d_error、host数据提交与alert/interrupt波形
步骤/决策：先建立合法Get/Put请求及未完成ID账本；分别注入无对应请求的响应和Get返回AccessAck或Put返回AccessAckData；观察host是否丢弃异常响应且不更新读数据/完成计数，同时产生规定告警；随后注入合法响应确认接口恢复；若异常响应被接受、仅超时未告警或后续事务错配则阻断；不在TL-UL fabric中伪造超时应答
验收：孤儿/错opcode响应不得进入有效数据或完成路径且产生项目定义告警；合法响应随后完成；协议无网络timeout伪响应，测试超时只用于失败检测

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: with_timeout
init_ref_tools.description: Wait on any awaitable, throw an exception if it waits longer than the given time.  When a :term:`python:coroutine` is passed, the callee coroutine is started, the caller blocks until the callee completes, and the callee's result is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the callee is killed and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  When a :term:`task` is passed, the caller blocks until the callee completes and the callee's result is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the callee `continues to run` and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  If a :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Trigger` or :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Waitable` is passed, the caller blocks until the trigger fires, and the trigger is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the trigger is cancelled and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised.  Usage: .. code-block:: python  await with_timeout(coro, 100, "ns") await with_timeout(First(coro, event.wait()), 100, "ns")

trigger.description: A single object that could be right of an :keyword:`await` expression in cocotb.

timeout_time.description: Simulation time duration before timeout occurs.

timeout_unit.description: Unit of timeout_time, accepts any unit that :class:`~cocotb.triggers.Timer` does.

round_mode.description: String specifying how to handle time values that sit between time steps (one of ``'error'``, ``'round'``, ``'ceil'``, ``'floor'``, ``None``). A ``None`` argument is converted to the current value of :attr:`.Timer.round_mode`.

return.description: First trigger that completed if timeout did not occur.

init_ref_tools.ori_input: trigger: Awaitable[T], timeout_time: float | Decimal, timeout_unit: TimeUnit = 'step', round_mode: RoundMode | None = None

When a :term:`python:coroutine` is passed, the callee coroutine is started, the caller blocks until the callee completes, and the callee's result is returned to the caller. If timeout occurs, the callee is killed and :exc:`SimTimeoutError` is raised. A ``None`` argument is converted to the current value of :attr:`.Timer.round_mode`.  Returns: First trigger that completed if timeout did not occur. scenario_design.application_scenario: TL-UL孤儿响应与读写ACK类型错配的主机拒收告警回归
scenario_design.scenario_description_raw:
触发: 主机适配器版本变更或总线故障注入计划要求证明异常设备响应不会成为有效读数据
对象：有请求跟踪表的TL-UL主机、设备响应通道和告警/中断路径
目标：隔离孤儿及opcode错配响应，并以独立告警记录故障
输入：已接受请求ID/opcode集合、注入的d_source/d_opcode/d_error、host数据提交与alert/interrupt波形
步骤/决策：先建立合法Get/Put请求及未完成ID账本；分别注入无对应请求的响应和Get返回AccessAck或Put返回AccessAckData；观察host是否丢弃异常响应且不更新读数据/完成计数，同时产生规定告警；随后注入合法响应确认接口恢复；若异常响应被接受、仅超时未告警或后续事务错配则阻断；不在TL-UL fabric中伪造超时应答
验收：孤儿/错opcode响应不得进入有效数据或完成路径且产生项目定义告警；合法响应随后完成；协议无网络timeout伪响应，测试超时只用于失败检测
scenario_design.package_or_combination_raw: TL-UL host adapter RTL、cocotb/HDL仿真器
scenario_design.composable_task_raw:
输入：已接受请求ID/opcode集合、注入的d_source/d_opcode/d_error、host数据提交与alert/interrupt波形
Python核心操作/决策：cocotb/Python可构造异常response、维护请求账本并解析alert波形；主机RTL需HDL仿真器或硬件
输出：异常响应分类、拒收/告警波形、合法后续完成状态
可复核验收：孤儿/错opcode响应不得进入有效数据或完成路径且产生项目定义告警；合法响应随后完成；协议无网络timeout伪响应，测试超时只用于失败检测

basic_info.name: SRAM存储位完整性翻转后的处理器侧检测责任验收

environment.description:
触发: SRAM内存ECC/完整性保护或处理器读路径变更，需要确认位翻转在端到端路径被检测而非误认为SRAM访问错误
对象：已写入合法数据/完整性的SRAM阵列、TL-UL读通道、处理器完整性检查器
目标：证明存储错误作为坏数据/完整性对穿过SRAM接口并在处理器侧触发预期安全处理
输入：被写入地址/数据/ECC、故障翻转位置、backdoor注入记录、TL d_data/data_intg/d_error、处理器完整性告警
步骤/决策：先读正常地址建立正确完整性基线；对已写入位置backdoor翻转数据或ECC，再从前门读；核查SRAM返回的内容/完整性保留故障且d_error按该内存合同不置位；跟踪处理器端检查和安全反应；若SRAM静默修正/重生完整性或处理器未报错则阻断；CSR总线完整性错误另按fatal_intg_error路径，不混同存储passthrough
验收：已写地址可追溯；翻转后坏完整性传播到处理器且产生项目规定响应，SRAM侧不以d_error掩盖存储错误；仅模拟波形证明被测RTL版本

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: Bus
init_ref_tools.description: Wraps up a collection of signals.  Assumes we have a set of signals/nets named ``entity.<bus_name><bus_separator><signal>``.  For example a bus ``stream_in`` with signals ``valid`` and ``data`` is assumed to be named ``dut.stream_in_valid`` and ``dut.stream_in_data`` (with the default separator '_').  TODO: Support for ``struct``/``record`` ports where signals are member names.

function.name: __init__

entity.description: :class:`SimHandle` instance to the entity containing the bus.

name.description: Name of the bus. ``None`` for a nameless bus, e.g. bus-signals in an interface or a ``modport`` (untested on ``struct``/``record``, but could work here as well).

signals.description: In the case of an object (passed to :func:`drive`/:func:`capture`) that has the same attribute names as the signal names of the bus, the *signals* argument can be a list of those names. When the object has different attribute names, the *signals* argument should be a dict that maps bus attribute names to object signal names.

optional_signals.description: Signals that don't have to be present on the interface. See the *signals* argument above for details.

bus_separator.description: Character(s) to use as separator between bus name and signal name. Defaults to '_'.

case_insensitive.description: Perform case-insensitive match on signal names. Defaults to True.

array_idx.description: Optional index when signal is an array.

function.ori_input: self, entity, name, signals, optional_signals = [], bus_separator = '_', case_insensitive = True, array_idx = None
function.ori_description: Args: entity (SimHandle): :class:`SimHandle` instance to the entity containing the bus. name (str): Name of the bus. ``None`` for a nameless bus, e.g. bus-signals in an interface or a ``modport`` (untested on ``struct``/``record``, but could work here as well). signals (list or dict): In the case of an object (passed to :func:`drive`/:func:`capture`) that has the same attribute names as the signal names of the bus, the *signals* argument can be a list of those names. When the object has different attribute names, the *signals* argument should be a dict that maps bus attribute names to object signal names. optional_signals (list or dict, optional): Signals that don't have to be present on the interface. See the *signals* argument above for details. bus_separator (str, optional): Character(s) to use as separator between bus name and signal name. Defaults to '_'. case_insensitive (bool, optional): Perform case-insensitive match on signal names. Defaults to True. array_idx (int or None, optional): Optional index when signal is an array.

function.description: Drives values onto the bus.

init_ref_tasks:
场景要求：触发: SRAM内存ECC/完整性保护或处理器读路径变更，需要确认位翻转在端到端路径被检测而非误认为SRAM访问错误
对象：已写入合法数据/完整性的SRAM阵列、TL-UL读通道、处理器完整性检查器
目标：证明存储错误作为坏数据/完整性对穿过SRAM接口并在处理器侧触发预期安全处理
输入：被写入地址/数据/ECC、故障翻转位置、backdoor注入记录、TL d_data/data_intg/d_error、处理器完整性告警
步骤/决策：先读正常地址建立正确完整性基线；对已写入位置backdoor翻转数据或ECC，再从前门读；核查SRAM返回的内容/完整性保留故障且d_error按该内存合同不置位；跟踪处理器端检查和安全反应；若SRAM静默修正/重生完整性或处理器未报错则阻断；CSR总线完整性错误另按fatal_intg_error路径，不混同存储passthrough
验收：已写地址可追溯；翻转后坏完整性传播到处理器且产生项目规定响应，SRAM侧不以d_error掩盖存储错误；仅模拟波形证明被测RTL版本

可合成任务：输入：被写入地址/数据/ECC、故障翻转位置、backdoor注入记录、TL d_data/data_intg/d_error、处理器完整性告警
Python核心操作/决策：Python可生成故障注入计划、关联TL波形和处理器告警；存储ECC/DUT/处理器检查由HDL仿真或硬件执行
输出：正常/翻转读数、d_error和处理器告警对照、责任归属及放行/阻断
可复核验收：已写地址可追溯；翻转后坏完整性传播到处理器且产生项目规定响应，SRAM侧不以d_error掩盖存储错误；仅模拟波形证明被测RTL版本

basic_info.name: SPI设备存储器局部写后全字完整性重算与未选字节保持

environment.description:
触发: SPI设备memory byte-enable写路径或integrity生成逻辑更新后，局部写后全字读取出现完整性异常
对象：已初始化的带数据完整性位的SPI设备存储器、字节选通信号和TL-UL访问端
目标：证明局部写只更新选中字节且以新整字数据计算并保存完整性
输入：原整字/原ECC、写地址、byte enable/新数据、写后整字/存储ECC、TL读返回与告警
步骤/决策：对每种合法字节使能和不同原字节模式执行局部写；独立拼接预期整字并计算完整性参考值；读取整字检查未选字节保持、选中字节更新及存储ECC匹配；若仅对写入字节算ECC或保留旧ECC导致后续告警，则定位内存更新拍并阻断；再注入控制/数据/ECC错误确认fatal alert路径能区分真实故障
验收：未选字节不变且写后ECC匹配新整字；后续无故障读不产生完整性告警，注入故障则按规范告警；ECC参考与DUT不能共用同一错误实现

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: Bus

For example a bus ``stream_in`` with signals ``valid`` and ``data`` is assumed to be named ``dut.stream_in_valid`` and ``dut.stream_in_data`` (with the default separator '_'). basic_info.name: ROM摘要核验未完成期间TL访问阻断与启动状态对账

environment.description:
触发: ROM镜像或KMAC摘要路径修改，启动期间CPU/总线可能在核验结束前读取ROM
对象：含预期摘要的ROM镜像、ROM_CTRL/KMAC接口、pwrmgr good/done状态与TL读端
目标：确保未验证ROM内容不会在done前经TL暴露，成功与失败状态和摘要相符
输入：匹配与不匹配两类ROM镜像、KMAC请求/响应、pwrmgr good/done、TL访问时序与响应
步骤/决策：以不匹配及匹配摘要镜像分别执行启动检查；在KMAC核验开始/中间/完成边界发TL读；监视KMAC输入、摘要比较和pwrmgr状态；若done前TL访问被接受或错误镜像使good置位，阻断；正确镜像完成后检查允许读取且数据与模型一致；失败镜像的后续状态按目标安全合同复核，不自行假设自动恢复
验收：两类摘要结果与good一致；done前所有TL访问按合同阻断，done后仅正确镜像正常读取；版本和镜像哈希可追溯

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

environment.description:

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. This will be a point where all the signal values are stable as there are no more RTL events scheduled for the timestep. The simulator will not allow scheduling of more events in this timestep. Useful for monitors which need to wait for all processes to execute (both RTL and cocotb) to ensure sampled signal values are final.

init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

basic_info.name: 访问控制拒绝响应与未完成SRAM响应同拍碰撞的仲裁验收

environment.description:
触发: SRAM存在未完成读请求时，新的TL-UL访问被ACL拒绝并由loopback产生响应
对象：SRAM响应路径、ACL拒绝loopback、响应仲裁/FIFO和主机请求日志
目标：证明并发正常与拒绝响应都被完整返回，且主机不会因少一响应而挂起
输入：未完成读ID、ACL拒绝请求ID、SRAM响应时序、RAZWI回环响应、d_valid/d_ready波形
步骤/决策：先维持若干未完成SRAM读，再安排ACL违规请求使RAZWI与SRAM响应同拍产生；逐源记录两个应答是否入队、被仲裁并最终返回原ID；如任一响应丢失/重复或主机等待超项目时限，则阻断回环逻辑并检查队列深度及仲裁；修复后扫响应背压和多笔并发，要求请求响应计数守恒

init_ref_tools.name: ReadOnly
init_ref_tools.description: Fires when the current simulation timestep moves to the read-only phase.  The read-only phase is entered when the current timestep no longer has any further delta steps. init_ref_tools.name: Clock
init_ref_tools.description: Simple 50:50 duty cycle clock driver.  .. code-block:: python  c = Clock(dut.clk, 10, "ns") c.start()  Args: signal: The clock pin/signal to be driven. period: The clock period. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator.  unit: One of ``'step'``, ``'fs'``, ``'ps'``, ``'ns'``, ``'us'``, ``'ms'``, ``'sec'``. When *unit* is ``'step'``, the timestep is determined by the simulator (see :make:var:`COCOTB_HDL_TIMEPRECISION`).  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 Renamed from ``units``.  impl: One of ``'auto'``, ``'gpi'``, ``'py'``. Specify whether the clock is implemented with a :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` (faster), or with a Python coroutine. When ``'auto'`` is used (default), the fastest implementation that supports your environment and use case is picked.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  set_action: One of :class:`.Immediate`, :class:`.Deposit`, or :class:`.Force`. Specify the action to use when setting the clock signal value. Defaults to the value of :attr:`default_set_action`.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  period_high: The period of time when the clock is driven to ``1``. Defaults to half of the *period*. Must be a multiple of the time precision of the simulator and less than *period*.  .. versionadded:: 2.0  When *impl* is ``'auto'``, if :envvar:`COCOTB_TRUST_INERTIAL_WRITES` is defined, the :class:`~cocotb.simulator.cpp_clock` implementation will be used. Otherwise, the Python coroutine implementation will be used. See the environment variable's documentation for more information on the consequences of using the simulator's inertial write mechanism.  If you need more features like a phase shift and an asymmetric duty cycle, it is simple to create your own clock generator (that you then :func:`cocotb.start_soon`):  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): # pre-construct triggers for performance high_time = Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") low_time = Timer(low_delay, unit="ns") await Timer(initial_delay, unit="ns") while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await high_time dut.clk.value = 0 await low_time  If you also want to change the timing during simulation, use this slightly more inefficient example instead where the :class:`Timer`\ s inside the while loop are created with current delay values:  .. code-block:: python  async def custom_clock(): while True: dut.clk.value = 1 await Timer(high_delay, unit="ns") dut.clk.value = 0 await Timer(low_delay, unit="ns")  high_delay = low_delay = 100 cocotb.start_soon(custom_clock()) await Timer(1000, unit="ns") high_delay = low_delay = 10 # change the clock speed await Timer(1000, unit="ns")  .. versionadded:: 1.5 Support ``'step'`` as the *unit* argument to mean "simulator time step".  .. versionremoved:: 2.0 Passing ``None`` as the *unit* argument was removed, use ``'step'`` instead.  .. versionchanged:: 2.0 :meth:`start` now automatically calls :func:`cocotb.start_soon` and stores the Task on the Clock object, so that it may later be :meth:`stop`\ ped.

验收：每个d_valid响应出口的data_intg与实际d_data匹配；非0/全1反例、直通与缓冲配置均通过host检查；开放issue未经修复和运行不能写已通过

environment.description:
触发: 回归中参考轨迹与待测设计轨迹不一致
对象：已有同一测试配置下的两份 VCD 和信号映射；时间刻度及采样约定需核对
目标：输出首个可比时间点的分歧信号与需补证的信号清单
输入：固定 VCD、信号映射、测试配置、参考轨迹来源
步骤/决策：核对 timescale/层级与同名信号；按时间顺序比较值变化；若信号缺失或时标不兼容则请求补导出或暂缓定位；否则交付首分歧窗口和上下文；不以首分歧直接断定 RTL 根因
验收：重算可得到相同首分歧；两个波形的信号映射和时间单位均可追溯；缺失信号不误报为设计故障

function.name: __init__
function.description: Parse a VCD file, and store information about it in this object.  The bulk of the parsed data can be obtained with :func:`parse_data`.  :ivar data: Parsed VCD data presented in an per-signal indexed list of deltas. Maps short (often signle character) signal names present in the VCD, to Signal objects. :vartype data: Dict[str,Signal]  :ivar deltas: Parsed VCD data presented in exactly the same format as the input, with all signals mixed up, but sorted in time. :vartype deltas: Dict[str,Any]  :ivar endtime: Last timestamp present in the last parsed VCD.  This can be extracted from the data, but we also cache while parsing. :vartype endtime: int  :ivar references_to_ids: map of long-form human readable signal names to the short style VCD dump values :vartype references_to_ids: Dict[str,str]  :ivar signals: The set of unique signal names from the parsed VCD, in the order they are defined in the file.  This can be extracted from the data, but we also cache while parsing. :vartype signals: List[str]  :ivar timescale: A dictionary of key/value pairs describing the timescale.  List of keys:  - "timescale": timescale in seconds (SI unit) - "magnitude": timescale magnitude as specified in the VCD file - "unit" : timescale unit as specified in the VCD file (string) - "factor" : numerical factor derived from the unit  :vartype timescale: Dict

vcd_path.description: path to the VCD file to parse

only_sigs.description: only parse the signal names under $scope and exit. The return value will only contain the signals section. This speeds up parsing if you only want the list of signals.

signals.description: only consider signals in this list. If empty, all signals are considered. Printing commands however will only print every wire once with the first reference name found. Any printing done uses this signal order. If repeated signals are given, they are printed twice.

signal_res.description: same as signals, but uses regular expressions

store_scopes.description: if False, don't store scopes that groups signals and possibly other scopes.

callbacks.description: callbacks that get called as the VCD file is parsed

vcd_string.description: use this string as the VCD content instead of vcd_path. vcd_path is ignored.

to_time.description: Only load value changes until and including this timestamp

init_ref_tools.name: Token
init_ref_tools.description: VCD token yielded from :func:`tokenize()`.  These are relatively high-level tokens insofar as each token fully captures an entire VCD declaration, command, or change descriptor.  The :attr:`kind` attribute determines the :attr:`data` type. Various kind-specific properties provide runtime type-checked access to the kind-specific data.  .. Note::  The :attr:`data` attribute may be accessed directly to avoid runtime type checks and thus achieve better runtime performance versus accessing kind-specific properties such as :attr:`scalar_change`.

init_ref_tools.description: Timescale magnitude and unit.  IEEE 1800-2023 allows only the magnitudes 1, 10, and 100, but nonstandard magnitudes appear in the wild and are accepted by both the reader and the writer. Beware that some tools mishandle nonstandard magnitudes; notably, VCD to FST conversion silently treats them as 1.

basic_info.name: JTAG请求响应跨时钟后接收域数据稳定性与时序资格

environment.description:
触发: rv_dm或lc_ctrl跨时钟FIFO重构后，CDC waiver或接收域长路径在时序分析中无法解释
对象：JTAG请求/响应aggregate、prim_fifo_async_simple两侧时钟/复位和既有valid握手
目标：确认接收域看到稳定且满足时序的数据，并使跨域证明可复核
输入：发送/接收域寄存器拓扑、valid/data波形、CDC报告、SDC例外、STA端点及RTL版本
步骤/决策：核对aggregate数据是否只在发送域寄存而接收域由跨域valid穿过多层逻辑许可；在请求和响应两个方向查看CDC及STA端点；若数据路径依赖未约束长组合链，则要求接收域寄存或等效受证设计；修订后做双时钟相位扫和STA/CDC复验，并检查请求/响应载荷与ID无变化
验收：接收域数据/valid关系有结构与仿真证据，相关路径完成CDC/STA签核且载荷逐笔不变；仅事务计数一致不足以放行

basic_info.name: 接壤供电IO单元被电源网分析误判断连时的签核阻断与复测

environment.description:
触发: IO环中部分pad的供电引脚经相邻单元接壤连接，但analyze_power_grid报PSM-0042无法连接宏/pad实例
对象：已有IO库LEF、PDN配置、含pad的DEF及失败日志；供电端口与接壤的实际几何需核对
目标：判清真实供电断路与分析器节点归属错误，阻断未证实的供电签核并交付复测结果
输入：同版LEF/DEF、PDN层和strap配置、PSM-0042实例列表、check_power_grid及analyze_power_grid报告、修复版OpenROAD版本和回归用例
步骤/决策：锁定报错pad与其VDD/VSS端口；从LEF/DEF核查供电端口形状、OBS、via和与邻接IO单元的接壤路径；按原issue区分PDN无法落strap和PSM未把接壤端口归属至电网节点；若真实几何不可连接则修库/PDN，否则使用包含接壤归属修复的分析器版本复跑；只有连接检查与电源网分析均通过且版本、版图证据可追溯时才交付
验收：每个报错pad的供电路径有可追溯几何证据；修复版检查在相同输入下无PSM-0042，相关供电网连接检查通过；不能仅凭PR合并宣称项目芯片已签核

init_ref_tools.name: Project
init_ref_tools.description: The Project class is the core object in SiliconCompiler, representing a complete hardware design project. It manages design parameters, libraries, flowgraphs, metrics, and provides methods for compilation, data collection, and reporting.

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.

design.description: The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.ori_description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.  Args: design (Union[Design, str], optional): The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.

return.description: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.

function.ori_description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.  Returns: Project: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.  Examples: >>> project.run() # Executes the flow, and returns a project object for the completed job.

job.description: Name of the historical job to retrieve.

return.description: The `Project` object representing the specified historical job.

function.ori_description: Returns a *mutable* reference to a historical job record as a Project object.  Args: job (str): Name of the historical job to retrieve.  Returns: Project: The `Project` object representing the specified historical job.  Raises: KeyError: If the specified job does not exist in the history.

function.name: set_flow
function.description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

flow.description: The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.

This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. Args: flow (Union[Flowgraph, str]): The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.  Raises: TypeError: If the provided `flow` is not a string or a `Flowgraph` object. function.name: get_flow

An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

name.description: The full or partial (prefix) name of the flowgraph to retrieve. If None, the currently selected flowgraph (:keypath:`option,flow`) is used.

return.description: The `Flowgraph` object corresponding to the resolved name.

environment.description:
触发: IHP SG13G2示例在DEF转GDS合并时报spi_DEF_FILL无匹配GDS/OAS cell，或开启GDS_ALLOW_EMPTY后错误被掩盖但填充消失
对象：已有含DEF fill的6_final.def、KLayout版本、def2stream脚本、工艺GDS与6_1_merge日志；最终GDS尚不可视作完整
目标：证明DEF生成的fill未在stream-out过程中清空或静默遗漏，决定是否阻断GDS交付
输入：源DEF的fill记录、KLayout及ORFS版本、def2stream.py版本、合并日志、输出GDS的fill层/单元几何与工艺填充要求
步骤/决策：锁定源DEF与KLayout/脚本版本；核查是否出现*_DEF_FILL无匹配单元及GDS_ALLOW_EMPTY配置；确认def2stream清理单元逻辑是否保留DEF fill；用修复版脚本重新生成GDS；将源DEF填充与输出GDS对应几何核对，并运行项目规定的密度/DRC检查；缺失或仅被允许空单元掩盖则阻断交付
验收：来源DEF中的应保留fill在输出GDS可定位且数量/层位与工艺规则相符，合并日志不含未处理的*_DEF_FILL空单元，密度/DRC按项目工具真实通过；PR自身不代表项目复跑

init_ref_tools.name: ASICFlow
init_ref_tools.description: A configurable ASIC compilation flow.  This flow targets ASIC designs, taking RTL through a complete synthesis, place-and-route, and finishing flow.  The flow is divided into the following major steps:  * **elaborate**: RTL elaboration using Slang. * **synthesis**: RTL synthesis using Yosys. * **floorplan**: Floorplanning, including macro placement, tapcell/endcap insertion, power grid generation, and pin placement. * **place**: Global and detailed placement. * **cts**: Clock tree synthesis and post-CTS timing repair. * **route**: Global routing, optional timing repair on the global routing parasitics, antenna repair, detailed routing, and antenna repair on the detailed routes. * **dfm**: Design-for-manufacturing steps, primarily metal fill. * **write**: Writing out final views of the design (GDSII, etc.).  The synthesis, floorplan, place, cts, and route steps support parallel execution to explore different strategies. This can be configured by setting the corresponding ``*_np`` argument to a value greater than 1.  Args: * name (str, optional): The name of the flow. If not provided, it defaults to 'asicflow-<language>'. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. One of 'verilog', 'systemverilog', 'systemverilog-sv2v', 'chisel', 'vhdl', or 'hls'. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects. See :mod:`~siliconcompiler.flows.sodaflow` for one. * syn_np (int): Number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): Number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): Number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): Number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): Number of parallel routing jobs to launch.

function.description: Initializes the ASICFlow with configurable parallel execution.
function.ori_input: self, name: Optional[str] = None, language: str = 'verilog', syn_np: int = 1, floorplan_np: int = 1, place_np: int = 1, cts_np: int = 1, route_np: int = 1, frontend: Optional[Flowgraph] = None
function.ori_description: Initializes the ASICFlow with configurable parallel execution.  Args: * name (str): The name of the flow. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * syn_np (int): The number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): The number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): The number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): The number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): The number of parallel routing jobs to launch. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects.

basic_info.name: MLEM首硅频率与功能实测回传流片签核假设复核

environment.description:
触发: 已流片设计的首批硅片返回，ATE/板级测试给出最高工作频率和核心、SRAM、外设功能结果；MLEM公开案例实测72 MHz @ 1.2 V
对象：冻结的同一设计流片版本与签核预期、首硅批次/芯片身份、测试程序/条件及实测数据
目标：把首硅实测反馈给设计签核与后续版本使用决策，识别一致性证据和未覆盖的角/功能，防止把计划指标当实测闭环
输入：设计/GDS与签核报告标识、工艺/封装批次谱系、ATE或板级程序版本、供电/温度/频率条件、功能测试向量和结果、签核PVT角与时序目标
步骤/决策：先以设计标识和lot/die谱系确认测试硅片来自冻结的流片工件；对齐签核预期和实测的电压、温度、频率定义及测试方法；将核心、SRAM、外设逐项关联测试覆盖；若可比角度下频率及功能满足项目签核验收则记录首硅确认和未覆盖角；若频率不符或功能失败则保留原始测试记录，分支检查测试程序/条件、封装板卡、工艺偏差及设计约束，再决定ECO、重测或扩大样本；只在真实硅片及批准测试角有证据时回闭
验收：每项实测可追溯同一设计工件和具体芯片、程序与电压/温度条件；仅在可比角下比较签核与实测；未测角或未覆盖功能不标为通过；公开MLEM文中的72 MHz不是其他项目通用阈值

init_ref_tools.name: Project
init_ref_tools.description: The Project class is the core object in SiliconCompiler, representing a complete hardware design project. It manages design parameters, libraries, flowgraphs, metrics, and provides methods for compilation, data collection, and reporting.

function.name: __init__
function.description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.

design.description: The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.ori_description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.  Args: design (Union[Design, str], optional): The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.

return.description: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.

function.ori_description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.  Returns: Project: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.  Examples: >>> project.run() # Executes the flow, and returns a project object for the completed job.

function.description: Returns a *mutable* reference to a historical job record as a Project object.

job.description: Name of the historical job to retrieve.

return.description: The `Project` object representing the specified historical job.

function.ori_description: Returns a *mutable* reference to a historical job record as a Project object.  Args: job (str): Name of the historical job to retrieve.  Returns: Project: The `Project` object representing the specified historical job.  Raises: KeyError: If the specified job does not exist in the history.

function.name: set_flow
function.description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

flow.description: The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.

function.ori_description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.  Args: flow (Union[Flowgraph, str]): The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.  Raises: TypeError: If the provided `flow` is not a string or a `Flowgraph` object. KeyError: If no loaded flowgraph matches the given name, or if a partial name matches more than one loaded flowgraph.

function.name: get_flow
function.description: Retrieves a flowgraph by name.  The name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

name.description: The full or partial (prefix) name of the flowgraph to retrieve. If None, the currently selected flowgraph (:keypath:`option,flow`) is used.

return.description: The `Flowgraph` object corresponding to the resolved name.

function.ori_description: Retrieves a flowgraph by name.  The name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.  Args: name (str, optional): The full or partial (prefix) name of the flowgraph to retrieve. If None, the currently selected flowgraph (:keypath:`option,flow`) is used.  Returns: Flowgraph: The `Flowgraph` object corresponding to the resolved name.  Raises: KeyError: If no flow is currently selected (when `name` is None), if no loaded flowgraph matches the given name, or if a partial name matches more than one loaded flowgraph.

init_ref_tools.name: ASICFlow
init_ref_tools.description: A configurable ASIC compilation flow.  This flow targets ASIC designs, taking RTL through a complete synthesis, place-and-route, and finishing flow.  The flow is divided into the following major steps:  * **elaborate**: RTL elaboration using Slang. * **synthesis**: RTL synthesis using Yosys. * **floorplan**: Floorplanning, including macro placement, tapcell/endcap insertion, power grid generation, and pin placement. * **place**: Global and detailed placement. * **cts**: Clock tree synthesis and post-CTS timing repair. * **route**: Global routing, optional timing repair on the global routing parasitics, antenna repair, detailed routing, and antenna repair on the detailed routes. * **dfm**: Design-for-manufacturing steps, primarily metal fill. * **write**: Writing out final views of the design (GDSII, etc.).  The synthesis, floorplan, place, cts, and route steps support parallel execution to explore different strategies. This can be configured by setting the corresponding ``*_np`` argument to a value greater than 1.  Args: * name (str, optional): The name of the flow. If not provided, it defaults to 'asicflow-<language>'. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. One of 'verilog', 'systemverilog', 'systemverilog-sv2v', 'chisel', 'vhdl', or 'hls'. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects. See :mod:`~siliconcompiler.flows.sodaflow` for one. * syn_np (int): Number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): Number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): Number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): Number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): Number of parallel routing jobs to launch.

function.ori_description: Initializes the ASICFlow with configurable parallel execution.  Args: * name (str): The name of the flow. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * syn_np (int): The number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): The number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): The number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): The number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): The number of parallel routing jobs to launch. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects.

场景要求：触发: 产品功耗目标促使设计团队将空闲寄存器或模块改写为显式保持/时钟门控可推断结构，准备替换原RTL
对象：基线RTL、目标工作负载的切换活动、修改后的RTL、同一综合约束及标准单元库版本可追溯
目标：只接受在目标工作负载下降低动态功耗、同时功能等价且门级时序/实现可用的RTL改写
输入：基线与候选RTL、时钟/复位和工作负载、VCD/SAIF活动、形式等价规则、综合和门级仿真/时序报告、功耗/面积报告
步骤/决策：用目标工作负载的活动证据选择门控候选并锁定基线/候选RTL、库、角和约束；先检查可综合性和时钟/复位语义，再运行项目形式等价及规定的门级含SDF仿真/时序检查；形式或门级失败即回退或改用合规ICG策略并复验，不因RTL自检通过放行；只有功能和时序均可接受时，才在相同负载、库角及功耗口径下对比动态/总功耗、面积与门控覆盖；收益不达项目目标或副作用越限则保留基线并保存失败证据。
验收：候选具备与基线相同输入/工作负载、库角、约束和活动统计口径；项目形式等价与时序满足要求，适用的门级含SDF检查实际通过，时钟保持/竞争失败有回退证据；功耗收益与面积副作用按项目限值评价；仅RTL仿真通过或论文案例10/10结果不证明本设计可发布或硅上收益。

basic_info.name: 自定义EDA步骤升级后的State契约与指标传播回归

environment.description:
触发: 自定义检查/转换Step或插件升级后，流程返回成功但下游final缺某view或metrics字段
对象：升级前后Step实现、声明的inputs/outputs/config_vars、固定输入State与期望指标
目标：确认步骤不会静默修改未声明view，也不会丢失用于后续签核的指标

init_ref_tools.name: ASICFlow
init_ref_tools.description: A configurable ASIC compilation flow.  This flow targets ASIC designs, taking RTL through a complete synthesis, place-and-route, and finishing flow.  The flow is divided into the following major steps:  * **elaborate**: RTL elaboration using Slang. * **synthesis**: RTL synthesis using Yosys. * **floorplan**: Floorplanning, including macro placement, tapcell/endcap insertion, power grid generation, and pin placement. * **place**: Global and detailed placement. * **cts**: Clock tree synthesis and post-CTS timing repair. * **route**: Global routing, optional timing repair on the global routing parasitics, antenna repair, detailed routing, and antenna repair on the detailed routes. * **dfm**: Design-for-manufacturing steps, primarily metal fill. * **write**: Writing out final views of the design (GDSII, etc.).  The synthesis, floorplan, place, cts, and route steps support parallel execution to explore different strategies. This can be configured by setting the corresponding ``*_np`` argument to a value greater than 1.  Args: * name (str, optional): The name of the flow. If not provided, it defaults to 'asicflow-<language>'. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. One of 'verilog', 'systemverilog', 'systemverilog-sv2v', 'chisel', 'vhdl', or 'hls'. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects. See :mod:`~siliconcompiler.flows.sodaflow` for one. * syn_np (int): Number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): Number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): Number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): Number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): Number of parallel routing jobs to launch.

function.name: check_manifest
function.description: Performs a comprehensive check of the project's manifest (configuration) for consistency and validity.  The checks are performed against a resolved copy of this project, so the configuration that :meth:`.Project.run()` would actually execute is what gets validated. Values that a run would infer, such as the design fileset or the ASIC main library, are therefore not reported as errors, but the inference itself is still reported as a warning. This project is left unmodified.

return.description: True if the manifest is valid and all checks pass, False otherwise.

function.name: set_flow
function.description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

flow.description: The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.

The flow is divided into the following major steps:  * **elaborate**: RTL elaboration using Slang. * **synthesis**: RTL synthesis using Yosys. * **floorplan**: Floorplanning, including macro placement, tapcell/endcap insertion, power grid generation, and pin placement. * **place**: Global and detailed placement. * **cts**: Clock tree synthesis and post-CTS timing repair. * **route**: Global routing, optional timing repair on the global routing parasitics, antenna repair, detailed routing, and antenna repair on the detailed routes. * **dfm**: Design-for-manufacturing steps, primarily metal fill. * **write**: Writing out final views of the design (GDSII, etc.).  The synthesis, floorplan, place, cts, and route steps support parallel execution to explore different strategies. This can be configured by setting the corresponding ``*_np`` argument to a value greater than 1.  Args: * name (str, optional): The name of the flow. If not provided, it defaults to 'asicflow-<language>'. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. One of 'verilog', 'systemverilog', 'systemverilog-sv2v', 'chisel', 'vhdl', or 'hls'. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects. See :mod:`~siliconcompiler.flows.sodaflow` for one. * syn_np (int): Number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): Number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): Number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): Number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): Number of parallel routing jobs to launch.

function.description: Initializes the ASICFlow with configurable parallel execution.

function.ori_description: Initializes the ASICFlow with configurable parallel execution.  Args: * name (str): The name of the flow. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * syn_np (int): The number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): The number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): The number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): The number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): The number of parallel routing jobs to launch. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects.

function.name: check_manifest
function.description: Performs a comprehensive check of the project's manifest (configuration) for consistency and validity.  The checks are performed against a resolved copy of this project, so the configuration that :meth:`.Project.run()` would actually execute is what gets validated. Values that a run would infer, such as the design fileset or the ASIC main library, are therefore not reported as errors, but the inference itself is still reported as a warning. This project is left unmodified.

return.description: True if the manifest is valid and all checks pass, False otherwise.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.

return.description: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.

function.name: get_flow
function.description: Retrieves a flowgraph by name.  The name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. init_ref_tools.name: ASICFlow
init_ref_tools.description: A configurable ASIC compilation flow.  This flow targets ASIC designs, taking RTL through a complete synthesis, place-and-route, and finishing flow.  The flow is divided into the following major steps:  * **elaborate**: RTL elaboration using Slang. * **synthesis**: RTL synthesis using Yosys. * **floorplan**: Floorplanning, including macro placement, tapcell/endcap insertion, power grid generation, and pin placement. * **place**: Global and detailed placement. * **cts**: Clock tree synthesis and post-CTS timing repair. * **route**: Global routing, optional timing repair on the global routing parasitics, antenna repair, detailed routing, and antenna repair on the detailed routes. * **dfm**: Design-for-manufacturing steps, primarily metal fill. * **write**: Writing out final views of the design (GDSII, etc.).  The synthesis, floorplan, place, cts, and route steps support parallel execution to explore different strategies. This can be configured by setting the corresponding ``*_np`` argument to a value greater than 1.  Args: * name (str, optional): The name of the flow. If not provided, it defaults to 'asicflow-<language>'. * language (str): The hardware description language of the design. One of 'verilog', 'systemverilog', 'systemverilog-sv2v', 'chisel', 'vhdl', or 'hls'. Ignored when ``frontend`` is given. * frontend (Flowgraph, optional): An elaboration flow to use instead of the one ``language`` selects. See :mod:`~siliconcompiler.flows.sodaflow` for one. * syn_np (int): Number of parallel synthesis jobs to launch. * floorplan_np (int): Number of parallel floorplan jobs to launch. * place_np (int): Number of parallel placement jobs to launch. * cts_np (int): Number of parallel clock tree synthesis jobs to launch. * route_np (int): Number of parallel routing jobs to launch.

init_ref_tools.name: Project
init_ref_tools.description: The Project class is the core object in SiliconCompiler, representing a complete hardware design project. It manages design parameters, libraries, flowgraphs, metrics, and provides methods for compilation, data collection, and reporting.

function.name: check_manifest
function.description: Performs a comprehensive check of the project's manifest (configuration) for consistency and validity.  The checks are performed against a resolved copy of this project, so the configuration that :meth:`.Project.run()` would actually execute is what gets validated. Values that a run would infer, such as the design fileset or the ASIC main library, are therefore not reported as errors, but the inference itself is still reported as a warning. This project is left unmodified.

return.description: True if the manifest is valid and all checks pass, False otherwise.

Values that a run would infer, such as the design fileset or the ASIC main library, are therefore not reported as errors, but the inference itself is still reported as a warning. This project is left unmodified.  Returns: bool: True if the manifest is valid and all checks pass, False otherwise.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.

return.description: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.

After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.  Returns: Project: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.  Examples: >>> project.run() # Executes the flow, and returns a project object for the completed job.

function.name: set_flow
function.description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

flow.description: The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.

environment.description:
触发: OPC输出后设计ECO、模型/量测配方修订或MPC/MDP重跑中断，使待写入mask数据与已签核OPC/量测证据版本可能不同
对象：目标版图与ECO版本、OPC/MPC/MDP作业输入输出、模型/配方版本、mask写入包和CD-SEM反馈元数据
目标：识别错配影响的下游光罩数据与验证证据，决定阻断写入、部分重跑或全链复核
输入：每阶段输入输出文件hash/版本、作业完成状态与依赖、ECO/模型变更清单、reticle图形/量测坐标映射、已签核验证记录
步骤/决策：从mask写入包逆向追踪目标版图、OPC模型/配方、MPC及MDP输入；核对作业完成状态和依赖边；若任一上游版本改变或输出不完整，标记其可达下游产物失效，按变更影响范围安排重跑及光刻验证；若仅元数据缺失则暂停签核并补证，不根据文件名推断版本；所有必需产物和量测坐标与同一批准版本一致后移交mask shop
验收：mask写入包可逐阶段回链批准版图/模型/配方及完整作业；受ECO影响的产物全部重跑或经批准豁免；必要签核和量测坐标对应同一版本；无实际写入后证据不宣称实体mask正确

init_ref_tools.name: Project
init_ref_tools.description: The Project class is the core object in SiliconCompiler, representing a complete hardware design project. It manages design parameters, libraries, flowgraphs, metrics, and provides methods for compilation, data collection, and reporting.

function.description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.

design.description: The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.ori_description: Initializes a new Project instance.  This sets up the fundamental schema for the project, including global options, default libraries, flowgraphs, and tool configurations. It also initializes the project-specific logger and working directory.  Args: design (Union[Design, str], optional): The top-level design for the project. Can be a `Design` object or the name of the design as a string. Defaults to None.

function.name: run
function.description: Executes the compilation flow defined in the project's flowgraph.  The run method orchestrates the entire compilation process. It starts by initializing the dashboard and then hands off execution to a `Scheduler` (or `ClientScheduler` for remote runs). The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.

return.description: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.

The scheduler manages the step-by-step execution of tasks defined in the flowgraph, respecting dependencies and handling errors.  After the scheduler completes, the dashboard is updated with the final run status, and non-global job parameters are reset. The method returns a `Project` object representing the completed job's history.  Returns: Project: A mutable reference to the completed job's record in the project history.  Examples: >>> project.run() # Executes the flow, and returns a project object for the completed job.

Returns: Project: The `Project` object representing the specified historical job.  Raises: KeyError: If the specified job does not exist in the history.

function.name: set_flow
function.description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

flow.description: The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.

function.ori_description: Sets the active flowgraph for this project.  This method allows you to specify the sequence of steps and tasks (the flow) that the project will execute. If a `Flowgraph` object is provided, it is first added as a dependency.  When given a string, the name is resolved against the flowgraphs already loaded into the project. An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.  Args: flow (Union[Flowgraph, str]): The flowgraph object, or the full or partial (prefix) name of a flowgraph already loaded into the project.  Raises: TypeError: If the provided `flow` is not a string or a `Flowgraph` object. KeyError: If no loaded flowgraph matches the given name, or if a partial name matches more than one loaded flowgraph.

function.name: get_flow

An exact match is preferred; if none exists, the name is treated as a prefix and matched against the loaded flowgraph names. This allows a short name to select a variant-suffixed flow, for example ``"synflow"`` resolves to ``"synflow-verilog"``. The match must be unique: if the prefix matches more than one loaded flowgraph, a warning listing the candidates is logged and a `KeyError` is raised.

name.description: The full or partial (prefix) name of the flowgraph to retrieve. If None, the currently selected flowgraph (:keypath:`option,flow`) is used.

return.description: The `Flowgraph` object corresponding to the resolved name.
